- (a1) Loads AGENTS.md when there is no CLAUDE.md: CONFIRMED, with conditions. It needs v2.1.277 or later. - (a4) .claude/skills in parent directories: REFUTED for this workspace. Search stops at the repository or worktree root, so .claude/skills does not load inside repos. This session's skill list confirms it.

(c) Gemini CLI, geminicli.com
- The default context file is GEMINI.md. `context.fileName` (a string or list, settable in a project .gemini/settings.json) can name AGENTS.md.
- @file imports are supported, recursive, with default maximum depth 5.

- Codex walks from the project (git) root down to the working directory and reads at most one file per directory, AGENTS.override.md before AGENTS.md. It is not on-demand. There are no @imports.

(1) Name collisions.
- Both CLI versions (1.7.1 and 1.5.12) key installs by name, and the last install wins.
- The second install overwrites, with no per-skill prompt.

Reconcile three findings that interact and conflict. READ-ONLY.

The findings:
(a) skills/ariestools-sdk/conventions.md, high: "prefer @ariestools/sdk/<module> subpaths creates duplicate class types when code also uses actor-kit or sdk-react".
(b) The same file, medium: "each subpath bundle has its own copy of shared classes, so instanceof fails across entries".
(c) skills/xy-toolchain/compilation.md, medium: "Monolith identity invariant, platform config and declaration sharing (10.0.9) missing".

Evidence so far:
- sdk-js 9.0.1 (HEAD 298fbb5bb, deployed 2026-09-24) was built with @ariestools/toolchain 10.0.7 (ariestools/sdk-js/pnpm-lock.yaml:724).
- That is before these toolchain 10.0.9 commits (dated 2026-10-01): 6e056462a "share one declaration tree across platforms", 92cf6bce9 "warn about platform shims that split module identity", and d0f17a92d (identity invariant in papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md and CHANGELOG).
- The local dist at packages/sdk/dist/neutral inlines classes in each entry: `var TimerScheduler = class` appears in 7 .mjs files, and PromiseEx in both index.mjs and promise.mjs.

Answer separately:
(1) Runtime identity: does instanceof fail between `@ariestools/sdk` and `@ariestools/sdk/<module>`, and between two different subpaths?
(2) TypeScript type identity: do classes with private or # members become incompatible across the duplicated .d.ts files?
(3) Answer (1) and (2) for published 9.0.1 (use `npm view @ariestools/sdk@9.0.1` metadata and the local dist built from the same commit; do not install). Then say which part toolchain ≥10.0.9 fixes on the next sdk-js build, and which part it does not fix.
(4) Which import style do the consumers use? grep '@ariestools/sdk' versus '@ariestools/sdk/' imports in ariestools/{actor-kit,sdk-react,browser-kit,cli-kit} sources and dist.

Output: the correct consumer guidance (root import, subpath, or one style used consistently across a dependency graph), how it interacts with the zod and OTel peer findings (the root barrel loads every peer), and corrected severities for (a), (b) and (c).
gapTasks.coverage:
Answers to the four questions:

(1) Runtime identity, 9.0.1: instanceof fails between root and any subpath, and between two subpaths that share code. Static state splits the same way (Base.defaultLogger via initDefaultLogger, MongoClientWrapper.clients in storage-adapters). This was tested in Node 26.9 against the local dist and the installed published 9.0.1 tarball (byte-identical), and against actor-kit's installed 9.0.0. Browser-condition runtime was checked by dist file inspection only; browser/index.mjs has its own class definitions.

(2) TypeScript, 9.0.1: under the house NodeNext tsconfig, classes with private/protected members (12 declaration files, no `#` members) are not assignable between root and subpath (TS2322). Subpath-to-subpath types are assignable because they share the neutral declaration tree, even though runtime differs. Bundler resolution without conditions shows no type error. Tested with tsc 6.0.3 on scratchpad files that symlink the local sdk dist.

(3) Toolchain 10.0.9 or later fixes only the type part. This was verified by running the toolchain's dedupeMonolithDeclarations source (at 812b27a91) on a scratchpad copy of the 9.0.1 dist: 482 copies were removed and the TS errors disappeared, while runtime identity stayed split. The dedupe runs for both linkages. The runtime fix requires sdk-js to opt into moduleLinkage 'external', which has been available since v8.6.7; 10.0.9 only adds checks for external linkage. Not done: building sdk-js (read-only rule) or simulating external linkage.

(4) Consumers, root/subpath imports: actor-kit 18/0, sdk-react 115/0 (src and dist), browser-kit 1/0 (spec only), cli-kit 0/0. XYO libraries are root-dominant. sdk-js's own specialist packages use subpaths only for types and stateless functions. storage-adapters consumers use /mongo exclusively (50/50).

Guidance: one import style per package across the dependency graph. For @ariestools/sdk 9.x that is the root barrel, which requires zod and @opentelemetry/api and confirms the known zod/OTel high findings. 'Subpaths keep peers optional' is true only when nothing in the graph imports the root. For storage-adapters it is the backend subpath; for sdk-react it is the umbrella or the sub-package subpaths.

Corrected severities: (a) stays high, restated as a runtime and static-state split; (b) is merged into it and raised from medium to high; (c) drops from medium to low.

Also found, and verified against registry metadata (no install): sdk-react has had no @ariestools/sdk peer since 11.1.6, and sdk-react-foundation has a latent React context split between its root barrel and /user-events.

Not checked: per-file class mixing inside XYO apps that mix styles (app-explore has 233 root and 318 subpath imports), and Vite/Rollup bundle-level dedupe behavior. Scratch files exist only under the session scratchpad; no repo was modified.

findings.title: The xy-agent link in Related skills points at a skill that consumer repos do not have installed, and nothing says how to install it
findings.current: SKILL.md:33 "**[xy-agent](../xy-agent/SKILL.md)** — *recommended, not required.* ..." (workflow.md:47 has the same relative link). There is no install hint.
findings.truth: The toolchain manages only three ariestools-skills skills: `ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain']`. `xy skills lint --fix` installs each required skill one at a time with `skills add <source> --skill <name>`, so it never installs xy-agent. A repo also cannot opt in through `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills: ['xy-agent']`, because `normalizeAdditionalSkills` throws "Unknown skills" for names outside the catalog. Two install paths do work: `xy skills defaults` (it runs `--all` against ariestools/ariestools-skills) and a package.json `xy.skills` entry that names an explicit source. As a result, `../xy-agent/SKILL.md` does not resolve in the consumer installs observed.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/defaults.ts:13-17 (ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS), :67-73 (defaults uses --all); lint.ts:91-95 (per-skill install); skillRules.ts:80-96 (unknown additionalSkills throw); packageSkills.ts:133-149 (out-of-catalog skill accepted with a declared source). Toolchain repo itself: `ls .agents/skills` → xy-development, xy-toolchain, xy-work (no xy-agent), and `diff -r` shows its xy-development matches the 0.1.5 source. Workspace survey: 30 repos under */* have xy-development v0.1.5 in .agents/skills and 0 have xy-agent (`ls -d */*/.agents/skills/xy-agent` → no matches). The toolchain work item .xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json already notes that xy-agent "also needs registering in src/actions/skills/defaults.ts (ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS) plus an optional-skills list".
findings.recommendation: At SKILL.md:33 and workflow.md:47, add an install hint: "If `../xy-agent/` is absent, install it with `npx skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --skill xy-agent`, or with `xy skills defaults` (installs the whole pack), or declare `{ "name": "xy-agent", "source": "ariestools/ariestools-skills" }` in package.json `xy.skills`." Do NOT suggest `xy skills pick --skill xy-agent`, `commands.skillsLint.skills`, or `additionalSkills`: as of 10.1.1 all three reject xy-agent. Qualify the 'recommended, not required / not defective' sentence as well, for example: "From @ariestools/toolchain 10.1.1, `xy check` runs `xy agent lint`. A missing AGENTS.md (agents.file-present) and a CLAUDE.md that copies AGENTS.md (agents.adapter-thin) are errors unless the repo lowers them in `commands.agentLint.rules`. `xy agent init` scaffolds the convention without overwriting existing files." Architecture follow-up in the toolchain: add xy-agent to ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS (defaults.ts) together with an optional or allowed list for every tier (skillRules.ts optionalSkillsForTier). That makes pick, presence and additionalSkills accept it and makes skillSourceForName resolve it to ariestools-skills, without skills.unnecessary warning in repos that install it.

SKILL.md:14 contains `xy-development v1.1.19`, and `git show 74f0248:skills/xy-development/SKILL.md` line 12 shows it was copied unchanged at the start. .release-please-manifest.json is 0.1.5. verify.skill: adjusted: The claim is real. SKILL.md:14 gives the example `xy-development v1.1.19`; the canonical version is 0.1.5 (SKILL.md:5, .release-please-manifest.json). The example was already present in the initial commit (`git show 74f0248:skills/xy-development/SKILL.md` line 12). findings.title: The git.md entry hides the "Never Rewrite History" prohibitions and the Gitflow model
findings.current: SKILL.md:21-22 "Read when creating commits, branches, or preparing changes for review. Covers conventional commits, atomic commit discipline, and branch naming patterns."
findings.truth: git.md:46-62 is a hard prohibition list: no `git commit --amend`, no rebase, no `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, no `reset --hard`, no filter-branch. git.md:64-90 defines the Gitflow branches and release and hotfix flow. These rules matter most when an agent amends, rebases, force-pushes, undoes a commit, or resolves a rejected push, and none of those triggers appear in the entry.
findings.evidence: skills/xy-development/git.md:46-62, 64-90. This repo's CLAUDE.md also states Gitflow with `develop` as the integration branch and "Never rewrite git history on shared branches". The workspace CLAUDE.md "Commit identity" section tells agents to rewrite an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email, which conflicts with git.md:51; that conflict belongs to git.md and is out of scope for this router.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the entry as: "Read when creating commits or branches, pushing, merging, undoing a change, or resolving a rejected push. Covers conventional commits, atomic commits, the never-rewrite-history rule (no amend, rebase, force-push or reset --hard), and Gitflow branching (main/develop, feature/fix/release/hotfix naming)."

verify.code: confirmed: git.md:46-62 is the Never Rewrite History list: no amend, rebase, force or force-with-lease push, reset --hard, or filter-branch. git.md:64-90 is the Gitflow model with release and hotfix flow. The router entry at SKILL.md:21-22 mentions only conventional commits, atomic commits and branch naming, so an agent about to amend, rebase or force-push gets no reason to open git.md. This repo's CLAUDE.md does state Gitflow with develop and no history rewrites on shared branches. The workspace CLAUDE.md 'Commit identity' rule ('Rewrite an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email') does conflict with git.md:51, and the finding correctly scopes that conflict out of this router.
verify.skill: confirmed: SKILL.md:21-22 says only 'creating commits, branches, or preparing changes for review' and summarizes the file as conventional commits, atomic commits and branch naming. git.md:46-62 is a hard prohibition list: no `--amend`, no rebase, no `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, no `reset --hard`, no filter-branch or `rebase --onto`. git.md:64-90 defines Gitflow, including the release and hotfix flow and the pragmatism exception. None of the high-risk triggers (amend, rebase, force-push, undo, rejected push) appear in the router, so an agent asked to 'amend that commit' or 'rebase onto develop' gets no prompt to open git.md. The router therefore leaves out the file's most consequential rule, which is a materially incomplete summary. Medium is proportionate. The recommended text accurately reflects git.md. The conflict with the workspace CLAUDE.md (rewrite an unpushed commit that has the wrong email) is correctly scoped out to git.md.

findings.title: Relative imports must use .ts/.tsx extensions, not .js
findings.current: "Use `.js` extensions in relative import paths (TypeScript resolves `.ts` → `.js`)" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:62)
findings.truth: The base tsconfig enables `allowImportingTsExtensions` with `noEmit`, and every @ariestools repo writes relative specifiers with `.ts`/`.tsx`. The lint barrel ban is spelled with `.ts` paths, so a `.js` specifier gets past it without any report.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:4 `"allowImportingTsExtensions": true`, :17 `"noEmit": true`. I counted relative `from './…'` specifiers in packages/*/src: toolchain 1809 .ts / 0 .js; sdk-react 891 .ts + 374 .tsx / 0 .js; actor-kit 268/0; cli-kit 288/0; browser-kit 130/0; sdk-js 1052 .ts / 29 .js (leftovers in packages/sdk/src/spec/typeof/*.spec.ts, packages/express/src/middleware/standardResponses/standardResponses.ts:5-6, storage-adapters). eslint-config-flat src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14 and src/rules/index.ts:8-17 list the restricted paths as './index.ts', '../index.ts', and so on. I linted a scratch file with recommendedConfig({tier:3,isTypeChecked:true}) through the ESLint API: `import { helper } from './index.ts'` gives `error no-restricted-imports`, and `import { helper } from './index.js'` gives no no-restricted-imports report. The pack disagrees with itself: skills/xy-toolchain/typescript.md:34 lists `allowImportingTsExtensions`.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 62 with: "Use explicit `.ts` / `.tsx` extensions in relative import paths (`import { x } from './x.ts'`). The base `@ariestools/tsconfig` enables `allowImportingTsExtensions` (with `noEmit`), and the toolchain compile resolves or rewrites them in emitted output. Do not use `.js` specifiers for TypeScript sources: the repos do not use them, and they bypass the lint rule that bans `./index.ts` barrel imports." Link ../xy-toolchain/typescript.md.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:4 sets allowImportingTsExtensions and :17 sets noEmit. 10.1.1 changed only package.json versions under packages/tsconfig and eslint-config-flat (git diff 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91 --stat). My own grep of relative specifiers in packages/*/src found toolchain 1853 .ts / 0 .js, sdk-js 1052 / 29, sdk-react 1265 / 0, actor-kit 268 / 0, cli-kit 288 / 0, browser-kit 130 / 0. The 29 sdk-js leftovers are in sdk/src/modules/typeof/*, sdk/src/spec/typeof/*, express standardResponses.ts and storage-adapters mongo/*. The restricted paths are spelled with .ts (eslint-config-flat src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14 and rules/index.ts:8-17). I ran a scratch lint with the built 10.1.1 dist, recommendedConfig({tier:3,isTypeChecked:true}): `import … from './index.ts'` gives `error no-restricted-imports`, while `from './index.js'` in the same file gives no no-restricted-imports report. `.js` specifiers still compile: tsc 6.0.3 with the base tsconfig accepts `./a.js` resolving to a.ts, and monolithCompileDeclarations.ts:46-72 rewrites both forms. So nothing fails outright. The severity is still justified, because following the skill silently gets past the enforced barrel ban, and the text contradicts every repo and skills/xy-toolchain/typescript.md:34. On the recommendation's "rewrites them on emit": library and bundle modes bundle with esbuild (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:220, resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts:105-117), and only monolith declarations rewrite specifiers. "Resolves them when emitting" would be more precise, but this is minor.
verify.skill: adjusted: The finding is real, but high overstates it. skills/xy-development/typescript.md:62 tells agents to use `.js` specifiers. That contradicts the pack's own skills/xy-toolchain/typescript.md:34 (`allowImportingTsExtensions`), toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:4,17, and every repo's practice. My grep count was toolchain 1853 .ts/0 .js, sdk-react 1265/0, actor-kit 268/0, cli-kit 288/0, browser-kit 130/0, sdk-js 1052/29. My scratch lint at tier 3 confirms that `./index.ts` gives a no-restricted-imports error, while `./index.js` only gets an import-x/no-duplicates warning, so it slips past the barrel ban (eslint-config-flat src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14). However, following the skill does not break anything. NodeNext resolves `.js` to `.ts`, no lint rule enforces extensions (grep finds only import-x/no-useless-path-segments), and sdk-js 9.0.1 builds and ships with 29 `.js` specifiers. So this is a convention contradiction, not a failing command: medium. Nothing changed in 10.1.1 (packages/tsconfig and eslint-config-flat only got package.json version bumps).

findings.title: The `any` escape hatch needs a rule-scoped eslint-disable, not a TODO comment
findings.current: "5. **Only then: `any`** — with a `// TODO: [reason alternatives don't work]` comment explaining the constraint." (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17)
findings.truth: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` is an error at every tier, so a TODO comment still fails lint. In the default type-checked mode, `any` that spreads also triggers the no-unsafe-* errors. The repos write `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- <reason>`. Blanket disables are banned (`unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable`), `@ts-ignore` is banned, and `@ts-expect-error` needs a description (`ban-ts-comment`).
findings.evidence: typescript-eslint 8.71.1 flat/recommended sets `no-explicit-any: 'error'`; it is spread at every tier in eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:186,196. Effective config from ESLint.calculateConfigForFile at tiers 2 and 3: no-explicit-any [2], no-unsafe-assignment [2], ban-ts-comment [2], unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable [2]. Type-checked is the default (src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:12-15). Scratch lint of `// TODO: reason alternatives don't work` followed by `const loose: any = helper` gives `10:16 error @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`. ban-ts-comment defaults are `'ts-ignore': true, 'ts-expect-error': 'allow-with-description'` (node_modules/@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin/dist/rules/ban-ts-comment.js:75-82). 29 source files in toolchain and sdk-js use `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`; the toolchain adds `-- reason` descriptions (packages/eslint-config-flat/src/index.ts:44).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite step 5 as: "Only then: `any`, scoped as narrowly as possible with `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- <why the alternatives don't work>`. `no-explicit-any` is an error at every lint tier. Never use a blanket `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore`. If you must suppress a compiler error, use `@ts-expect-error <description>`." Also note under 'contained, never contagious' that `any` flowing into other values triggers the type-checked `no-unsafe-*` errors.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. Effective config gives @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any [2] at tiers 0, 1, 2 and 3, and ban-ts-comment [2] at every tier. unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable is [2] at tiers 2 and 3 only. Type-checked is the default (recommendedConfig.ts:12-15). In a scratch tier-3 lint, a `// TODO: reason alternatives don't work` line followed by `const loose: any = helper` gives `error @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, and using `loose` triggers no-unsafe-assignment and no-unsafe-member-access errors. A `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- reason` line suppresses the error cleanly. ban-ts-comment 8.71.1 defaults are ts-ignore: true and ts-expect-error: 'allow-with-description' (dist/rules/ban-ts-comment.js:74-81). Following step 5 as written therefore fails lint, so high is correct. Some of the finding's evidence is imprecise. Across toolchain and sdk-js, 32 files disable no-explicit-any, but most use a file-scoped `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any */` (24 occurrences, nearly all in sdk-js threads). Only about 10 use next-line, and only 1 carries a `-- reason`. The cited packages/eslint-config-flat/src/index.ts:44 `-- reason` example is a no-deprecated disable, not an any disable. The recommendation's "scoped as narrowly as possible" wording still fits.
verify.skill: confirmed: skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17 says to use `any` with only a `// TODO` comment, and nothing in the pack mentions eslint-disable. Effective config (ESLint 10.12 calculateConfigForFile with recommendedConfig at tiers 2 and 3) shows `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` [2], `no-unsafe-assignment` [2], `ban-ts-comment` [2] and `unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable` [2]. My scratch lint of `// TODO: …` followed by `export const loose: any = helper` gave `error @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`. The same declaration preceded by `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- reason` gave no error. So following step 5 literally makes `xy lint` fail, and high is justified. One evidence detail is off: I found 7 files, not 29, using that disable comment in toolchain and sdk-js packages. In toolchain src, 24 of 27 eslint-disable comments carry a `-- reason` (e.g. eslint-config-flat src/index.ts:44). This does not change the conclusion. Not affected by 10.1.1.

findings.title: Return-type guidance contradicts the workspace rule 'explicit return types on exported functions'
findings.current: "## Return Types: Prefer Inference … **Do not annotate return types** unless one of these applies: public API boundary / unexpectedly wide / type guard / recursive" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:23-31)
findings.truth: The workspace style rules and the SDK repo rules require explicit return types on exported functions, and require async functions to declare `Promise<T>` (never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`). Lint does not enforce this (`explicit-module-boundary-types` is off), so the skill is the only place an agent outside this workspace would learn it, and right now it teaches the opposite default. In practice almost all exported functions are annotated.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:43 "Explicit return types on exported functions", :46 "When a function uses `await`, declare the return as `Promise<T>` — never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`"; AGENTS.md:251,254; sdk-js/AGENTS.md:58 "Explicit return types on exported functions". Lint: eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:101 and src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:54 set `explicit-module-boundary-types` to off; explicit-function-return-type is not configured. A regex scan of `export function` declarations found return types on 712 of 742 in toolchain packages and 102 of 124 in sdk-js packages. `Promisable` is defined at sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/promise/types.ts:6.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the section: "Annotate return types on exported functions and methods (the module contract). Let inference handle local helpers, callbacks and inline arrow functions. When a function uses `await`, declare `Promise<T>`, never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`. Always annotate type guards (`x is T`) and recursive functions." Keep the covariance and inference rationale only for non-exported code. Note that this is a convention: lint does not enforce it (`explicit-module-boundary-types` is off).

verify.code: adjusted: Facts verified. CLAUDE.md:43 says "Explicit return types on exported functions" and :46 gives the Promise<T>, never Promise<Promisable<T>> rule. AGENTS.md:251,254 says the same, and sdk-js/AGENTS.md:57 says "Explicit return types on exported functions". Effective lint config has explicit-module-boundary-types [0] (typescript/index.ts:101, managed-rules.ts:54), and explicit-function-return-type is undefined. isolatedDeclarations is not used anywhere in the toolchain. My TS-AST count of annotated exported function declarations is 735 of 765 in toolchain and 101 of 124 in sdk-js. Promisable is at sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/promise/types.ts:6. Severity is the problem. Neither lint nor the compiler enforces the rule, so following the skill makes no command fail and breaks no enforced check. The skill also already lists "public API boundary" as an exception. That makes this a material contradiction of documented convention, which is medium on the rubric, not high.
verify.skill: adjusted: The conflict is real. skills/xy-development/typescript.md:23-31 defaults to 'Do not annotate return types', while CLAUDE.md:43,46, AGENTS.md:251,254 and sdk-js/AGENTS.md:58 require explicit return types on exported functions and `Promise<T>` for async functions. Most exported functions are annotated: a single-line regex alone matched 484 of 768 in toolchain and 173 of 219 in sdk-js, which undercounts multi-line signatures. However, lint does not enforce this. Effective `explicit-module-boundary-types` is [0], `explicit-function-return-type` is undefined, and tsconfig has no isolatedDeclarations. Following the skill therefore produces code that passes lint, compile and tests. The skill's own 'public API boundary' exception also partly covers exported package API. That makes this a convention contradiction, not a breakage: medium. The recommendation itself is sound.

(skills/xy-development/typescript.md:64-78)

The Layer 3 ariestools-sdk skill tells agents to prefer subpaths, so Layer 1 contradicts Layer 3. (2) The 'Avoid' packages are now deprecated compatibility shims. findings.title: Enums, parameter properties and runtime namespaces are compile errors (erasableSyntaxOnly), not just 'prefer unions'
findings.current: "**Prefer union types** over enums: `type Status = 'active' | 'inactive'` rather than `enum Status { Active, Inactive }`" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:85). The Readonly section suggests "Class properties set in the constructor that shouldn't change" (:51) but says nothing about parameter properties.
findings.truth: The base `@ariestools/tsconfig` sets `erasableSyntaxOnly: true` and `noImplicitOverride: true`. As a result `enum`, constructor parameter properties (`constructor(private readonly x: T)`) and namespaces with runtime code fail to compile, and overriding members need the `override` keyword. Lint also flags enums and suggests string-literal unions or a `const` object. The SDK ships an `Enum()` helper for the const-object pattern.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8 `"erasableSyntaxOnly": true`, :19 `"noImplicitOverride": true`. I ran tsc 6.0.3 with that tsconfig on a scratch file: `export enum Status {…}`, `constructor(private readonly x: number) {}` and `export namespace NS { export const y = 1 }` each fail with `error TS1294: This syntax is not allowed when 'erasableSyntaxOnly' is enabled.` eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:161-167 configures no-restricted-syntax on TSEnumDeclaration with the message "Enums are disallowed. Consider using a union of string literals or a `const` object instead." `@typescript-eslint/no-namespace` is effective [2]. sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/enum/{Enum.ts,model.ts} exports `Enum`, `EnumKey`, `EnumValue` via `@ariestools/sdk/enum`.
findings.recommendation: Change the bullet to: "No `enum`. It is a compile error under the base tsconfig (`erasableSyntaxOnly`). Use a string-literal union, or an `as const` object (optionally `Enum({...} as const)` from `@ariestools/sdk/enum`) when you need runtime values." In the Readonly section add: "Declare `readonly` fields explicitly. Constructor parameter properties are not allowed (`erasableSyntaxOnly`). Mark overriding members with `override` (`noImplicitOverride`)."

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. tsconfig.json:8 sets erasableSyntaxOnly and :19 sets noImplicitOverride. I ran tsc 6.0.3 (the repos pin ~6.0.3) with the base tsconfig on a scratch file. `export enum`, `constructor(private readonly x: number)` and `export namespace NS { export const y = 1 }` each give TS1294, and an override without the keyword gives TS4114. Lint also flags enums: no-restricted-syntax on TSEnumDeclaration is effective [1] (warn) at tier 3. @typescript-eslint/no-namespace is [2]. sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/enum/Enum.ts exists and is exported as `./enum` in package.json. The skill's "prefer" wording leaves room for enums, which would fail tsc. Medium is reasonable because the skill already steers away from enums.
verify.skill: confirmed: typescript.md:85 only says 'Prefer union types over enums', and the Readonly section (:51) is silent on parameter properties. packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8 sets `erasableSyntaxOnly: true` and :19 sets `noImplicitOverride: true`. tsc 6.0.3 on a scratch file with that tsconfig gave TS1294 for `enum`, `const enum`, the `constructor(private readonly x: number)` parameter property and `namespace NS { export const y = 1 }`. An unmarked override gave TS4114. Lint `no-restricted-syntax` on TSEnumDeclaration is effective [1] (warn) with the union/const-object message. sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/enum/Enum.ts:48 exports `Enum` through the `./enum` subpath. One nit: Enum takes a `const T` generic and its JSDoc example calls `Enum({...})` without `as const`, so the `as const` in the recommendation is redundant but harmless. The only other pack mention, ariestools-sdk/modules.md:33, is consistent. Medium is right because 'prefer' implies enums are sometimes acceptable, when in fact they fail to compile.

findings.title: 'Strictness Posture' says these conventions are what linters can't catch, but most of them are lint- or compiler-enforced
findings.current: "Most opinions are enforced via ESLint. The conventions below cover what linters can't catch — judgment calls that require understanding intent." (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:5)
findings.truth: Several conventions in this file are hard rules at the default tier 3 with type checking. Enforced by lint: interface over type (`consistent-type-definitions` error), optional chaining and nullish coalescing (`prefer-optional-chain` / `prefer-nullish-coalescing` error), no `any` (`no-explicit-any` error), no `require()` (`no-require-imports` error), no enums (`no-restricted-syntax`), import order (`simple-import-sort`). Enforced by the compiler: `strict`, `noImplicitAny`, `noImplicitOverride`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`. The file never mentions the tsconfig side.
findings.evidence: Effective rules from ESLint.calculateConfigForFile with recommendedConfig({tier:3,isTypeChecked:true}): consistent-type-definitions [2], prefer-optional-chain [2], prefer-nullish-coalescing [2], no-explicit-any [2], no-require-imports [2], no-restricted-syntax [1,{TSEnumDeclaration}], simple-import-sort/imports [1]. The defaults are tier 3 and type-checked (src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:12-15), and `xy lint init` generates `recommendedConfig({ tier: 3, isTypeChecked: true })` (packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts, generateEslintConfig). tsconfig: packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8,18,19,25.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the posture paragraph: "We are strict. The compiler (`@ariestools/tsconfig`: strict, noImplicitAny, noImplicitOverride, erasableSyntaxOnly) and ESLint (`@ariestools/eslint-config-flat`, tier 3 type-checked by default) enforce much of what follows; items marked *(enforced)* fail `xy lint` or `tsc`, and `pnpm xy fix` autofixes formatting, import order and type-import style. The rest are judgment calls." Tag the enforced bullets and link ../xy-toolchain/eslint.md and ../xy-toolchain/typescript.md for details.

verify.code: adjusted: Core issue verified. typescript.md:5 says the conventions cover "what linters can't catch". Effective tier-3 type-checked config shows consistent-type-definitions, prefer-optional-chain, prefer-nullish-coalescing, no-explicit-any and no-require-imports all [2]. simple-import-sort/imports, consistent-type-imports and the enum no-restricted-syntax rule are [1] (warn). The tsconfig enforces strict, noImplicitAny, noImplicitOverride and erasableSyntaxOnly. `xy lint init` generates `recommendedConfig({ tier: 3, isTypeChecked: true })` (lint-init.ts generateEslintConfig). One flaw in the recommendation: "items marked *(enforced)* fail `xy lint`/`tsc`" is wrong for warn-level rules. actions/lint.ts:232 adds `--max-warnings 0` only in --strict mode, so import order, type-import style and the enum lint warning do not fail a default `xy lint`. Enums still fail tsc.
verify.skill: adjusted: The claim is accurate. typescript.md:5 says the conventions cover 'what linters can't catch'. Yet several bullets in the file are hard rules at the default tier 3 (lint-init.ts:102 generates `recommendedConfig({ tier: 3, isTypeChecked: true })`): consistent-type-definitions [2], prefer-optional-chain [2], prefer-nullish-coalescing [2], no-explicit-any [2], no-require-imports [2], no-restricted-syntax enums [1], simple-import-sort [1]. The tsconfig settings strict, noImplicitAny, noImplicitOverride and erasableSyntaxOnly are never mentioned in this file. However, the defect is one framing sentence. findings.title: Null handling must cover strict-boolean-expressions (no implicit truthiness on nullable strings/numbers)
findings.current: "**Null handling**: prefer optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`) over manual null checks" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:87). Nothing about truthiness checks.
findings.truth: At the default tier 3 with type checking, `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions` is an error. With the default options, `if (name)` on `string | undefined` or `if (count)` on `number | undefined` is rejected, so agents must write explicit checks (`name !== undefined`, `name.length > 0`, `count !== undefined && count > 0`). `unicorn/no-typeof-undefined` is also an error, so compare with `=== undefined` directly. `null` itself is allowed (`unicorn/no-null` is off).
findings.evidence: eslint-config-flat src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:57 sets `strict-boolean-expressions` to {0:'off', 3:'error'} and requires type checking; it is effective [2] at tier 3 and [0] at tier 2. Scratch lint at tier 3: `if (name)` with `name: string | undefined` gives `error @typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions - Unexpected nullable string value in conditional`; `if (count)` with `count?: number` gives "Unexpected nullable number value in conditional"; `typeof loose === 'undefined'` gives `error unicorn/no-typeof-undefined`. managed-rules.ts:154 has `unicorn/no-null` off.
findings.recommendation: Expand the null-handling bullet into a short subsection: use `?.`/`??` *(enforced)*; write explicit comparisons in conditions for nullable strings, numbers and booleans (strict-boolean-expressions); compare with `=== undefined`/`=== null` rather than `typeof x === 'undefined'`; prefer `undefined` for absent values in new code, but `null` is not banned.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. strict-boolean-expressions is [0] at tier 2 and [2] at tier 3 with default options (managed-rules.ts:57, type-checking required). In a scratch tier-3 lint, `if (name)` with `string | undefined` gives "Unexpected nullable string value in conditional", `if (count)` with `count?: number` gives "Unexpected nullable number value in conditional", and `typeof loose === 'undefined'` gives `error unicorn/no-typeof-undefined`, which is [2] at tiers 2 and 3. unicorn/no-null is [0] (managed-rules.ts:154). The current skill bullet at :87 does not mention truthiness, so this is a real gap and medium fits.
verify.skill: confirmed: typescript.md:87 covers only `?.` and `??`, and a grep finds no strict-boolean, truthy or typeof-undefined guidance anywhere in the pack. managed-rules.ts sets `strict-boolean-expressions` to {0:'off', 3:'error'} with type checking required. It is effective [0] at tier 2 and [2] at tier 3. My scratch lint at tier 3: `if (name)` on `string | undefined` gave 'Unexpected nullable string value in conditional' (error); `if (count)` on `count?: number` gave 'Unexpected nullable number value' (error); `typeof loose === 'undefined'` gave `unicorn/no-typeof-undefined` (error). `unicorn/no-null` is effective [0]. `if (x)` on nullable values is an extremely common agent pattern, so this is a real lint failure at the default tier. Medium is proportionate. Unchanged in 10.1.1.

findings.title: Add the enforced import-style rules: node: protocol, default imports for node:path, separate `import type`, no namespace imports

Lint therefore requires type-only imports to be marked as types, and separate statements are just what the fixer emits.
verify.skill: confirmed: The pack never states the `node:` prefix rule, the default-import rule for node:path, separate `import type` statements, or the ban on `import * as X`. They only appear implicitly in code examples such as eslint.md:32,45. Effective tier 2 and 3 config: `unicorn/prefer-node-protocol` [2], `unicorn/import-style` [2,{}], `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` [1, separate-type-imports] (eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:129), `import-x/no-namespace` undefined. findings.title: Add the remaining house conventions from CLAUDE.md (named exports, top-level function declarations, boolean prefixes, file naming, `_` unused)
findings.current: "**Naming**: PascalCase for types and interfaces, camelCase for variables and functions" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:86) is the only naming or structure guidance.
findings.truth: Several workspace rules are missing from the skill. Some are convention-only, so the skill is the only carrier outside this workspace: named exports over default exports; `function` declarations at top level with arrows only for callbacks; booleans prefixed `is`/`has`/`should`/`can` (`unicorn/consistent-boolean-name` is deliberately disabled). The toolchain follows the boolean rule itself (`typeChecked` was renamed to `isTypeChecked`). One is lint-enforced: file names in camelCase for modules and PascalCase for components/classes (`unicorn/filename-case` error at tier 3, which also accepts kebab-case). Unused variables and parameters take a `_` prefix (the no-unused-vars ignore pattern).
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:42-47; sdk-js/AGENTS.md:51-57. eslint-config-flat src/unicorn/index.ts:96-103 and :365 disable consistent-boolean-name globally. src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:7-9 defines `isTypeChecked`, and :65-70 still parses the legacy `typeChecked`; src/tiers/rule-catalog/types.ts:17 has `isTypeCheckingRequired`. src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:149 and src/tiers/opinionated.ts:20-30 set filename-case to error at tier 3 with cases camelCase/kebabCase/pascalCase. src/typescript/index.ts:94-99 sets no-unused-vars with `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'`, `varsIgnorePattern: '^_'`. Effective import-x/no-default-export and func-style are undefined (not enforced).
findings.recommendation: Extend 'Other Conventions' with: named exports only (no default exports); top-level `function` declarations, arrows only for callbacks; booleans and boolean-returning predicates named `is…`/`has…`/`should…`/`can…`; files camelCase for modules and PascalCase for classes/components; prefix intentionally unused bindings with `_`. Mark which ones are lint-enforced.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. CLAUDE.md:42-47 and sdk-js/AGENTS.md:51-58 list named exports, top-level function declarations, boolean prefixes, file casing and `_` for unused bindings. unicorn/consistent-boolean-name is disabled globally (unicorn/index.ts:97, :365), and effective config is [0]. unicorn/filename-case is [0] at tier 2 and [2] at tier 3 with camelCase, kebabCase and pascalCase (managed-rules.ts:149, opinionated.ts:20-30,49). @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars is [1] with argsIgnorePattern and varsIgnorePattern '^_'. import-x/no-default-export and func-style are undefined, and scratch `export default function main(...)` gives no report. recommendedConfig.ts:7-9 uses isTypeChecked, and :65-70 still parses legacy typeChecked. The skill's only naming guidance is :86.
verify.skill: confirmed: typescript.md:86 is the only naming guidance, and SKILL.md:19 advertises that the file covers 'naming conventions'. The workspace rules in CLAUDE.md:42-47, AGENTS.md:250-255 and sdk-js/AGENTS.md:53-58 are absent from the pack: named exports over default, top-level `function` declarations, is/has/should/can boolean prefixes, file casing. ariestools-sdk/conventions.md:5 is about importing, not exporting. Verified enforcement: `unicorn/filename-case` is [0] at tier 2 and [2,{camelCase,kebabCase,pascalCase}] at tier 3. `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` is [1] with `^_` ignore patterns. `import-x/no-default-export` and `func-style` are undefined. `unicorn/consistent-boolean-name` is disabled globally (unicorn/index.ts:96-97,364-365, commented 'too disruptive for org-wide enforcement'). Convention-only rules therefore reach agents only through this skill. Not breaking, but materially incomplete: medium is fine. The recommendation correctly asks to mark which rules are lint-enforced.

findings.title: Import-ordering bullet should defer to simple-import-sort groups and its autofix
findings.current: "**Import ordering:** External packages first, then internal modules, separated by a blank line" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:80-81)
findings.truth: `simple-import-sort` v14 sets the order (warn at tiers 2 and 3, autofixable). Its default groups are side-effect imports, then `node:` built-ins, then packages, then absolute imports, then relative imports, each separated by a blank line. Agents should run the fixer instead of ordering by hand.
findings.evidence: eslint-config-flat src/import/index.ts:26-28 and src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:131 configure `simple-import-sort/imports`; it is effective [1] at tier 3. node_modules/eslint-plugin-simple-import-sort/imports.js:5-13 defines defaultGroups (`^\u0000`, `^node:`, `^@?\w`, absolute, relative); the installed version is 14.0.0. Scratch lint reported `warn simple-import-sort/imports - Run autofix to sort these imports!`.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: "Import order is enforced and autofixed by simple-import-sort: side-effect imports, then `node:` built-ins, then packages, then relative imports, with a blank line between groups. Run `pnpm xy fix` (or `pnpm xy lint --fix`) rather than ordering by hand."

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. simple-import-sort/imports is ['warn'] (import/index.ts:27; managed-rules.ts:131) and effective [1] at tier 3. The installed version is 14.0.0, and imports.js:5-17 defaultGroups are side-effect, ^node:, packages, absolute, then relative, each separated by a blank line. Scratch lint gives "Run autofix to sort these imports!". `xy lint` has -f/--fix and `xy fix` exists (both --help checked). The current text is incomplete (no node: group, no autofix) rather than wrong, so low fits.
verify.skill: confirmed: typescript.md:80-81 gives a two-group order. eslint-config-flat src/import/index.ts:26-27 sets `simple-import-sort/imports` to ['warn'] (effective [1] at tier 3). The managed catalog lists {3:'error'}, but the effective config is warn. The installed eslint-plugin-simple-import-sort 14.0.0 imports.js defines defaultGroups as side-effect, `^node:`, packages, absolute, relative. Hand-ordering by the skill misses the separate `node:` group, and my scratch lint reported 'Run autofix to sort these imports!'. `pnpm xy fix` exists in the 10.1.1 CLI (`xy.mjs fix --help`). The skill is a simplification rather than wrong and the rule only warns and autofixes, so low is correct.

findings.title: Mention the code-shape limits that are lint errors (complexity, statements, lines, depth) and member conventions
findings.current: absent
findings.truth: From tier 1 these are errors: `complexity` 18, `max-statements` 32 per function, `max-lines` 512 per file (blank lines and comments skipped), `max-depth` 6, `max-nested-callbacks` 6. Class members: no `public` keyword (`explicit-member-accessibility: no-public`), and `member-ordering` enforces group order and then alphabetical order (error at tier 3). These limits shape how agents should split functions and files.
findings.evidence: eslint-config-flat src/rules/consistency.ts:8-21; src/typescript/index.ts:14-87 (member-ordering, `order: 'alphabetically'`) and :126 (explicit-member-accessibility). Effective tier-3 values: complexity [2,18], max-statements [2,32], max-lines [2,{max:512,…}], @typescript-eslint/member-ordering [2,…], explicit-member-accessibility [1,{accessibility:'no-public'}].
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence under Strictness Posture, for example: "Keep functions small (lint errors above complexity 18 / 32 statements / depth 6) and files under 512 code lines; omit `public`; class members are ordered by kind and then alphabetically." Put the full numbers in ../xy-toolchain/eslint.md (Layer 2) and link to it from here.

These are all undefined at tier 0 and [2] from tier 1 (verified effective). @typescript-eslint/member-ordering is [1] at tiers 1-2 and [2] at tier 3, with order 'alphabetically' (typescript/index.ts:14-87); scratch lint gives "Member alpha should be declared before member zed". explicit-member-accessibility is [1] with no-public (typescript/index.ts:126). findings.title: Gitflow is presented as the default branching model, but almost every repo, including all @ariestools code repos and anything `xy repo init` creates, works off main only
findings.current: git.md:66 "We follow [Gitflow](...) where possible."; git.md:83 "New work starts as a `feature/` branch off `develop`"; git.md:89-90 treats main-only as a "Pragmatism" exception for "smaller projects or early-stage work".
findings.truth: Only 9 of the 80 local clones under ariestools/, xylabs/ and XYOracleNetwork/ have an origin/develop branch. None of the @ariestools library repos have one (toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit). `xy repo init` runs `git init -b main` and scaffolds a build workflow that triggers on pushes to main. Gitflow is used in the skill-pack repos (ariestools-skills, xyo-skills, xyo-skills-internal) and a few legacy app repos. Branch prefixes in practice also differ: the toolchain has `feat/typescript-native-compiler`, `fix/lint-worker-memory-budget` and `claude/*` worktree branches that are merged straight into main.
findings.evidence: Shell loop over ariestools/* xylabs/* XYOracleNetwork/* checking `git branch -a | grep remotes/origin/develop$` printed "9 of 80". Per-repo output shows develop=0 for ariestools/{toolchain,sdk-js,sdk-react,actor-kit,browser-kit,cli-kit}. toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/repo-init/scaffold.ts:100-103 (`spawnSync('git', ['init', '-b', 'main'])`). toolchain packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/github/workflows/build-pnpm.yml.tmpl:3-7 (push branches: main). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:40 and xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 are the repos that declare Gitflow. `git -C toolchain branch -a` lists feat/..., fix/..., claude/... and no develop. Toolchain log: 5acf512db "Merge branch 'claude/eloquent-wright-73114e'" into main.
findings.recommendation: Make detecting the repo's model the first rule. Read the repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/DEVELOPMENT.md and check `git ls-remote --heads origin develop`. If `develop` exists, use Gitflow (`feature/*` off develop). If it does not (the default for `xy repo init` and all @ariestools library repos), use short-lived branches off `main` merged back into `main`. Match the branch prefixes the repo already uses (`feature/` vs `feat/`). Drop "where possible" and fold the Pragmatism paragraph into this rule.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. Of the 80 local clones, 9 have origin/develop (ariestools-skills, web-coin-react, web-coinapp.co-react, api-xyo-nodejs, app-portal, infrastructure, sdk-xyo-typechain, xyo-skills, xyo-skills-internal). `git ls-remote --heads origin` on ariestools/{toolchain,sdk-js,sdk-react,actor-kit,browser-kit,cli-kit} shows no develop head. The toolchain remote has feat/typescript-native-compiler next to feature/eslint-flat and feature/esm-run-mode. Its main merges fix/lint-worker-memory-budget (b6e839f2b) and claude/* branches (5acf512db, 48d96e78b). sdk-js main merges claude/, codex/ and feat/ branches. In toolchain 10.1.1 (812b27a91), scaffold.ts initGitRepo runs `spawnSync('git', ['init', '-b', 'main'])` (lines ~99-103), and templates/repo/cli/root/github/workflows/build-pnpm.yml.tmpl:3-7 triggers on push to main only. Gitflow is declared in ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:40 and xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63. git.md:66, :83 and :89-90 read as cited. No downstream xyo-skills file links into git.md anchors, so restructuring is safe.
verify.skill: confirmed: The skill text matches the claim. git.md:66 says "We follow Gitflow where possible", git.md:83 starts new work off `develop`, and git.md:89-90 limits main-only to "smaller projects or early-stage work" while asking for full Gitflow "when the project has releases". Checked: a loop over ariestools/*, xylabs/* and XYOracleNetwork/* found origin/develop in 9 of 80 clones. Those are ariestools-skills, web-coin-react, web-coinapp.co-react, api-xyo-nodejs, app-portal, infrastructure, sdk-xyo-typechain, xyo-skills and xyo-skills-internal. None of the @ariestools library repos is in that list. `xy repo init` runs `git init -b main` (toolchain scaffold.ts:100), and the build template triggers on main. The library repos' AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md say nothing about branching, so this skill is an agent's only guidance there, and it points at a `develop` branch that does not exist. Prefixes are mixed in practice: the toolchain has local feat/ and fix/ branches and remote feature/eslint-flat and feature/esm-run-mode. In these repos most work lands directly on main (toolchain: 254 first-parent commits since 2026-07, 15 merges). Medium is right: the guidance is wrong by default but not destructive. The detection-first recommendation is correct and in the right layer.

findings.title: The release flow (`release/<version>` branches, manual tagging, "every commit on main is a release") matches no repo
findings.current: git.md:69 "`main` — production-ready code. Every commit on main is a release."; git.md:75 "`release/<version>` — release prep (version bumps, final fixes), branched from `develop`, merged to both `main` and `develop`"; git.md:85-86 "create a `release/` branch ... Merge the release branch into `main` (tag it) and back into `develop`"; git.md:76/87 hotfix branches.
findings.truth: No Gitflow repo has release/* or hotfix/* branches. Gitflow repos release through release-please: a `develop` → `main` PR with a `feat:`/`fix:` title merged as a merge commit, then release-please opens a release PR that bumps versions and tags, then an automated `main` → `develop` sync. Versions are never bumped by hand. The main-only @ariestools repos release with `pnpm xy deploy patch|minor|major`, then `pnpm xy publish`, then an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag. Their main branch carries many commits that are not releases ("workitem", "updo", "lint" between "Deploy" commits), so "every commit on main is a release" is false in both models. The xy-toolchain skill currently documents neither `xy deploy` nor `xy publish`.
findings.evidence: `git branch -r | grep -E 'release/|hotfix/|release-please'` across ariestools-skills, xyo-skills, xyo-skills-internal, infrastructure, web-coin-react and app-portal found only `origin/release-please--branches--main--components--ariestools-skills`. ariestools-skills DEVELOPMENT.md:70-78 and release-please-config.json (`versioning: always-bump-patch`). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md "Do not bump versions by hand". xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:76-83. toolchain CONTRIBUTING.md:36-47 (release checklist: xy deploy, then xy publish, then annotated tag). `git -C toolchain log`: 7eb43c3c2 "workitem", 3320116a4 "Deploy", 00e1d4d82 "updo", 6cdd67c35 "Deploy". `grep -rn -i 'xy deploy\|xy publish' skills/xy-toolchain` returned nothing.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `release/<version>` branch type and workflow steps 3-4; no repo has ever used it. Reword git.md:69: `main` holds released or releasable code, and releases are tagged. Replace the release steps with: "Releases follow the repo's documented process (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, DEVELOPMENT.md or CONTRIBUTING.md); never hand-edit version fields." Then name the observed patterns. (a) Gitflow repos with release-please (the skill packs): open a develop → main PR with a feat:/fix: title, merge it as a merge commit, merge the release-please PR, and let the automated main → develop sync run. (b) Gitflow repos without release-please: merge develop into main as the repo instructs (some, such as infrastructure, reserve merging for curators). (c) Main-only @ariestools toolchain repos: `pnpm xy deploy <level>`, commit any bumps, create the annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag, `pnpm xy publish` (or `--tag next`), then push commits and tags. Link (c) to an xy-toolchain deploy/publish section, which needs to be added. Keep `hotfix/*` because it is used: branch from main, merge into main, then bring main back into develop, through the automated sync where it exists or a back-merge PR otherwise.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue is real. Since 2025 no repo among the 80 has merged a release/* branch. The main-only toolchain releases per CONTRIBUTING.md:36-47. Main carries non-release commits: the 10.1.1 main log has e8bd980d1, 4d19a803f, 8688075c9, 8f2768dfd, b75077b16, b8653a52d and 9a9f3a413 'updo' between 3320116a4 Deploy and 812b27a91 Deploy. `xy deploy --help` and `xy publish --help` both exist in 10.1.1, and grep finds neither documented in skills/xy-toolchain. Two parts of the truth claim are wrong, though. (1) 'No Gitflow repo has ... hotfix/* branches' is false. XYOracleNetwork/infrastructure, which has a develop branch, merged hotfix/increase-producer-ram (#149, 2025-12-23) and hotfix/max-bridge-amount (#158/#159, 2026-03-12), then back-merged by hand via feature/backmerge-hotfix (#150). xyo-chain (#457) and app-node.xyo.network-react also used hotfix/*. (2) 'Gitflow repos release through release-please' overgeneralizes. Only the three skill-pack repos have release-please-config.json and release-please.yml. infrastructure has no workflows. web-coin-react deploys beta on push to develop (.github/workflows/develop.yml). Also, CONTRIBUTING orders the steps as deploy, then commit bumps and create the annotated tag, then publish, then push, not deploy, publish, tag. Separately, 10.1.1 commit b75077b16 makes deploy and publish always run the toolchain preflight unless --defer is passed, which the planned xy-toolchain deploy/publish section should note.
verify.skill: adjusted: The core problem is real. git.md:75 and git.md:85-86 prescribe release/<version> branches, and a search of the full history of all 80 clones found no release/ branch merge anywhere. git.md:69 "Every commit on main is a release" is false for the main-only repos, where main carries "workitem", "updo" and other non-Deploy commits. xy-toolchain does not document `xy deploy` or `xy publish` (grep found only publish-check mentions), and both still exist in 10.1.1 per `xy.mjs --help`. Three parts of the finding are wrong, though. (1) "No Gitflow repo has ... hotfix/* branches" is false. XYOracleNetwork/infrastructure is a Gitflow repo (its CLAUDE.md:32) and merged hotfix/increase-producer-ram (3738410, 2025-12) and hotfix/max-bridge-amount (2a7b9d2 and 9ac29ed, 2026-03) into main, then back-merged by hand through feature/backmerge-hotfix (d1e9775). (2) "Gitflow repos release through release-please" holds only for the 3 skill-pack repos. infrastructure, app-portal, sdk-xyo-typechain, web-coin-react, web-coinapp.co-react and api-xyo-nodejs have no release-please-config.json and no sync-main-to-develop workflow, so "let the sync carry it to develop" does not apply to them. (3) The recommended toolchain order is wrong. CONTRIBUTING.md:41-44 runs `xy deploy`, then commits and creates the annotated vX.Y.Z tag (step 5), then `xy publish` (step 6), then pushes commits and tags. It is not deploy, then publish, then tag.

findings.title: Merge-method rules are missing (squash throwaway branches; use merge commits between long-lived branches)
findings.current: absent. git.md never mentions how PRs are merged. git.md:52 says "`git rebase` ... — merge instead", with no guidance on squash merges.
findings.truth: Gitflow repos set the merge method by PR type: `feature/*` → develop is squashed, `develop` → main is a merge commit, release-please → main is squashed, and `main` → develop is a merge commit (automated). Branches between long-lived branches must never be squashed, because that leaves phantom commits in `git log main..develop`. Squash-merging a feature PR is the sanctioned way to collapse branch commits, so with squash the PR, not each commit on the branch, is the unit that lands on develop.
findings.evidence: ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:47-50 (merge-method table). ariestools-skills DEVELOPMENT.md:89-96. xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:65-74 ("squash is fine when the source branch is throwaway ... Squash is harmful when both source and target are long-lived branches"), :80 ("Do not squash this PR if you ever merge it manually").
findings.recommendation: Add a short "Merging pull requests" note under the branching section. (1) Use the merge method the repo documents, and do not merge at all where the repo reserves merging for maintainers. (2) Invariant: never squash between long-lived branches (develop ↔ main); always use a merge commit, or `git log main..develop` fills with phantom commits. (3) Squashing a throwaway branch (a feature/fix PR or a release-please PR) is acceptable where the repo uses it. It is a merge-time choice and does not conflict with the history-rewrite rule. (4) In squash-merge repos the PR, not each branch commit, is the unit that lands, so its title must be a valid conventional-commit subject. Combine this with the PR-title note from finding 4.

verify.code: adjusted: Confirmed that git.md has no merge-method guidance; git.md:52 only says 'merge instead' of rebase. The per-PR-type table exists in ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:43-50 and DEVELOPMENT.md:89-96, and in xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:65-74 with the phantom-commit rationale and :80. However, 'Gitflow repos set the merge method by PR type: feature/* → develop is squashed' overgeneralizes. Only the three release-please skill-pack repos document it. XYOracleNetwork/infrastructure, also Gitflow, merges feature PRs into develop with merge commits (#294, #296, #287). xyo-skills itself has merge-commit feature PRs on develop (#94, #88). The main-only @ariestools repos merge local branches into main with merge commits (toolchain 5acf512db and b6e839f2b; sdk-js 69534d452 and dd29a9700). The universal rule is the long-lived-branch one; squashing feature PRs is a per-repo convention.
verify.skill: adjusted: Merge guidance is genuinely missing: no skill file mentions squash or merge methods (grep across skills/). But the finding generalizes from the 3 release-please skill-pack repos. Their merge tables are in ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:43-50 and DEVELOPMENT.md:89-96, xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:65-74, and xyo-skills-internal AGENTS.md:28-31. Each repo documents its table authoritatively, so an agent there already gets it. The other Gitflow repos do not squash features: infrastructure's develop has 34 "Merge branch 'feature/...' into develop" merge commits since 2026-06, and its CLAUDE.md says "Never merge PRs — repository curators handle merging". So "squash throwaway branches" is not a universal Layer 1 rule. The only universal invariant is never squashing between long-lived branches. The skill is silent rather than wrong, so following it breaks nothing, and the severity should be low.

findings.title: The commit-type list is missing perf/style/revert and has no breaking-change (`!` / BREAKING CHANGE) notation
findings.current: git.md:11-19 lists only feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, build, ci. git.md:21-25 has no rule for marking breaking changes.
findings.truth: The PR-title lint for develop also accepts `style`, `perf` and `revert`. Breaking changes are marked with `!` and this is used in practice: the toolchain's major-version removals were `feat(toolchain)!:`, and xyo-skills used `feat!:` for breaking redistribution changes. `style:` is in active use as well. release-please and the CHANGELOG depend on the `!` marker to signal a breaking change.
findings.evidence: ariestools-skills .github/workflows/lint-pr-title.yml:43-54 (types feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, test, style, perf, build, ci, revert). `git -C ariestools/toolchain log --all`: 13350616a "feat(toolchain)!: remove lintlint, republint, node-lint, gitlint aliases", 78f3807d6 "feat(toolchain)!: delete republintCommand shim module", 6fb65ed66 "style: resolve remaining unicorn warnings across packages and specs". xyo-skills b67cd91 "feat!: redirect xy-development and xy-toolchain to ariestools-skills (#72)". xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:77 ("`feat!:` for breaking").
findings.recommendation: Add `perf` (performance improvement), `style` (formatting or lint-only, no logic change) and `revert` to the Types list. Add a Rules bullet: "Mark breaking changes with `!` after the type/scope (e.g. `feat(toolchain)!: remove gitlint aliases`) and/or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Use it when removing or renaming a stable public export, CLI command or flag, or config field." Do not say release tooling depends on it.

verify.code: confirmed: git.md:11-19 lists only feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, build and ci, and git.md:21-25 has no breaking-change rule. ariestools-skills .github/workflows/lint-pr-title.yml:43-54 accepts feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, test, style, perf, build, ci and revert for develop PRs; the xyo-skills and xyo-skills-internal copies are identical apart from repo names. Verified commits: 13350616a and 78f3807d6 (2026-09-03, `feat(toolchain)!:`), 6fb65ed66 (2026-10-06, `style:`), xyo-skills b67cd91 (`feat!:`, 2026-08-25). xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:77 lists `feat!:` for breaking. Nuance: the release-please repos use always-bump-patch, so `!` changes changelog sections rather than forcing a major bump. The toolchain's CHANGELOG is hand-maintained. The recommendation still holds.
verify.skill: adjusted: The omission is real. git.md:11-19 lists only feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, build and ci, and nothing in skills/ covers breaking-change notation. ariestools-skills lint-pr-title.yml:43-54 also accepts style, perf and revert. `!` is used: toolchain 13350616a and 78f3807d6 (`feat(toolchain)!:`), xyo-skills b67cd91, 00ae679 and 0081693 (`feat!:`), and toolchain 6fb65ed66 is `style:`. Two claims are overstated, though. "release-please and the CHANGELOG depend on the `!` marker" is weak: the release-please repos use `always-bump-patch`, so `!` only changes changelog text, and the toolchain CHANGELOG is maintained by hand with versions set by `xy deploy` (CONTRIBUTING.md:39-41). Actual use is rare: 2 `!` commits in the toolchain's full history, no perf or revert commits, 1 style commit. No policy makes `!` "required" on every removed export. The related policy, toolchain docs/STABILITY.md:11 and :24, requires a major version bump for breaking stable `xy` changes and says nothing about commit notation. Following the current skill causes no failure, so low is the proportionate severity.

findings.title: Nothing says PR titles must be conventional commits, or that PRs into main accept only feat:/fix:
findings.current: absent. git.md covers commit messages only, and its type list (git.md:12-19) includes chore/docs/etc. with no warning that main rejects them in PR titles.
findings.truth: `lint-pr-title.yml` (ariestools-skills, xyo-skills, xyo-skills-internal) fails PRs into main unless the title is `feat:` or `fix:`; release-please branches are exempt. PRs into develop may use any conventional type. With squash merges the PR title becomes the commit subject that release-please reads for the changelog. An agent that titles a develop → main PR `chore: ...` fails CI.

findings.recommendation: In the same "Pull requests" subsection as the merge note: a PR title must itself be a valid conventional-commit subject, because in squash-merge repos it becomes the commit subject that changelog tooling reads. Where the repo lints PR titles, follow its allowed types. In the release-please skill-pack repos, PRs into `main` accept only `feat:`/`fix:` (use `fix:` for an integration PR with no features), and PRs into `develop` accept any conventional type.

findings.title: The absolute "Never Rewrite History" ban contradicts the workspace commit-identity policy and the repo-scoped rule
findings.current: git.md:48 "Git history is append-only. We always add to it, never rewrite it." git.md:51-54 forbid `git commit --amend`, any `git rebase`, `git push --force`/`--force-with-lease` and `git reset --hard` with no exceptions; git.md:61 "Bad commit message? Let it stand".
findings.truth: The workspace CLAUDE.md requires rewriting an unpushed commit that carries the wrong author email (keeping its tree, parents, message and dates) and allows a force-push of an already-pushed one after asking the user. ariestools-skills scopes the ban to shared branches ("no force-push to main/develop"). An agent following git.md literally would refuse the identity fix and push a commit with the wrong author. xyo-skills keeps the absolute wording, so the repos disagree and the skill should state the scope.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:52-56 (Commit identity: "Rewrite an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email ... ask before force-pushing one that is already pushed"; do not override identity with --author / -c user.email / GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL). AGENTS.md:260-264 (same). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:41 ("Never rewrite git history on shared branches (no force-push to main/develop)"). xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 (absolute form).
findings.recommendation: Scope the rule. Never rewrite pushed or shared history (main, develop, or any branch someone else may have fetched), and never force-push main/develop. Local, unpushed commits may be corrected when the repository's or workspace's own instructions require it, for example fixing commit identity while preserving tree, parents, message and dates. Force-pushing an already-pushed feature branch needs explicit user approval. Add "Repository and workspace CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md take precedence over this section." Optionally add generic identity guidance: commit with the configured git identity, never override it with --author or GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, and check `git log --format='%h %ae %ce' @{u}..HEAD` before pushing.

verify.code: confirmed: git.md:48-61 states the absolute ban, including `--amend`, any rebase, `--force`/`--force-with-lease` and 'Bad commit message? Let it stand'. CLAUDE.md:52-56 and AGENTS.md:260-264 require checking `git log --format='%h %ae %ce' <upstream>..HEAD`, rewriting an unpushed commit with the wrong email while keeping tree, parents, message and dates, and asking before force-pushing a pushed one. ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:41 scopes the ban to shared branches ('no force-push to main/develop'). xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 keeps the absolute form. An agent following git.md literally would refuse a required identity fix.
verify.skill: confirmed: The skill text matches. git.md:48 says history is append-only, git.md:50-55 forbid amend, rebase, force-push and reset --hard with no exceptions, and git.md:61 says a bad message should stand. The workspace CLAUDE.md:56 and AGENTS.md:264 require rewriting an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email, and allow force-pushing an already-pushed one after asking. This repo's own CLAUDE.md:41 limits the rule to shared branches ("Never rewrite git history on shared branches (no force-push to main/develop)"). xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 keeps the absolute form, so the scope needs stating. CLAUDE.md normally outranks a skill, and the scenario needs a wrong-identity commit to exist first. That makes this a real contradiction but not a routinely breaking one, and medium fits. The recommendation (scope the rule to pushed and shared history, allow repo- or workspace-directed fixes to local commits, require approval before any force-push, defer to repo instructions, add generic identity guidance) is correct and stays generic for outside consumers of the skill.

findings.title: No principle says tests must be independent, order-free and deterministic, which the standard runner setup assumes
findings.current: absent. testing.md covers naming, AAA, one concept, public interface, mocking and coverage. It mentions determinism only as a reason to mock the clock or randomness (testing.md:51).
findings.truth: Under the org preset, spec files run file-parallel by default. A spec under a plain spec/ folder runs in both the Node project and the real-browser project. Only explicitly serialized projects turn file parallelism off, and those are meant for e2e suites that share external state. So by default tests must not share mutable state, depend on run order or assume one runtime.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/vitest-config/src/defineXyVitestProjects.ts:47-50 ('spec/ — runs in BOTH realms'). toolchain/packages/vitest-config/src/defineXySerializedProject.ts:5-9,18 (serialized 'for e2e-style suites that share external state', fileParallelism: false only there). `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs test --help` shows '-j, --jobs Max parallel jobs [default: 16]'. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/test.ts:8-15 (xy test runs `vitest <path>` with the root projects config).
findings.recommendation: Add a short framework-agnostic section, 'Independent and Deterministic Tests'. Each test arranges and cleans up its own state and must pass in any order. Other test files may run at the same time, so never assume exclusive access to external resources such as fixed ports, shared temp paths, databases, environment variables or a shared chain. Control the clock, randomness and network rather than depending on them. Keep slow or stateful end-to-end suites separate from fast unit tests. Add one sentence pointing to xy-toolchain/testing.md for how spec placement selects the runtime and how to declare serialized suites. Drop the `xy test --jobs` evidence: that global flag is not forwarded to Vitest. The parallelism comes from Vitest's default fileParallelism: true, which the preset leaves on.

verify.code: adjusted: The core gap is real. Layer 1 has no independence or order rule; the only related mention is determinism at testing.md:51. A grep of skills/ for independent, any order and flaky finds nothing in testing guidance. Vitest 5.0.3 defaults to fileParallelism true (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/cac.*.js:937 and index.*.js:14438) and isolate true (defaults.*.js:52). The org preset does not override either (vitest-config/src/defineXyVitestConfig.ts:14-22, defineXyVitestProjects.ts:14-41). Only defineXySerializedProject sets fileParallelism: false (defineXySerializedProject.ts:5-9,18). Plain spec/ runs in both realms only when the browser project is enabled (defineXyVitestProjects.ts:47-50,59-61). Two problems with the evidence. First, `xy test -j/--jobs [default: 16]` is a global xy option that the test action never passes to Vitest: actions/test.ts:8-15 just runs `vitest <path>`. It is not evidence of test parallelism. Second, because Vitest isolates each file by default, in-memory module state is not shared across files. The real hazards are run-order dependence and shared external resources (ports, temp paths, databases, env, chains) touched by spec files running in parallel. 'Tests must pass … when run concurrently' overstates this: tests within a file run sequentially unless marked concurrent.
verify.skill: confirmed: I grepped every non-SDK skill for independen|any order|parallel|isolat|shared state|determinis|concurren. Layer 1 has no test-independence or order-independence principle. The only related text is the clock/randomness mocking bullet (testing.md:51) and 'every commit should … pass tests independently' (git.md:39), which is about commits, not tests. The underlying claim holds. Vitest's default file parallelism is never turned off by the preset (defineXyVitestProjects.ts:14-41 sets no fileParallelism). Only defineXySerializedProject sets fileParallelism: false (defineXySerializedProject.ts:5-9,18), for 'e2e-style suites that share external state'. Plain spec/ files run in both realms when browser is enabled (defineXyVitestProjects.ts:47-50). One piece of evidence is wrong: `xy test -j/--jobs` (default 16) is the global xy option, and actions/test.ts:8-15 never passes it to vitest. Parallelism comes from Vitest's own default, not from --jobs. The recommendation, a framework-agnostic 'Independent and Deterministic Tests' section plus a pointer to Layer 2 for realm routing and serialized suites, is correct and in the right layer. Low is proportionate.

findings.title: `pnpm install --resolution-only` is rejected by pnpm 12, the version every Aries Tools repo pins
findings.current: workflow.md:88 "After adding or changing dependencies, run `pnpm install --resolution-only` to force a fresh resolution check that surfaces all peer dependency warnings."
findings.truth: All Aries Tools repos pin pnpm 12.x through `packageManager`. pnpm 12.4.2 exits with "unexpected argument '--resolution-only'", and its `install --help` does not list the flag. pnpm 12 checks peers with a separate command, `pnpm peers` (also run as `pnpm peers check`), which "Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues" and supports `--json` and `--lockfile-only`.
findings.evidence: `pnpm --version` printed 12.4.2. `pnpm install --resolution-only --help` printed "error: unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found / tip: a similar argument exists: '--production'". The full `pnpm install --help` output has no resolution-only option. `pnpm --help` lists "peers: Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues", and `pnpm peers --help` says "The only subcommand is `check`, which is also what a bare `pnpm peers` runs". The `packageManager` fields are pnpm@12.4.2 in toolchain/package.json, sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit, and pnpm@12.9.1 in sdk-react.
findings.recommendation: Replace the last two sentences of workflow.md:88 with: "After adding or changing dependencies, run `pnpm peers` (pnpm 12+; same as `pnpm peers check`; add `--json` for automation or `--lockfile-only` to check without node_modules) to list unmet or missing peers. On older pnpm releases, `pnpm install --resolution-only` served this purpose." Drop the claim that "`pnpm install` suppresses warnings when the lockfile is already up to date" unless it can be re-verified on pnpm 12.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim holds on 10.1.1. workflow.md:88 tells the agent to run `pnpm install --resolution-only`. With pnpm 12.10.1, which toolchain/package.json now pins (it moved from 12.4.2 in updo 9a9f3a413, per `git diff 7eb43c3c2..HEAD -- package.json`), `pnpm install --resolution-only --help` fails with "error: unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found / tip: a similar argument exists: '--production'". `pnpm install --help` lists only `--lockfile-only`. `pnpm --help` lists "peers  Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues", and `pnpm peers --help` documents `check` as the only subcommand plus `--json` and `--lockfile-only`. sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit pin pnpm@12.4.2 and sdk-react pins 12.9.1. Two details are off. The toolchain pin is now 12.10.1, not 12.4.2. The recommendation's "applies only to pnpm 7–10" range was never checked: only pnpm 12 was tested, so pnpm 11 is unknown. The "`pnpm install` suppresses warnings when the lockfile is up to date" claim could not be re-tested without running an install.
verify.skill: confirmed: workflow.md:88 does tell the agent to run `pnpm install --resolution-only`. With the installed pnpm (now 12.10.1), `pnpm install --resolution-only --help` fails with "error: unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found / tip: a similar argument exists: '--production'". `pnpm install --help` has no resolution option. `pnpm --help` lists "peers  Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues", and `pnpm peers --help` shows `--json` and `--lockfile-only`, with `check` as the only subcommand (also what a bare `pnpm peers` runs). The packageManager pins are all pnpm 12: toolchain is now pnpm@12.10.1 (it was 12.4.2 at the baseline), sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit are @12.4.2, and sdk-react is @12.9.1. No other skill covers peer checking with a working command (grep for resolution-only or `pnpm peers` across skills/ finds only this line). Following the DoD step runs a failing command and skips the peer check, so high is justified. 10.1.1 does not change this.
