findings.title: Monorepo scoping example `pnpm --filter <package> build` fails in XY repos and contradicts the root-scoped `xy` convention
findings.current: workflow.md:27 "Use workspace-aware commands: `pnpm --filter <package> build`, not `cd packages/foo && pnpm build`"
findings.truth: XY workspace packages have no `build` script, so `pnpm --filter <pkg> build` has nothing to run. The convention is to run `xy` at the repository root and pass the package name as a positional argument (`pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`), because the CLI discovers workspaces, orders compilation and aggregates diagnostics. `--filter` still works for scripts a package really defines, for example the toolchain's own `pnpm --filter @ariestools/toolchain run package-compile`.
findings.evidence: Every sdk-js/packages/*/package.json has empty `scripts` except sdk (`sync-sdk-layout`, `test`), testing (`test`) and express (`coverage`). `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs build --help` shows "pnpm xy build [package] … package  Specific package to build". CLAUDE.md:32 "Append a package name to scope: `pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`". xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:46 "Use `xy` at repository/workspace scope." toolchain/package.json scripts.bootstrap-toolchain = `pnpm --filter @ariestools/toolchain run package-compile`.
findings.recommendation: Reword line 27: "Run commands at the scope the repo's tooling expects. If a root CLI orchestrates the workspace (XY repos: `pnpm xy <cmd> <package-name>` from the root), use its package argument. Otherwise use `pnpm --filter <package> run <script>` for scripts the package actually defines. Never `cd` into a package to build it."

verify.code: confirmed: Reproduced directly. In sdk-js, `pnpm --filter @ariestools/crypto build` (crypto has `scripts: {}`) printed "Error: ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT × None of the selected packages has a \"build\" script" and exited 1. Every sdk-js package lacks a build script; only sdk, testing and express define any scripts (sync-sdk-layout/test, test, coverage). cli-kit packages define only test/test:ci. `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs build --help` (10.1.1) shows "pnpm xy build [package] … package  Specific package to build". CLAUDE.md:32 and xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:51 ("Use `xy` at repository/workspace scope") back the root-scoped convention. The toolchain repo's `bootstrap-toolchain` script shows that `--filter … run <script>` remains valid for scripts a package really defines. The example on workflow.md:27 is a failing command in XY repos, so high is right.
verify.skill: adjusted: workflow.md:27 does give `pnpm --filter <package> build` as the example. No sdk-js package defines a `build` script: every packages/*/package.json scripts object is empty except sdk (sync-sdk-layout, test), testing (test) and express (coverage), so the literal example has nothing to run in XY repos. `xy build --help` (10.1.1) shows `pnpm xy build [package]`, and CLAUDE.md and xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:51 both say to run `xy` at repo scope with a package argument. The line's principle, to use workspace-aware commands instead of cd-ing into a package, is still correct, and step 2 conditions script use on the script existing. Running the example produces an immediate, self-evident "no script" error, not a silent wrong result. That makes it a stale, misleading example (medium), not a breaking instruction. The recommended rewording is correct.

findings.title: DoD gates name `pnpm build` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` / `pnpm compile` and require "zero warnings", but give no XY mapping or way to prove zero warnings
findings.current: workflow.md:68 "The repo's build command (`pnpm build` or equivalent)". :73 "The repo's lint command (`pnpm lint` or equivalent) passes with zero errors and zero warnings". :81 "Run the repo's test command (`pnpm test` or equivalent)". :89 "A clean `pnpm compile` does not guarantee the app will run".
findings.truth: In XY repos the equivalents are: `pnpm xy build` (compile + publint + deplint + ESLint; no tests), `pnpm xy test`, and `pnpm xy check` (git/packman/publint/repo/lint-config/skills policy). No `compile` script exists outside the toolchain repo itself; the command is `pnpm xy compile`. `xy lint` / `xy build` exit 0 when only warnings are present. Warnings fail the gate only with `--strict` or `XY_STRICT=1`. Many tier-2–4 rules, including the newly staged unicorn v77 rules, are warnings, so an exit code of 0 does not show "zero warnings".
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lintNext.ts:226 `exitCode: totalErrors + (isStrictMode() ? totalWarnings : 0)`. actions/lint.ts:232 adds `--max-warnings 0` only in strict mode. lib/reporting/xyReporter.ts:46-48 `isStrictMode()` reads the --strict flag or `process.env.XY_STRICT === '1'`. `xy.mjs --help` says "--strict  Treat warnings as errors" and "pnpm xy check  Run git lint, packman lint, publint, repo lint, lint lint, and skills lint". Toolchain commit a499070cc "stage unicorn v77 rules across tiers 2-4". xy-toolchain/commands.md:29 "Do not infer that a zero exit code means zero warnings unless `--strict` was active"; commands.md:34-39 lifecycle-gates table; project-profiles.md:144-152 "Verify the selected profile". CI runs `pnpm xy build` then `pnpm xy test` (sdk-js verify.yml:46,52).
findings.recommendation: Keep layer 1 generic, but add one line under Definition of Done: "In repos using `@ariestools/toolchain`, the build/lint/dependency gates are `pnpm xy build --strict` (or `pnpm xy lint --strict` + `pnpm xy deplint --strict`), tests are `pnpm xy test` (`xy build` does not run tests), and repository policy is `pnpm xy check`. See [xy-toolchain › Lifecycle gates](../xy-toolchain/commands.md#lifecycle-gates) and [Verify the selected profile](../xy-toolchain/project-profiles.md#verify-the-selected-profile)." Change `pnpm compile` on line 89 to "a clean compile (`pnpm xy compile` or the repo's equivalent)". Under §2, add: "A zero exit code proves zero warnings only if the lint command runs in strict / max-warnings-0 mode." Under §4 (phantom dependencies), point to `xy deplint`.

verify.code: confirmed: Verified on 10.1.1. lintNext.ts:226 `exitCode: totalErrors + (isStrictMode() ? totalWarnings : 0)`; lint.ts:232 adds `--max-warnings 0` only in strict mode; xyReporter.ts:46-48 `isStrictMode()` = flag || `XY_STRICT === '1'`. build.ts combines publint/deplint/lint results, and result.ts:57-66 sums the component exit codes, so `xy build` without `--strict` exits 0 when only warnings remain. `xy build --help` shows "--strict  Treat warnings as errors (exit code = errorCount + warningCount)". Only the toolchain repo has a root `compile` script; the others need `pnpm xy compile`. Commit a499070cc (unicorn v77 staged across tiers 2-4) is on main. The anchors commands.md#lifecycle-gates (line 31) and project-profiles.md#verify-the-selected-profile (line 143) exist, and commands.md:29 already warns about zero-exit vs. zero-warnings. One 10.1.1 detail: `xy check` now also runs agent lint ("Run agent lint, git lint, packman lint, publint, repo lint, lint lint, and skills lint"). That does not change the recommended wording, which only names `pnpm xy check`.
verify.skill: confirmed: workflow.md:68, 73, 81 and 89 name `pnpm build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm compile` and require zero warnings, but they give no `xy` mapping and no way to prove zero warnings. Source confirms the claims. In xyReporter.ts:46-47, isStrictMode() reads the flag or XY_STRICT==='1'. lintNext.ts:226 counts warnings toward the exit code only in strict mode. lint.ts:232 adds `--max-warnings 0` only in strict mode. `xy build --help` (10.1.1) says "--strict  Treat warnings as errors". The xy-toolchain skill already documents this (commands.md:29 and the lifecycle gates table at :31-42; project-profiles.md:143-152 "Verify the selected profile"), and both anchors the recommendation uses exist. A cross-reference from layer 1 is the right fix. In 10.1.1, `xy check` also runs agent lint (top-level help: "Run agent lint, git lint, packman lint, publint, repo lint, lint lint, and skills lint"). findings.title: Dependency-add guidance misses pnpm workspace-root targeting and the repos' `minimumReleaseAge` policy
findings.current: workflow.md:35 "when adding new dependencies, always use `pnpm add <package>` … to resolve the latest published version."
findings.truth: In a multi-package pnpm workspace, `pnpm add <dep>` at the root is refused unless `-w` / `--ignore-workspace-root-check` is passed. Package dependencies go in with `pnpm --filter <pkg> add <dep>`. Every Aries Tools repo also sets `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` (24h, excluding `@ariestools/*`) and an `allowBuilds` allowlist in pnpm-workspace.yaml. `pnpm add` will therefore resolve a version that can be older than `npm view <pkg> version` on purpose. Agents should not "fix" that by hand-pinning, and a new dependency with install scripts needs an `allowBuilds` entry.
findings.evidence: `pnpm add --help` (12.4.2): "--ignore-workspace-root-check  Permit adding dependencies to a multi-package workspace root without `-w`"; `-F, --filter`; `-w, --workspace-root`. pnpm-workspace.yaml in toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react and cli-kit all contain `minimumReleaseAge: 1440`, `minimumReleaseAgeExclude: ['@ariestools/*']` and `allowBuilds: {esbuild: true, unrs-resolver: true…}`.
findings.recommendation: Extend step 5: "In a workspace, add to the owning package: `pnpm --filter <pkg> add <dep>` (`-D` for dev). Use `-w` only for true root tooling. Respect the repo's `minimumReleaseAge`: the resolved version may trail npm `latest` by design, so do not override it. If the new dependency needs install scripts, add it to `allowBuilds` in pnpm-workspace.yaml."

verify.code: confirmed: `pnpm add --help` (pnpm 12.10.1) lists "--ignore-workspace-root-check  Permit adding dependencies to a multi-package workspace root without `-w`", `-F, --filter` and `-w, --workspace-root`. pnpm-workspace.yaml in toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit all set `minimumReleaseAge: 1440`, `minimumReleaseAgeExclude: ['@ariestools/*']` and an `allowBuilds` map (esbuild/unrs-resolver true; toolchain also has `core-js: false`). No skill file mentions minimumReleaseAge, allowBuilds or workspace-root targeting (grep of skills/). workflow.md:35 gives only bare `pnpm add <package>`.
verify.skill: confirmed: Grep across skills/ finds no mention of `-w`/`--workspace-root`, `--filter … add`, minimumReleaseAge or allowBuilds, so the gap exists across the whole pack, not just this file. Every repo's pnpm-workspace.yaml (toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit) sets `minimumReleaseAge: 1440`, `minimumReleaseAgeExclude: ['@ariestools/*']` and an `allowBuilds` allowlist (esbuild, unrs-resolver; the toolchain also sets core-js: false). `pnpm add --help` lists `--ignore-workspace-root-check`, `-F, --filter` and `-w, --workspace-root`. workflow.md:35 tells agents that `pnpm add` resolves "the latest published version", which is false under minimumReleaseAge, and the toolchain reads this policy itself (lib/pnpmConfig/readMinReleaseAge.ts). Layer 1 already speaks pnpm directly, so this belongs here. Medium is right.

findings.title: Credential Safety says to always gitignore `.npmrc` and all `.env.*`, which conflicts with toolchain behavior and its gitignore template
findings.current: workflow.md:52 "`.npmrc` — may contain npm auth tokens after `npm login`. Always add it to `.gitignore`." workflow.md:53 "`.env`, `.env.*` … Always gitignored." workflow.md:55 "verify `.gitignore` includes `.npmrc` and `.env`".
findings.truth: `xy packman convert` (to pnpm) creates an empty project `.npmrc` (convertToPnpm.ts:120-126, step 5 at :163), and the toolchain and sdk-react repos track an empty `.npmrc`. The toolchain gitignore template, which `xy gitignore` merges, ignores `.env` and `.env.*` but re-includes `!.env.example`, and has no `.npmrc` entry. Auth tokens belong in the user-level ~/.npmrc or an env-var reference, not in the project file.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/packman/convertToPnpm.ts:120-126 (`writeFileSync(npmrcPath, '', 'utf8')`). `git ls-files .npmrc` is tracked in toolchain and sdk-react, and both files are empty. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/gitignore/template.gitignore:24-27 (`.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`; no .npmrc). browser-kit/.gitignore:25 and ariestools-skills/.gitignore:74 do ignore .npmrc, so practice is inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Reword: "Never commit auth tokens. Keep registry credentials in the user-level `~/.npmrc` or as `${NPM_TOKEN}` references. A tracked project `.npmrc` must contain no secrets; some toolchain-converted repos track an empty one, so do not delete or untrack it. Gitignore `.env` and `.env.*` but keep the `!.env.example` exception that the toolchain gitignore template ships."

findings.title: Single-package pnpm repos with no exports or bin are auto-classified as workspace-root, not service or app. The skill never says to set the role
findings.current: project-profiles.md:63 says "Deplint auto-detects a **role**". :72 describes `workspace-root` as "Monorepo root / meta package". :108-115, the single-package section ("Treat the repository root as the package"), never mentions roles. :129 says "A private monorepo root is commonly `workspace-root`".
findings.truth: Deplint's detectRole checks for a workspace root before it checks for service or app. Any package directory with a `workspaces` field or a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file, and with no library surface or bin, becomes `workspace-root`. Its defaults are runtimeEntry 'none', prodInstallMatters false and peerTarget 'none'. With runtimeEntry 'none' the source fallback is off, so every runtime import counts as non-runtime. The graph also counts as trusted, so `move-to-dev` is allowed. Every pnpm repo must keep a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: packman lint (part of `xy check`) fails at error level without one, and its fix cannot create the file. The pnpm package manager also treats an empty `packages:` list as a single-package repo. The result: a single-package private service or app (start script `node dist/...`, no main/exports/bin) is classified `workspace-root`, and `xy fix` (which runs `deplint --fix`) demotes its runtime dependencies to devDependencies.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/deplint/isTerminalPackage.ts:234-242 (isWorkspaceRootPackage: `workspaces` field or pnpm-workspace.yaml/yml exists), :282-285 (workspace-root branch runs first in detectRole), :142-148 (workspace-root facets). snapshot.ts:260-261 (runtimeEntry 'none' counts as trusted), :271 (useSourceFallback is runtimeEntry !== 'none'). getExternalImportsFromFiles.ts:126-128 (no source fallback, so the runtime import set is empty). actions/packman/lint.ts:147-152 ("No pnpm-workspace.yaml found" fails the check), :170-172 (the fix returns false when the file is missing), :321-333 (`packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAge` defaultLevel 'error'). pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:55-63 (single-package repos keep pnpm-workspace.yaml with empty packages). actions/fix.ts:21 (`xy fix` runs `deplint --fix`). Read-only check, running the classifier source with `node -e "import { classifyDeplintPackage } from '.../isTerminalPackage.ts' ..."`: xylabs/api-coin-xl1 (private, start `node dist/node/index.mjs`, no role configured) → `workspace-root {"prodInstallMatters":false,"runtimeEntry":"none"}`. xylabs/web-xylabs.com-react and XYOracleNetwork/app-portal.xyo.network-react (Vite apps) → `workspace-root`. XYOracleNetwork/api-automation-witness-nodejs/xy.config.ts:6 already works around this with `deplint: { role: 'service', runtimeRoots: ['src/index.ts'] }`.
findings.recommendation: Add a step to "Single-package repository": "If the root package has no `main`/`module`/`exports` and no `bin` (a typical single-package service, app or tooling repo), set `commands.deplint.role` explicitly in the root `xy.config.ts`, for example `{ role: 'service', runtimeRoots: ['src/index.ts'] }`. Deplint classifies any package directory that has `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (which packman lint requires) or a `workspaces` field, and no library or bin surface, as `workspace-root`, and that role demotes runtime dependencies aggressively." Reword :72 and :129: `workspace-root` detection depends on a workspace marker plus no library or bin surface, not on the repo being a monorepo. Separately, consider filing a toolchain issue: detectRole should not treat a root whose pnpm-workspace.yaml lists no packages as `workspace-root`.

findings.title: Deplint auto-detects `library/cli` only from main/module or non-root export subpaths. A bin with a `.`-only export (or types only) is classified `cli`
findings.current: :25 "A package with both `bin` and an importable public API is **library/CLI**". :49 "role `cli` unless it also exposes an importable API (`library/cli`)". :63 "Deplint auto-detects a **role**".
findings.truth: When `bin` is present, hasLibrarySurface is true only for `main`, `module`, or an exports map with a key other than `.`, `./package.json` or `./README.md`. Several bin shapes therefore auto-detect as `cli` (hasImportConsumers false, peerTarget 'dep') even when `.` is a real importable API: bin with only a `.` export, bin with a string `exports`, and bin with only `types`. Library peer rules then do not apply. @ariestools/toolchain itself (bin plus `types`, consumers import `XyConfig`) classifies as `cli`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/deplint/isTerminalPackage.ts:76 (EXPORT_META_KEYS = '.', './package.json', './README.md'), :157-176 (hasLibrarySurface / isCliOnlyExports), :287-293. spec/deplint/isTerminalPackage.spec.ts:111-145 ("bin plus CLI-only exports as cli"; only an extra `./utils` subpath or `main`/`module` gives library/cli). Read-only classifier run: ariestools/toolchain/packages/toolchain → `cli`; ariestools/sdk-meta-server-nodejs (bin plus `./getFlags` and other subpaths) → `library/cli`.
findings.recommendation: After :25, or in the role section after :63, add one note: "Deplint auto-detects `library/cli` only when a `bin` package also has `main`, `module`, or an export subpath other than `.`, `./package.json` or `./README.md`. A bin package with only a `.` export (or a types-only surface) auto-detects as `cli`. If that surface is a real importable API, set `commands.deplint.role: 'library/cli'` in the package's xy.config.ts."

findings.title: Missing visibility axis and the error-level `dep.*.not-public` rules for public packages that depend on private or restricted workspace siblings
findings.current: :36 "Identify whether the package is independently publishable, deployable, or only a private workspace orchestrator." :125 "Keep workspace-internal runtime packages in `dependencies`; do not convert them mechanically to peers." The file never mentions `publishConfig.access` or the not-public rules.
findings.truth: Since toolchain v10.0.3 (commit 2f9db7e4e, included in 10.1.0), deplint has `dep.dependencies.not-public` and `dep.peerDependencies.not-public`. Both default to error and cannot be auto-fixed. A package is public when it is not `private` and is either unscoped or has `publishConfig.access: 'public'`; a scoped package without `access` counts as restricted. For a public package, `dependencies` and `peerDependencies` may not list: a private or restricted workspace sibling, a `file:`/`link:`/`portal:`/`catalog:`/`patch:`/git spec, or a name that is not on npmjs. Following :125 (keep a private sibling in `dependencies` of a published package) therefore fails `xy deplint` and `xy build`. The fixes are to publish the sibling or to use vendor mode, which keeps private packages in devDependencies.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/classifyPackageVisibility.ts:13-23. actions/deplint/rulesNotPublic.ts:39-50, :55-70, :123-127 and :141-145 (severity 'error'). actions/deplint/rules.md:3, :17, :211, :231. `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs deplint --rules` shows `error │ dep.dependencies.not-public │ no` and `error │ dep.peerDependencies.not-public │ no`. `git tag --contains 2f9db7e4e` → v10.0.3 … v10.1.0.
findings.recommendation: Add a Visibility axis (private / restricted / public, based on `private` and `publishConfig.access`) to the table at :17-23. Extend monorepo item 5: "…in `dependencies`, but a public package may only depend on public siblings. Give each sibling `publishConfig.access: 'public'`, or bundle private implementations with vendor mode (private packages in devDependencies; see compilation.md#vendor-mode). `dep.dependencies.not-public` / `dep.peerDependencies.not-public` are errors and are not auto-fixable."

Both `dep.dependencies.not-public` and `dep.peerDependencies.not-public` have severity 'error' and fixable []. `xy.mjs deplint --rules` shows both as `error … no`. `git tag --contains 2f9db7e4e` lists v10.0.3 through v10.1.1. grep shows no mention of not-public, publishConfig or visibility anywhere under skills/. docs/vendor-mode.md:303-316 confirms that vendored private packages belong in devDependencies. findings.title: Install command fails at a pnpm monorepo root because it has no -w flag
findings.current: toolchain.md:43-45 gives `pnpm add -D @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript`, and toolchain.md:51 says `xy` runs at repository/workspace scope.
findings.truth: The toolchain is installed at the repo root because `xy` must run from there. In a multi-package pnpm workspace, `pnpm add` refuses to add to the root unless you pass `-w` / `--workspace-root` (or `--ignore-workspace-root-check`). The scaffolded monorepo also puts @ariestools/toolchain in the root devDependencies. So the command as written fails in the default (monorepo) topology.
findings.evidence: Command `pnpm --version` printed 12.4.2. Command `pnpm add --help` lists `--ignore-workspace-root-check  Permit adding dependencies to a multi-package workspace root without -w` and `-w, --workspace-root`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/README.md:54 says to run `xy` from the repository root. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:39-50 puts @ariestools/toolchain in the root devDependencies.
findings.recommendation: Show the root form `pnpm add -D -w @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript eslint`. Explain that -w is required when pnpm-workspace.yaml lists more than one `packages` pattern (pnpm otherwise refuses with ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT) and is harmless otherwise. -w needs a pnpm-workspace.yaml, which packman lint requires anyway. Add one sentence: toolchain, config, eslint, typescript and vitest devDependencies belong on the root package, because `xy` runs from the root.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived. The toolchain repo now pins pnpm 12.10.1 (package.json:49; the finding cited 12.4.2). `pnpm add --help` under that version lists `--ignore-workspace-root-check  Permit adding dependencies to a multi-package workspace root without -w`, so a plain `pnpm add -D ...` at a monorepo root is rejected. toolchain.md:44 has no -w. packages/toolchain/README.md says to run `xy` from the repository root. templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:39-51 puts @ariestools/toolchain, the config packages, eslint, typescript and vitest in the root devDependencies. 10.1.1 does not change this. Under the vocabulary, a failing command is high severity.
verify.skill: adjusted: The skill text is quoted correctly: toolchain.md:43-45 has no -w. But the claim that the command fails 'in the default (monorepo) topology' is wrong as stated. pnpm only throws ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT when the `packages:` list in pnpm-workspace.yaml has more than one pattern. Evidence: pnpm 10.33.2 dist/pnpm.cjs:165583 checks `opts.workspacePackagePatterns.length > 1`, the value comes from `workspaceManifest?.packages ?? ['.']` (:18886), and pnpm 11.25.0 dist/pnpm.mjs:225456 and :171359 do the same. The scaffold template (templates/repo/cli/root/pnpm-workspace.yaml: one pattern, `packages/**/*`), toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react and cli-kit all have a single pattern, so the bare command succeeds there. It does fail in many real org repos with several patterns: sdk-xyo-client-js (7), xl1-protocol (4), sdk-xyo-react-js (4), ariestools/ariestools (3), dapp-kit (2). The pnpm 12 native binary's condition could not be checked. Because the failure only happens in multi-pattern repos and pnpm's error message names the -w fix, medium fits better than high.

findings.title: pnpm-workspace.yaml and its release-age/verify settings are required in every pnpm repo; the skill says 'when needed'
findings.current: toolchain.md:37 says "For pnpm workspaces, keep `pnpm-workspace.yaml` at the repository root." toolchain.md:114 says "Pin pnpm in `packageManager` and create the correct workspace file when needed."
findings.truth: `xy check` runs `xy packman lint`, which is stable. For any pnpm repo, single-package or monorepo, it raises errors (exit code is non-zero) unless pnpm-workspace.yaml contains three settings: `minimumReleaseAge` of at least 1440 minutes, a `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` covering the scopes actually used (@ariestools/*, @xylabs/*, @xyo-network/*), and `verifyDepsBeforeRun`. If the file is missing, the check reports "No pnpm-workspace.yaml found", and `--fix` cannot create it. Separately, `xy repo lint` raises an error if a pnpm monorepo declares `workspaces` in package.json (`repo.workspaces-field-placement`).
findings.evidence: Command `xy.mjs packman lint --rules` shows packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAge, packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAgeExclude and packman.pnpm.verifyDepsBeforeRun, all at level error. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/packman/lint.ts:147-169 (needs the yaml file, reads minimumReleaseAge from it), :172-174 (fix returns false when the file is missing), :39 (DEFAULT_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN='warn'). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/pnpmConfig/readMinReleaseAge.ts:12 (floor 1440). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/releaseAgeExcludeScopes.ts:6. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/checkCommand.ts:13,55-56 (check runs packman lint). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint.ts:176-197 (pnpm: no package.json `workspaces`). toolchain/docs/STABILITY.md:84 (packman lint is stable and part of xy check). The toolchain's own pnpm-workspace.yaml:7-10 is a working example.

findings.title: Root scripts example uses `vitest run` and leaves out how `xy` defers to same-named root scripts
findings.current: toolchain.md:96-106 shows root scripts build/compile/lint/`lint:fix: xy lint --fix`/`"test": "vitest run"`. This conflicts with toolchain.md:23 ("Do not substitute a raw ... Vitest invocation for a repository wrapper"). Root-script deferral is not mentioned anywhere in the file.
findings.truth: When you run `xy <command>` with no subcommand and the root package.json has a script of the same name, xy hands off to that script (`pnpm run <command>`). XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT=1 stops this from recursing, and `--no-defer` or `XY_NO_DEFER=1` turns it off. With the skill's example, `pnpm xy test` silently runs `vitest run` and skips `xy test`'s target handling. The package README hello-world and the `xy repo init` template both use `build/compile/lint/fix/test/check` mapped to `xy <cmd>`, including `"test": "xy test"` and `"check": "xy check"`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:60-67. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/tryRunLocalScript.ts:13-52 (root scripts only, XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT guard, delegates via `run <name>`). Output of `xy.mjs --help` shows `--no-defer  Do not defer to local package.json script of the same name`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/README.md:22-32. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:28-35.
findings.recommendation: Align the example with the upstream README and template: build/compile/lint/fix/test/check each map to `xy <cmd>`, i.e. `"test": "xy test"`, `"fix": "xy fix"`, `"check": "xy check"`; keeping `lint:fix` is fine. Add one sentence: `xy <cmd>`, run with no positional argument, defers to a same-named root script, and `"build": "xy build"` is safe because XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT=1 guards against recursion. `--no-defer` or `XY_NO_DEFER=1` forces the built-in command. Since 10.1.1, `publish` and `deploy` never defer unless `--defer` is passed. Link to commands.md#global-behavior instead of repeating the flag table.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue holds. In the xyParseOptions.ts middleware, `xy <cmd>` with no positional argument hands off to a same-named root script through tryRunLocalScript. XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT=1 prevents recursion (tryRunLocalScript.ts:32), and --no-defer or XY_NO_DEFER=1 turns hand-off off. So with toolchain.md:103, `pnpm xy test` runs `vitest run`. The README hello-world and the repo init template (package.json.tmpl:28-35) map build/compile/lint/fix/test/check to `xy <cmd>`. Three details differ from the finding. (1) 10.1.1 commit b75077b16 changes the rule: `publish` and `deploy` no longer hand off unless `--defer` is passed (tryRunLocalScript.ts:13, 45-50; the new `--defer` option is in xyParseOptions.ts and `xy --help`). (2) Hand-off is skipped when a positional target is given (`argv._.length > 1`), so `xy test <path>` always runs the built-in. (3) The hand-off is not silent: it prints 'Delegating "test" to local script'.
verify.skill: adjusted: The example is real (toolchain.md:96-106 has `"test": "vitest run"`) and differs from upstream: packages/toolchain/README.md:22-32 uses `xy test`/`xy check`, and the repo-init template (package.json.tmpl:28-35) adds `fix` and `check`. The claimed harm is overstated. Deferral only happens when no positional argument is given (xyParseOptions.ts:61-67: `if (!commandName || argv._.length > 1) return`), so `xy test <target>` never defers and target handling is never skipped. With no target, the built-in `xy test` runs `vitest .` (actions/test.ts:13-14), which is equivalent to the deferred `vitest run` apart from watch mode. The deferral is also not silent: it logs 'Delegating "test" to local script'. commands.md:26 already documents `--no-defer`. 10.1.1 (b75077b16) adds a rule the recommendation must include: `publish` and `deploy` no longer defer unless `--defer` is passed (tryRunLocalScript.ts:13,45-50). This is a consistency/polish issue, so low.

findings.title: 'Require Node.js 22' step does not match the enforced engines/volta placement policy
findings.current: toolchain.md:115 says "Require Node.js 22 or newer unless the consuming product imposes a newer version."
findings.truth:
Where the Node requirement goes depends on the package:
- The root package must not declare `engines`. `repo.engines-non-terminal` is an error with the message "use volta instead".
- Private (terminal) workspace packages must not declare `engines`.
- Non-private workspace packages must declare `engines`.
- Publishable packages with Node exports need `engines.node` inside ">=22" (node.engines-node-range).
- Browser/neutral-only packages must not declare `engines.node` (node.engines-node-portable).
- The root `volta.node` should track the latest Node (node.volta-node-latest). The toolchain root itself uses volta node "26".
- The engines and volta values must include the latest Node version (repo.engines-lts, error).

An agent that adds `engines.node >=22` at the root, or to a neutral library, trips these rules.
findings.evidence: Output of `xy.mjs repo lint --rules`: repo.engines-non-terminal (error), repo.engines-lts (error), repo.volta-only-root (error). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint-engines.ts:71-87. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/node-lint.ts:18 (REQUIRED_NODE_RANGE='>=22'), :110-166. Output of `xy.mjs node lint --rules`. toolchain/package.json:50-52 (volta node 26, no engines).
findings.recommendation: Replace step 2 with these rules. Monorepo: no `engines` on the root package; pin Node there with `volta.node` (latest; only the root declares volta). Private workspace packages: no `engines`. Every publishable workspace package: declares `engines` with `node: ">=22"` (a range inside >=22 that still includes the latest Node, or repo.engines-lts errors). Do not strip `engines` from neutral/browser packages: `xy node lint` (warn-only, not in `xy check`) may flag `engines.node` there, but removing `engines` trips the error-level repo.engines-non-terminal. Single-package repo: repo lint does not run, and the root is the published package, so `engines.node: ">=22"` belongs at the root. Verify with `pnpm xy repo lint` / `pnpm xy check`.

verify.code: adjusted: Real issue: toolchain.md:115 says nothing about where the Node requirement goes, and repo lint enforces placement. Several details are wrong. (a) Every repo.* engines/volta rule runs only in monorepos: package-lint.ts:534-536 prints 'Not a monorepo — skipping repo lint checks'. In a single-package repo the root is the published package, and node lint expects `engines.node` within >=22 there when it has Node exports. (b) node.engines-node-range, node.engines-node-portable and node.volta-node-latest are warn-level (`xy node lint --rules`), and node lint is not part of `xy check`. (c) repo.engines-lts errors only on engines ranges; old volta pins produce warnings (package-lint-engines.ts:190-215). (d) The recommendation to leave `engines.node` off neutral packages conflicts with repo.engines-non-terminal: every non-private workspace package must declare `engines` (package-lint-engines.ts:85-86). If node lint --fix removes the only key, it deletes `engines` entirely (node-lint.ts:145-149), which then trips that error. The toolchain's own neutral packages (tsconfig, tsconfig-dom, tsconfig-react, lib-neutral) keep engines.node '>=22' and accept the node.engines-node-portable warning: running `xy node lint` in the toolchain repo shows exactly those warnings. Severity medium stands.
verify.skill: adjusted: toolchain.md:115 is vague about placement, and the enforced rules are real. In 10.1.1, repo.engines-non-terminal (error, in `xy check` via repo lint) rejects root `engines` ('use volta instead'), rejects `engines` on private workspace packages, and requires `engines` on every non-private workspace package (package-lint-engines.ts:71-87). repo.volta-only-root is also an error. These apply only to monorepos: repo lint is skipped for non-monorepos (package-lint.ts:534-536). The finding's recommendation to leave `engines.node` off browser/neutral packages is wrong. node.engines-node-portable is only a warning, `xy node lint` is not part of `xy check`, and its fixer deletes `engines` entirely when node was the only key (node-lint.ts:146-153). That then trips the error-level repo.engines-non-terminal ('is a library but has no engines field', :85-86), whose fixer copies a sibling's engines back (:139-140). Upstream repos keep `engines.node` on neutral packages and accept the warning: `xy node lint` in toolchain flags lib-neutral and tsconfig*, and in sdk-js flags 8 packages. Also, repo.engines-lts makes `engines` ranges that exclude the latest Node an error, while an old volta pin is only a warning (:195-216).

findings.title: Root compile config does not cascade into a package that has its own xy.config.ts
findings.current: "Root configuration cascades to packages under that root. Package-level configuration overrides or deep-merges the applicable root settings." (compilation.md:29)
findings.truth: Root-to-workspace merging only exists for `commands.*`, through loadWorkspaceCommandConfig/mergeCommandConfig. `package-compile` runs in the package directory (`pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec package-compile`) and calls `loadConfig()`. That does a cosmiconfig search from cwd ('global' strategy, stopping at the .git root) and uses the first xy.config it finds. When a package has its own xy.config.ts, root `compile.*` settings such as `compiler`, `node`, `validate`, `mode` and `bundlePackages` are dropped, not deep-merged. Root compile settings reach only packages with no config of their own. One exception: the shared validator does fall back to the root `compile.validate`. The real repos show this. sdk-js and toolchain set `compile.compiler: 'native'` at the root and then repeat it in every package config.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/lib/loadConfig.ts:53-59 (cosmiconfig with stopDir), 62-92 (ensureRootConfigLoaded/loadConfig = search() from cwd, merged only with params), 210-241 (cascade only in loadWorkspaceCommandConfig for commands); src/pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:185-188 (runInWorkspaceByName = pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec); src/actions/package/compile/compile.ts:16-19 (packageCompile -> loadConfig(inConfig)); node_modules cosmiconfig@10.0.1 dist/index.js:104,120 (searchStrategy 'global' when stopDir set); src/actions/tsc-validate/tscValidate.ts:30 (shared path is the only compile cascade: `wsConfig.compile?.validate ?? rootValidate`); sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 + sdk-js/packages/crypto/xy.config.ts:5 + sdk-js/packages/sdk/xy.config.ts:10; toolchain/xy.config.ts:7 + toolchain/packages/vitest-config/xy.config.ts:5 (compiler repeated per package). toolchain docs/xy-config.md:15 makes the same inaccurate claim.
findings.recommendation: Split the sentence. `commands.*` cascades: the root provides defaults, workspace configs deep-merge, rule tuples are replaced per id, arrays are unioned. `compile.*` does not: `package-compile` uses the nearest xy.config.ts, so a package config fully replaces the root compile block. Repeat any root compile settings you need (e.g. `compiler`, `validate`) in each package xy.config.ts. Root-only compile fields (`compile.validator`) are read from the repo-root config. Also file a toolchain docs fix for docs/xy-config.md:15.

Package config deep-merges.'). Here is how compile config is actually loaded. bin/package/compile.ts:12 calls packageCompile({verbose}). That calls loadConfig(inConfig) (package/compile/compile.ts:19), which runs getExplorer().search() from the process cwd (loadConfig.ts:53-57, 69) and deep-merges only with the params passed in (loadConfig.ts:90-93). findings.title: Validation-then-emit ordering is wrong for workspace `xy compile`
findings.current: "By default, `xy compile` performs a no-emit TypeScript validation pass over the full package ... then emits package output through the selected compiler mode." (compilation.md:82)
findings.truth: Validate-then-emit is the order only for `package-compile` with no flags, which is what `xy compile <pkg>` runs. Monolith mode runs layout sync, then validation, then emit. A workspace-level `xy compile` (also build/recompile) runs two phases. First every package emits in topological order over dependencies and devDependencies with `package-compile --emit-only`, which does no type check, and a failure stops dependents. Then validation runs, either `package-compile --validate-only` per package or a single shared-host pass. So when validation fails in a workspace compile, dist has already been written. With `compile.validate: false` the workspace path skips the no-emit check entirely, while a single-package compile still runs the narrower per-source-folder check.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/compile.ts:417-426 (Compile:Emit topological, `--emit-only`), 428-445 (Compile:Validate per-package `--validate-only` or shared), 556-570 (single package runs plain package-compile); src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileEsbuild.ts:401-414 (shouldRunFolderChecks = !fullValidation && !emitOnly), 471-478 (validate before emit inside one package); src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileMonolith.ts:135-171.
findings.recommendation: Reword the Type validation paragraph. Single-package `package-compile` (what `xy compile <pkg>` runs) does a full-package no-emit tsc pass (specs, stories, configs, .storybook), then emits. Monolith syncs the layout first. Workspace `xy compile`/`xy build`/`xy recompile` emits every package topologically (dependencies and devDependencies) with `--emit-only` first. That phase skips the full-package validation, but declaration emit still runs tsc over each compiled source folder, so source type errors fail emit and stop dependents. The validation phase runs afterwards (`--validate-only` per package, or the shared host). A workspace compile that fails validation can therefore leave fresh dist output. With `compile.validate: false`, the workspace path runs no extra check, while a single-package compile still runs a per-source-folder check. Also correct compilation.md:134: declaration emit runs before esbuild in each folder, so a declaration failure prevents that folder's JS emit.

verify.code: adjusted: The ordering problem is real. runCompileAll (actions/compile.ts:417-445) first runs Compile:Emit topologically over dependencies and devDependencies with `package-compile --emit-only`, stopping dependents on failure. Only then does it run Compile:Validate (`--validate-only` per package, or the shared host). compilePackage (actions/compile.ts:556-561) runs plain package-compile, which validates the full package and then emits (packageCompileEsbuild.ts resolveCompileMode plus the full-validation-before-emit block). Monolith syncs, then validates, then emits (packageCompileMonolith.ts:155-170). With compile.validate:false the workspace path does no extra check, while a single package runs the per-folder check (shouldRunFolderChecks = !fullValidation && !emitOnly). One part of the finding is wrong: it says `--emit-only` 'does no type check'. Emit-only skips the full-package no-emit validation and the per-folder check, but compileFolder still runs the tsc declaration emit (createDeclarationEmitter -> runTsc with emitDeclarationOnly; createTypescriptConfig sets no noCheck) before esbuild. Type errors in the compiled source folder (excluding specs and stories) therefore still fail the emit phase and stop dependents. The full-package pass that runs later adds specs, stories, configs and .storybook. 10.1.1 does not change this.
verify.skill: confirmed: compilation.md:82 says `xy compile` validates and then emits. runCompileAll (actions/compile.ts:417-445) does the opposite. It first runs 'Compile:Emit' topologically over dependencies and devDependencies with `package-compile --emit-only`, returns early if emit fails, and only then validates (per-package `--validate-only` or the shared host). compilePackage (compile.ts:556-570) runs a plain package-compile, which validates before emitting (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:461-478). The folder-check logic (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:401-414) supports the note about validate:false. Monolith runs sync, then validation, then emit (packageCompileMonolith.ts:143-171). The skill's troubleshooting line 134 hints that the phases are separate but never corrects the order. A failed workspace compile leaving fresh dist output is a material behavior to document. The recommended rewording is accurate.

findings.title: Target object shape is misdescribed as an 'options object'
findings.current: "Enable a target with `true` or a non-empty options object." (compilation.md:36); "If no target is enabled, build `neutral`." (compilation.md:35)
findings.truth: A platform target object is keyed by source directory, e.g. `{ src: {} }` or `{ src: { entry: [...], ...esbuildOptions } }`. It is not a bag of options. Each key is treated as a srcDir, so `node: { minify: true }` enables node (and turns neutral off), finds no `minify/` directory and silently emits nothing. The legacy `esbuildOptions` key is stripped before classification, so `node: { esbuildOptions: {...} }` alone counts as disabled. Neutral is the default only when `neutral` is unset. With `neutral: false` and no other target, nothing builds. Shared esbuild overrides belong in `compile.esbuild.options`. `compile.tsup.options` is deprecated but still honored.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:14-22 (strip esbuildOptions), 35-57 (non-empty after strip -> build), 79-83 (neutral default only when unset); src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileEsbuild.ts:237-243, 292-297 (missing srcDir -> return 0 silently), 427-443 (srcDir iteration and merge order incl. compile.esbuild.options); src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:243-272 (doc example `{ src: {} }`, tsup deprecated).

findings.title: A local no-restricted-imports block, including the one lint init generates, silently replaces the shared tier-0 barrel/src import bans
findings.current: eslint.md:22 "derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels"; eslint.md:130 "Place justified local overrides after the recommended config. Run `xy lint lint` to distinguish intentional additions from redundant shared rules and overrides requiring review."
findings.truth: The shared config sets `no-restricted-imports` at error level. Its options ban `./index.ts` … `../../../../../../../index.ts` barrel paths and the `**/src/**` import patterns. If you accept a barrel prompt, `xy lint init` adds an unscoped `{ rules: { 'no-restricted-imports': ['warn', { paths: [...barrels] }] } }` block after the recommended config. In flat config a later rule entry with options replaces the earlier options completely. The result is that the barrel-index.ts and src/ bans disappear and the rule drops to warn. `xy lint lint` deliberately exempts this block from `lintlint.rule-override` (isLintInitBarrelRestriction), so nothing reports it. This works against the workspace policy "no importing from barrel index.ts files".
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14,24-27 (restrictedImportPaths, error); src/rules/index.ts:19-26,40-56 (src patterns); src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:46 (tier 0 error). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:132-138 (unscoped 'warn' block appended after recommendedConfig). lintlint.ts:183-191 (exemption). Empirical: calculateConfigForFile('src/index.ts') with recommendedConfig({tier:3}) gives [2,{paths:['./index.ts',...],patterns:[{group:['**/src/**',...]}]}]. Adding the generator-style block gives [1,{paths:[{name:'@xylabs/hex',...}]}]. Real consumers affected: XYOracleNetwork/xl1-faucet-twitter/eslint.config.ts:145-150, XYOracleNetwork/webble/eslint.config.ts:67-70.
findings.recommendation: Add a caution in 'Overrides and troubleshooting' and next to the lint init text (eslint.md:22, 130). In flat config, any later `no-restricted-imports` entry that has options replaces the shared index.ts `paths` and the src/ `patterns` entirely, even when it is scoped with `files`. The block that `xy lint init` generates when you accept a barrel prompt does exactly this: it drops the shared bans and lowers the rule to warn. `xy lint lint` intentionally does not report that block. Tell agents to put barrel steering under a different rule id (e.g. `@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports`) so the shared core rule stays intact. The other option is to rebuild the shared options from the exported `correctnessRulesConfig` (all files) and `srcImportsConfig` (src files only, same `files` glob) at `error` and add the barrel paths to both. Do not suggest scoping with `files` as a fix. Separately, flag a toolchain fix: lint-init should emit a non-clobbering rule, and lintlint's isLintInitBarrelRestriction comment/exemption should be revisited.

findings.title: lint init description is inaccurate: it is interactive, the barrel list is fixed, and it may install barrel packages
findings.current: eslint.md:16-22 "Prefer the generator: pnpm xy lint init … It detects React, installs the applicable config package and ESLint, generates `eslint.config.ts`, includes repository `.gitignore` behavior when the file exists, and derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels. Review the generated diff before accepting an overwrite."
findings.truth: `xy lint init` has no flags and no non-interactive mode. It reads stdin via readline for these prompts: first a 'Replace it with eslint.config.ts? (y/N)' confirmation, asked before anything is generated, so there is no diff to review at that point. Then one y/N prompt per hard-coded barrel: @xylabs/sdk-js, @xyo-network/sdk-js, @xyo-network/xl1-sdk and @xyo-network/chain-sdk, plus @xylabs/sdk-react, @xyo-network/react-chain and @xyo-network/react-sdk for React repos. @ariestools/sdk is not among them. If an accepted barrel is not installed, init adds it to devDependencies at `latest` and runs `pnpm install`. findings.title: Lint execution modes and performance controls are missing, though SKILL.md sends 'lint performance' questions here
findings.current: absent (SKILL.md:38 routes "diagnosing lint performance" to eslint.md; the Commands table eslint.md:115-124 has no --mode/--profile/--jobs)
findings.truth: `xy lint --mode` takes package-workers (the default: persistent worker pool), shared-typecheck (experimental: shared TypeScript ingestion, semantic phase runs without the ESLint cache) and workspace-eslint (direct workspace ESLint CLI; a package target delegates to that package's lint script). The hidden `--next`/`--prev` flags are deprecated aliases. `-p/--profile` prints per-package config/lint/spawn timings, and `-j/--jobs` caps parallelism. `XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB` (default 2048) sets the RSS budget at which a worker is recycled. Workers are recycled to prevent out-of-memory failures on large monorepos.
findings.evidence: `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs lint --help` (shows --mode choices, --profile, --jobs); toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lintMode.ts:1-9; src/xy/lint/lint/runCommand.ts:43-60; `xy.mjs --stability --json` experimentalConfig {id:'lint.mode.shared-typecheck'}; src/xy/stability.ts:158-160; docs/STABILITY.md:61; packages/toolchain/README.md:240-266; src/actions/lintNextWorker.ts:381-382; commit bc8e52802 (2026-09-25).
findings.recommendation: In eslint.md, add a short 'Performance' note. `xy lint --mode package-workers|shared-typecheck|workspace-eslint`: package-workers is the default, shared-typecheck is experimental and its semantic phase skips the ESLint cache, and workspace-eslint is the direct ESLint CLI. Use --mode and not the deprecated --next/--prev. Cross-reference the global `--profile` and `--jobs` flags in commands.md rather than duplicating them. Mention XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB only as an undocumented worker-recycling budget (default 2048 MB) for memory-bound runners, or leave it out until the toolchain documents it.

findings.title: All-workspace xy lint runs incrementally by default and can lint nothing; the troubleshooting section does not say so
findings.current: eslint.md:132 "If no files are linted, verify workspace discovery, source globs, meta-package handling, and `--skip-empty`."
findings.truth: runCommand passes `incremental: argv.incremental !== false`, so incremental mode is on unless disabled. When no package is given and neither --fix nor --analyze is set, `xy lint` lints only the workspaces changed since the last clean snapshot. If none changed it prints 'No changed packages to lint.' and exits 0. `--no-incremental`, or `--fresh` (which clears the snapshot), forces a full run. Other relevant flags: `--meta full|skip` (default full), `--no-skip-empty`, and `-c/--no-cache`.

findings.recommendation: In eslint.md Commands/troubleshooting, add the following. An all-workspace `xy lint` with no package, no --fix and no --analyze is incremental by default and lints only workspaces changed since the last fully clean run. 'No changed packages to lint.' means nothing changed since then. `--no-incremental` forces a full run. Also list `--meta full|skip` (default full), `--no-skip-empty` and `--no-cache`. Fix commands.md:27 so `--no-incremental` covers lint as well as compile/build.

The skill's troubleshooting line (eslint.md:132) does not mention incremental selection. Its only --no-incremental guidance (commands.md:27, toolchain.md:108) is framed as compile/build only.
verify.skill: adjusted: The facts are accurate. runCommand.ts:124 passes `incremental: argv.incremental !== false`. lint.ts:94-98 uses incremental only when there is no package and no --fix/--analyze. lint.ts:146-157 prints 'No changed packages to lint.' and returns 0. The practical risk is smaller than 'can lint nothing' suggests. The lint snapshot is written only on a fully clean result with zero errors and zero warnings (lint.ts:173-182, result.ts:53-55 isCleanResult), and root config changes force a full plan (incremental.ts:466 'root configuration changed'). findings.title: Per-platform type handling is described too vaguely, and a Node package without compile.node fails declaration emit
findings.current: typescript.md:82 "Keep browser and neutral packages free of Node types unless the source genuinely requires them. The compiler resolves platform-specific types when producing browser, neutral, and node targets." The Node types section (typescript.md:64-80) tells agents to add `types: ["node"]` but never says the node target must be opted into.
findings.truth: For each target, `xy compile` writes its own check and declaration tsconfig at `build/tsconfig.package-{check|dts}-<platform>-<src>.json`, and that config extends the package tsconfig. The browser and neutral passes remove `node` from `types`. When `types` is unset, those two passes get `types: []`. Only the node pass keeps the declared types. The browser pass also forces `moduleResolution: 'Bundler'` and `customConditions: ['browser']`. The node pass uses `customConditions: ['node']`. Each pass sets `module` (ESNext for browser, NodeNext for node) only when the package's own tsconfig.json omits `module`. Neutral is the only target built unless another target is opted in. So a package with `types: ["node"]` and no `compile.node: true` builds only the neutral declaration pass, which has no Node types. That pass fails with "Compile:Declaration emit had N errors" even though raw `tsc` passes. A package tsconfig that sets `module: NodeNext` and also emits a browser target gets NodeNext with Bundler resolution, which TS rejects (TS5095).
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 (`platform === 'node' ? [...userTypes] : userTypes.filter(type => type !== 'node')`, `undefined` → `[]` for non-node); spec/actions/resolvePlatformTypes.spec.ts:32-47; createTypescriptConfig.ts:45-61 (default module only when the package's own tsconfig omits it), 75-97 (Bundler + browser condition, node condition), 135-151 (generated file path under build/); packageCompileEsbuild.ts:304-310 (per-platform check), 360-370 (per-platform dts emit via tsc); resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:63-96 (neutral is built only when nothing else is enabled; enabling one target turns the others off); typescript 6.0.3 lib/typescript.js:129880-129882 (TS5095 for bundler with a non-ESM module).
findings.recommendation: Replace the typescript.md:82 paragraph with a short 'Per-target type passes' note. (1) The browser and neutral passes always drop `node` from `types` (and use `types: []` when unset), so Node globals and `node:` modules exist only in the node pass. (2) A Node package must pair `types: ["node"]` with `compile.node: true` in xy.config.ts. Otherwise only the neutral target builds, and declaration emit fails even though raw tsc passes. Link compilation.md#target-selection and the Node library row in project-profiles.md. (3) Do not set `module` in a package tsconfig that emits a browser target. Browser passes always use `moduleResolution: Bundler` and set `module: ESNext` only when the package tsconfig omits `module`, so an explicit `module: NodeNext` triggers TS5095. (4) When declaration emit fails but validation passes, inspect `build/tsconfig.package-dts-<platform>-<src>.json`.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue is real and unchanged in 10.1.1. `git diff 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91` touches only XyConfig.ts in the compile directory. Verified in code: resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 keeps the user's `types` only for node, removes 'node' for browser and neutral, and turns unset into [] (spec resolvePlatformTypes.spec.ts:32-47). resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:72-96 builds neutral only when no target is enabled. packageCompileEsbuild.ts:401-411 and 470-475: by default the full-package validation runs against the package's own tsconfig, which still has node types, so it passes and the per-folder check is skipped. The neutral dts pass (createDeclarationEmitter, 360-370) then fails at compileFolder:313-317 with 'Compile:Declaration emit had N errors'. TS5095 is confirmed in typescript 6.0.3 lib/typescript.js:129881-129882 (diag at :10387): Bundler requires a non-node ESM module kind, and NodeNext also trips TS5110 on the next branch. Two details in the recommended text are inaccurate. (a) createTypescriptConfig.ts:80-85 always forces `moduleResolution: 'Bundler'` in the browser pass. Only `module` is conditional: readRootTsconfigModule reads the package's own tsconfig.json and not the extends chain (45-61). So 'switches to ESNext/Bundler only when the package inherits them' is wrong, and setting `module: ESNext` is fine (sdk-js packages/sdk does it). (b) 'Node globals are never visible … whatever types says' overstates the code, which only filters the literal 'node' entry from `types`. A `/// <reference types="node" />` still pulls the globals in. Medium severity stands: compilation.md:31-53 documents target opt-in, so following the skill does not fail outright.
verify.skill: adjusted: The mechanism checks out on 10.1.1. resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 removes 'node' from the neutral and browser passes and maps unset types to []. resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:72-96 builds only neutral by default. Under default settings validateFullPackage passes, because it uses the package tsconfig with types:["node"]. shouldRunFolderChecks is false when full validation runs (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:405-409), so the neutral dts emit is where it fails, with 'Compile:Declaration emit had N errors' (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:314-318). A package that sets `module: ESNext` and emits a node target is likewise at risk from the inherited NodeNext resolution. typescript.md:115 already warns against resetting module resolution in general. Medium severity stands: following typescript.md alone for a Node package makes `xy compile` fail.

findings.title: The `include: ["src"]` examples shrink xy compile's full-package validation and contradict the toolchain templates
findings.current: typescript.md:46-51, 55-60, 72-79 and 94-101 all show `"include": ["src"]`. Meanwhile typescript.md:117 says to "keep `tsconfig.json` broad for validation", and typescript.md:123 says "full-package validation includes non-emitted TypeScript files by design."
findings.truth: The validation pass is not independent of the package tsconfig. It takes the file list the package tsconfig.json produces (excluding nested `packages/`), forces noEmit, and writes `build/tsconfig.package-validate.json`. With `include: ["src"]`, package-root `xy.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `eslint.config.ts` and `.storybook/` are never validated. The toolchain's own repo-init templates and the @ariestools consumer repos use exclude-only configs instead. Emission inputs come from a separate derivation: `src/**/*` minus spec, stories and example files. A package with no tsconfig.json skips validation and only prints a warning.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/validateFullPackage.ts:30-66 (files = parsed.fileNames of the package tsconfig), 72-76 ("Compile:Validate skipped — tsconfig.json not found"); createTypescriptConfig.ts:123-131 (emission excludes *.spec.*, *.stories.*, *.example.*, spec/**, stories/**); templates/repo/cli/package/tsconfig.json.tmpl (`{"exclude": ["dist"], "extends": "{{tsconfigPackage}}"}`); templates/repo/cli/root/tsconfig.json.tmpl (exclude list only); sdk-js/tsconfig.json, sdk-js/packages/crypto/tsconfig.json, actor-kit/cli-kit/browser-kit tsconfig.json (exclude-only or include ["**/*"]); papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md:263 (validation covers "src, specs, stories, configs, Storybook").
findings.recommendation: Change the basic, React, Node and lib-neutral examples to the template shape, e.g. `{ "extends": "@ariestools/tsconfig", "exclude": ["dist"] }` (root: `"exclude": ["dist", "docs", "**/dist", "**/docs", "coverage", "**/coverage"]`). Add one sentence: narrowing `include` to `src` removes root configs and Storybook from `xy compile` validation; emission inputs are derived from `src` automatically. Also note that every package needs its own tsconfig.json, because validation is skipped without one.

verify.code: confirmed: Verified in code, and unchanged in 10.1.1. validateFullPackage.ts:30-66 takes `parsed.fileNames` of the package tsconfig.json, filters out nested `packages/`, and writes build/tsconfig.package-validate.json with noEmit. So `include: ["src"]` drops package-root xy.config.ts, vitest/eslint configs and .storybook from validation. That contradicts typescript.md:117 and :123, compilation.md:82 and YELLOW-PAPER.md:262. validateFullPackage.ts:72-76 confirms the missing-tsconfig skip warning. createTypescriptConfig.ts:123-131 derives emission from `src/**/*` minus spec, stories and example files. Templates templates/repo/cli/package/tsconfig.json.tmpl (`exclude: ["dist"]`) and root/tsconfig.json.tmpl are exclude-only. The consumer repos sdk-js, sdk-js/packages/crypto and actor-kit/cli-kit/browser-kit use exclude-only configs or `include: ["**/*"]`. The package must declare its own `exclude`: the base exclude list (packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:28) is resolved relative to the base config's location, so it does not cover the package. Minor nit: the root template's exclude also lists ".yarn". The scaffold also still emits a legacy templates/repo/cli/package/tsconfig.build.json with `include: ["src"]`, but xy compile does not use it.
verify.skill: confirmed: The skill shows `"include": ["src"]` at typescript.md:46-51, 55-60, 72-79 and 94-101. It also says at typescript.md:117 and 123, and at compilation.md:82, that validation covers specs, stories, configs and Storybook. validateFullPackage.ts:30-66 validates exactly `parsed.fileNames` of the package tsconfig.json, minus nested packages/. findings.title: No guidance on TypeScript 7: typescript must stay at major 6 or below, and the native compiler is an experimental side-by-side alias
findings.current: typescript.md:25 "Use TypeScript 5.9 or 6 with the current toolchain. Follow the consuming repository's exact range policy." Nothing about TypeScript 7, `typescript-native` or `compile.compiler`, and no skill file mentions them.
findings.truth: The peer range is `typescript: ^5.9 || ^6.0`. `xy updo` will not offer a bump past major 6, even with `--latest`, because TypeScript 7 is the Go compiler and exports none of the compiler API that ESLint, deplint, dead and api-exposure load from `typescript`. TS 7 can only be installed alongside, as `"typescript-native": "npm:typescript@~7.0.2"`, with `compile.compiler: 'native'`. That is enabled by the experimental `xyex enable ts-native`, and it does not work with `compile.validator: 'shared'`. deplint keeps the alias even though nothing imports it. The stability catalog says public examples must not require the native compiler. This shipped 2026-08-10 and is in 10.1.0.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/package.json:99-100 (dev `typescript ~6.0.3`, `typescript-native npm:typescript@~7.0.2`), 106-108 (peer `^5.9 || ^6.0`); src/lib/updo/majorCeiling.ts:16-28; src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:142-157, 171-177; src/actions/package/compile/resolveTscBin.ts:5-34; src/actions/deplint/rules.md:219; docs/STABILITY.md:59, 98-99; `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs --stability --json` → experimentalConfig `compile.compiler.native`: "TypeScript 7 (Go) compiler. Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`. This repo may dogfood it; public examples must not require it."; `xyex enable --help` lists `ts-native`; git log c2b9db449 2026-08-10 "feat(toolchain): optional native TypeScript compiler".
findings.recommendation: Pin TypeScript in every install command in typescript.md:16-22, and also in toolchain.md:44, e.g. `pnpm add -D @ariestools/tsconfig typescript@~6.0`. npm's `latest` for typescript is now 7.x, and the repo-init template uses `typescript ~6.0.3`. Extend line 25: keep the `typescript` dependency within the toolchain peer `^5.9 || ^6.0` and never upgrade it to 7. TypeScript 7 is the Go compiler and exports no compiler API, and ESLint, deplint and `xy compile` validation load it from `typescript`; `xy updo` caps it at major 6. The TS 7 compiler is optional and experimental. `pnpm xyex enable ts-native` installs it side by side as `typescript-native` and sets `compile.compiler: 'native'`. It is incompatible with `compile.validator: 'shared'`, and shared examples must not require it. Link compilation.md for the compile fields.

verify.code: adjusted: All stated facts check out in 10.1.1. Peer `typescript: ^5.9 || ^6.0` and dev `typescript-native npm:typescript@~7.0.2` are at packages/toolchain/package.json:99-108. majorCeiling.ts:16-38 caps updo at major 6, and is still used in resolveVersions.ts:278. XyConfig.ts:142-157 and 171-177 cover compiler/nativePackage. compile.ts:348-352 downgrades shared to per-package under native. deplint rules.md:219 is confirmed. `xy --stability --json` reports compile.compiler.native as 'Enable with `xyex enable ts-native` … public examples must not require it'. `xyex enable --help` lists ts-native. The feature shipped in c2b9db449 (2026-08-10), first tagged v10.0.0. However the severity is understated. `npm view typescript dist-tags` shows `latest: '7.0.2'`. TS 7's root export is only './lib/version.cjs' (`npm view typescript@7.0.2 exports`), so there is no compiler API. That means the skill's own unpinned install commands at typescript.md:16, 19 and 22 (`pnpm add -D … typescript`) install TypeScript 7 today. That violates the peer range and breaks ESLint, deplint and the toolchain's `import ts from 'typescript'` (e.g. resolvePlatformTypes.ts:5, validateFullPackage.ts:5). `xy updo` will not repair it, because majorCeilingFor (majorCeiling.ts:35-38) leaves declarations already above the ceiling alone. The repo-init templates pin `typescript ~6.0.3` (templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:48, package/package.json.tmpl:53).

findings.title: The `types` explanation assumes TS 5.9 auto-inclusion; on TS 6 `types` defaults to []
findings.current: typescript.md:66 "The base is not a license to expose Node globals everywhere." typescript.md:104 "Setting `compilerOptions.types` disables automatic `@types/*` inclusion."
findings.truth: TypeScript 6 is the toolchain's dev compiler and the one repo-init installs. On TS 6, automatic type directives are `options.types ?? []`, and `@types/*` packages are discovered only when `types` contains "*". So on TS 6 the base config exposes no Node, Vitest or other `@types` globals unless they are listed. Setting `types` disables auto-inclusion only on TS 5.9.

[]`), 21973-21975 (`usesWildcardTypes` = types includes "*"); toolchain packages/toolchain/package.json:99 (`typescript ~6.0.3`); templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:48 (`typescript ~6.0.3`).
findings.recommendation: Reword only typescript.md:104. On TS 5.9, setting `compilerOptions.types` turns off automatic `@types/*` inclusion. On TS 6, nothing from `@types/*` is included unless `types` lists it (or contains "*"). Either way, list Node, test-global and lib-neutral types explicitly. Optionally add to the Troubleshooting sentence at line 123 that on TS 6 a missing `process` or `Buffer` usually means `types` was never declared. Leave line 66 unchanged.

On TS 6, therefore, nothing from @types is auto-included unless listed, and 'setting types disables auto-inclusion' (typescript.md:104) is only meaningful on 5.9. The toolchain dev compiler is ~6.0.3 (packages/toolchain/package.json:99), and both repo-init templates pin ~6.0.3 (root/package.json.tmpl:48, package/package.json.tmpl:53). findings.title: The experimental `xyex tsc-validate` type-check-only command is not mentioned anywhere
findings.current: absent. typescript.md:40 and 117 talk about separating validation from emission but name no type-check-only command. compilation.md:89-91 covers `compile.validator: 'shared'` and `--validator shared` only. A grep of skills/ finds no `tsc-validate`.
findings.truth: `xyex tsc-validate [package]` type-checks all workspaces in one process with a shared source-file cache. It respects `compile.validate: false` and skips packages without a tsconfig. It is the same engine as `compile.validator: 'shared'`, is catalogued as experimental, and does not work with the native compiler. The stable path is still `xy compile`, whose validation pass runs before emit.

It is experimental, respects `compile.validate: false`, skips packages without a tsconfig.json, and is incompatible with `compile.compiler: 'native'`. findings.title: Workspace-scoped test runs (`xy test @scope/package`, `xy retest @scope/package`, vitest 'in the correct package') skip the root @ariestools/vitest-config preset
findings.current: testing.md:171-177 "Use the toolchain for all tests, one workspace, or one file/folder path: ... pnpm xy test @scope/package"; testing.md:182-183 "pnpm xy retest @scope/package"; testing.md:186 "invoke the installed Vitest through the package manager in the correct package". The same file recommends one root preset config for monorepos (testing.md:25, 98).
findings.truth: When the target is a workspace, `xy test` and `xy retest` run `pnpm --filter <name> exec run-or-exec vitest .` (retest runs `--clearCache` first), so Vitest starts in the package directory. Vitest 5.0.3 looks for a config file only in cwd/--root and does not search upward. The root preset config is therefore never loaded. That means no `browser` project, no spec/node and spec/browser routing (spec/browser specs run in plain Node), no `watch: false`, no `**/.claude/**` exclude, and no root-level setup such as sdk-js's dotenv load; Vitest's default include applies instead. Running `pnpm exec vitest` inside a package directory has the same effect. A path target that exactly matches a workspace location (e.g. `packages/foo`) also resolves as a workspace and goes down this route. The org repos that use the preset (sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit) have no package-level vitest config, and sdk-js, actor-kit and browser-kit have spec/browser directories.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/test.ts:10-11 (`pm.runInWorkspace(target, 'vitest', ['.'])`); actions/retest.ts:10-14; pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:180-188 (`['pnpm', ['--filter', resolved, 'exec', 'run-or-exec', script, ...args]]`); lib/runOrExecPlan.ts:12-17 (no local `vitest` script -> exec `vitest .`); pm/resolveWorkspace.ts:10-14 (matches name, then exact location) and pnpmPackageManager.ts:112 (location is the relative dir). Vitest 5.0.3 node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DpLw24bj.js:14267-14275 `findConfigFile(root)` checks only `resolve(root, configFile)` and returns false otherwise; :14823-14836 resolveConfigPath is called with `resolve(options.root || process.cwd())` (this is the `resolveConfig` the CLI imports at cli-api.C4x4GGip.js:3,26). `find ariestools/{sdk-js,sdk-react,actor-kit,browser-kit,cli-kit}/packages -maxdepth 2 -name 'vitest.config.*'` returns 0 in every repo; spec/browser dir count: sdk-js 2, actor-kit 1, browser-kit 2.
findings.recommendation: In 'Running tests', state that with a root preset, scoped runs must start from the directory that holds vitest.config.ts (the repo root). Use a path that is not exactly a workspace location, e.g. `pnpm xy test packages/example/src`, or run `pnpm exec vitest run packages/example/` from the root, adding `--project node` or `--project browser` when needed. Change 'in the correct package' to 'from the directory containing vitest.config.ts (the repo root under the preset)'. Keep `pnpm xy test @scope/package` / `xy retest @scope/package` only with a caveat: they run Vitest inside the package and use only a package-level vitest config. Optionally raise a toolchain issue to make workspace-mode test and retest pass `--root`/`--config` or run from the root with a path filter.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived at 10.1.1, where none of these paths changed since 7eb43c3c2. actions/test.ts:10-11 and retest.ts:10-14 call pm.runInWorkspace(target,'vitest',['.']) whenever findWorkspace(target) matches. pnpmPackageManager.ts:185-187 runs `pnpm --filter <name> exec run-or-exec vitest .`, so Vitest starts in the package directory. resolveWorkspace.ts:10-14 matches the name, then the exact location, then the short name, so `packages/foo` also resolves as a workspace. In Vitest 5.0.3, index.DpLw24bj.js:14267-14275 (findConfigFile only checks resolve(root, file) and returns false otherwise) and :14823-14836 (root = options.root || cwd) mean the root config is never found. None of sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit or cli-kit has a package-level vitest.config (find returns 0 in each). sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/spec/browser/readResponseText.spec.ts calls document.createElement, so `pnpm xy test @ariestools/sdk` would run it in plain Node and fail. Severity high is justified.
verify.skill: confirmed: Still true at 10.1.1. In toolchain, actions/test.ts:10-11 and retest.ts:10-14 did not change between 7eb43c3c2 and 812b27a91. findings.title: `xy test`/`xy retest` defer to a same-named root script, even with a target; this interacts badly with the suggested `"test": "vitest run"`

With the skill's suggested root script `vitest run`, `pnpm xy test @scope/package` becomes `vitest run @scope/package`, a filename filter that matches no files, and Vitest exits 1. The scaffold uses `"test": "xy test"`, which avoids this via the XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT recursion guard. Current ariestools repos (sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit, toolchain) define no root `test` script and rely on `pnpm xy test`.

findings.truth: Since 8.2.0 (b86f3a024, 2026-08-27, "bounded cancellable response reads"), fetchJson, FetchClient and FetchJsonClient accept `maxResponseBytes` (validated positive safe integer), a caller `signal` that stays active through body consumption, and a client `timeout` composed with that signal. The module also exports `readResponseText` and `ReadResponseTextOptions`. 9.0.1 (158476cd7) adds a fallback to response.text() for bodies that are not streams when a signal or byte cap is set. These are the main safety controls for untrusted HTTP responses, and an agent routed by SKILL.md:32 would not know they exist.

findings.title: zod is not really optional: the root barrel and the /hex, /object and /zod subpaths load zod at runtime
findings.current: overview.md:40 "`zod` | **Optional peer** — install only if you use zod helpers (`@ariestools/sdk/zod`, hex zod helpers, etc.)"; overview.md:44-45 "# Only if you use zod helpers from the SDK / pnpm add zod"; overview.md:22-25 shows the root-barrel import `import { assertEx, delay, exists, fetchJson } from '@ariestools/sdk'` as the default with no zod caveat.
findings.truth: zod is declared as an optional peer (`^4.6`), but the root barrel (node, browser and neutral builds), `@ariestools/sdk/hex`, `@ariestools/sdk/object` and `@ariestools/sdk/zod` all import `zod/mini` or `zod/v4/core` at the top level. Without zod, `import ... from '@ariestools/sdk'` fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, even for assertEx or fetchJson. Zod-free subpaths such as /assert, /delay, /exists and /fetch load fine. The version must be zod v4 (`^4.6`), because the code uses the `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core` entry points. Downstream, `@ariestools/pixel` imports `@ariestools/sdk/object` at runtime but does not declare zod. `@ariestools/express` declares `zod ^4.6` as a required (non-optional) peer. The upstream umbrella README:234 makes the same wrong 'optional' claim.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json:403-411 (peerDependencies zod ^4.6, peerDependenciesMeta zod optional); package.json:401 devDep zod ~4.6.5. Runtime imports: packages/sdk/src/modules/hex/hex/hex.ts:1 `import * as z from 'zod/mini'` (used by `export const HexZod = z.pipe(...)` at :11), hex/address/address.ts:1, hex/hash/hash.ts:1, hex/zod.ts:1, hex/ethAddress.ts:1, object/JsonObject.ts:1, zod/zodAsFactory.ts:1 (`zod/v4/core`). Root barrel src/index.ts:21,23,36 re-exports #hex, #object, #zod. Built output (dist built 2026-09-24 = published 9.0.1): `grep -n '^import' dist/neutral/index.mjs` shows `import * as z from "zod/mini"` at :988 and `zod/v4/core` at :3266, and the same holds for dist/node/index.mjs and dist/browser/index.mjs. Simulation with a resolve hook that makes 'zod*' unresolvable (node 26.9.0): FAIL dist/node/index.mjs, dist/browser/index.mjs, dist/neutral/index.mjs, hex.mjs, object.mjs and zod.mjs (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND 'zod/mini'); OK for assert.mjs, fetch.mjs, delay.mjs and exists.mjs. pixel/src/XyUserEventHandler.ts:1 `import { type EmptyObject, toSafeJsonObject } from '@ariestools/sdk/object'` → pixel/dist/browser/index.mjs:514; pixel/package.json has no zod. express/package.json peers {winston-transport ^4.9, zod ^4.6}, with no peerDependenciesMeta.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the zod row: "`zod` (^4.6, v4 only) — declared optional, but **required at runtime** for the root barrel `@ariestools/sdk` and the `/hex`, `/object` and `/zod` subpaths (and, transitively, for `@ariestools/pixel`; `@ariestools/express` lists it as a required peer). Skip it only if you import zod-free subpaths exclusively (e.g. `/assert`, `/delay`, `/exists`, `/fetch`)." Change the snippet to `pnpm add @ariestools/sdk zod@^4.6` as the default install. Add a note under the root-barrel example (lines 22-29) that the root barrel needs both `zod` and `@opentelemetry/api` installed, and that subpath imports avoid both. Optionally file an sdk-js issue to fix packages/sdk/README.md:234 and pixel's undeclared zod.

findings.title: zod is a hard runtime import of /hex, /object and the root barrel, not an optional extra
findings.current: modules.md:41 "`hex` | `@ariestools/sdk/hex` | Hex strings, hashes, address helpers, optional zod"; modules.md:56 "`zod` | ... | Zod helpers — requires optional peer `zod`"; the install section at modules.md:7-16 says nothing about peers.
findings.truth: Core hex code imports `zod/mini` at module load, so zod is needed for any hex import, not only the zod helpers. The `object` module does the same through JsonObject. The root barrel re-exports both. Without `zod` installed, `@ariestools/sdk/hex`, `@ariestools/sdk/object`, `@ariestools/sdk/zod` and `@ariestools/sdk` all fail to load. Because zod is declared as an optional peer, pnpm does not install it automatically. The imports are `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core`, so zod 4 (^4.6) is required. The root barrel also loads `@ariestools/telemetry`, which needs the required peer `@opentelemetry/api`.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/hex/hex/hex.ts:1, hex/address/address.ts:1, hex/hash/hash.ts:1, hex/ethAddress.ts:1, hex/zod.ts:1 and object/JsonObject.ts:1 each have `import * as z from 'zod/mini'`.
