findings.recommendation: Change the hex row to "Hex/hash/address/EthAddress helpers. Requires peer `zod` ^4.6 (imports `zod/mini` at load)". Change the zod row to "Zod factories (`zodIsFactory`, `zodAsFactory`, `zodToFactory`, …). Requires peer `zod` ^4.6". Note on the object row that it also needs zod (JsonObject guards). Under "Install and import", add that `pnpm add zod` is required when importing `/hex`, `/object`, `/zod` or the root barrel, and that the root barrel also needs `@opentelemetry/api`. findings.title: The retry example hides that retry ignores thrown errors and does not retry by default
findings.current: modules.md:72-80 ("Delay and retry"): `await retry(async () => doWork(), { /* options per package API */ })`. The table row at modules.md:47 says only "Retry helpers".
findings.truth: `retry(func, config?)` has no try/catch, so a thrown error propagates on the first attempt and is never retried. It retries only while `complete(result)` is false; the default check is `result !== undefined`. Defaults are `retries = 0` (no retries), `interval = 100` ms and `backoff = 2`. When everything is exhausted it returns `undefined` rather than throwing. As written, the `doWork()` example (void result) is never "complete": with `retries: N` it runs N+1 times even on success and returns undefined.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/retry/retry.ts:5-18 (RetryConfig: backoff, interval, retries; RetryConfigWithComplete: complete), :26-41 (`const result = await func()` with no try/catch at :30; defaults at :28; `return undefined` when retries <= 0). src/spec/retry/retry.spec.ts covers only undefined/complete cases, with no throw case.
findings.recommendation: Replace the placeholder with a concrete example: `const value = await retry(() => fetchMaybe(), { retries: 3, interval: 100, backoff: 2, complete: v => v !== undefined })`. Add a note that retry re-runs on an incomplete/undefined result, not on exceptions, so the function should catch and return undefined to trigger a retry. Also note that the default is 0 retries and that exhaustion returns `undefined`.

verify.code: confirmed: src/modules/retry/retry.ts:26-41 calls `const result = await func()` (line 30) with no try/catch, so a throw propagates on the first attempt. The defaults at :28 are complete = value !== undefined, retries = 0, interval = 100 and backoff = 2. :34-35 return undefined once retries are exhausted. The JSDoc at :10 also says 'Defaults to 0 (no retries)'. src/spec/retry/retry.spec.ts has five cases, all about undefined results or a complete predicate, and none for throwing. The placeholder at modules.md:79 hides behavior that differs from the usual retry-on-throw expectation.
verify.skill: confirmed: retry.ts:26-41 has no try/catch, so `const result = await func()` at :30 lets an exception propagate on the first attempt. The defaults at :28 are complete = value !== undefined, retries = 0, interval = 100 and backoff = 2. When retries are exhausted it returns undefined (:34-35). The skill's example at modules.md:79 is a placeholder, and the row at :47 says only 'Retry helpers', so an agent will likely assume retry-on-throw semantics, which is wrong. A void doWork() is never 'complete'. retry.spec.ts has no throw case. Medium is proportionate, and the recommended example and note are accurate.

findings.title: assertEx pattern needs the falsy-value and function-argument caveats
findings.current: modules.md:27 "`assertEx`, `assertDefinedEx` — throw on invalid state"; modules.md:68 `const value = assertEx(maybe, () => 'missing value')`
findings.truth: `assertEx` throws on any falsy value (undefined, null, false, 0, '', 0n). `assertDefinedEx` throws only on `undefined`. For both, the second argument must be a function that returns a message or an Error. Passing a string throws "Invalid assertEx usage: second argument must be a function or undefined".
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/assert/assertEx.ts:50 (falsy checks) and :55-57 (non-function argument throws); assert/assertDefinedEx.ts:51 (`if (expr !== undefined) return expr`) and :56-58.
findings.recommendation: Add one line after the Assert example: use `assertDefinedEx` when 0, '' or false are valid values, and always pass a function (`() => 'msg'` or `() => new MyError()`), never a string.

verify.code: confirmed: assert/assertEx.ts:50 returns expr only when it is not undefined, null, false, 0, '' or 0n, so it throws on any falsy value. assertDefinedEx.ts:51 passes anything that is not undefined. Both throw 'Invalid … usage: second argument must be a function or undefined' when the second argument is not a function (assertEx.ts:55-57, assertDefinedEx.ts:56-58). findings.title: Forget section lacks the API and its timeout semantics
findings.current: modules.md:82-84: prose only ("Use forget helpers when intentionally not awaiting a promise…"), with no import or config.
findings.truth: Usage is `forget(promise, { name, timeout, onCancel, onComplete, onException })`. The default `timeout` is 30 000 ms, and on expiry it only calls `onCancel` and the timeout handler; the underlying work keeps running. `ForgetPromise.activeForgets` and `ForgetPromise.awaitInactive(interval, timeout)` let tests and shutdown paths drain pending forgets. Global defaults can be set via `globalThis.xy.forget.config`.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/forget/ForgetConfig.ts:5-24 (fields) and :27 (`defaultForgetConfig = { timeout: 30_000 }`); forget/forget.ts:6-10 ("Timeouts notify via `onCancel` but do not stop the underlying work"); forget/ForgetPromise.ts:26,33,45 (activeForgets, active, awaitInactive); forget/ForgetPromiseNode.ts:28-30 (globalThis.xy?.forget?.config merge).
findings.recommendation: Add `import { forget, ForgetPromise } from '@ariestools/sdk/forget'; forget(sendMetrics(), { name: 'metrics', onComplete: ([, error]) => { if (error) logger.warn(error) } })`. Note that rejections are logged and reported through `onComplete`, and that `onException` fires only for synchronous setup errors. Note that the default `timeout` (30s) only notifies (onCancel plus an error log) and does not cancel the work. Note that `await ForgetPromise.awaitInactive()` should run before process exit or in test teardown, and that global defaults can be set via `globalThis.xy.forget.config`.

verify.code: adjusted: The gap is real. ForgetConfig.ts:5-19 has name, onCancel, onComplete, onException and timeout, and :22 sets defaultForgetConfig = { timeout: 30_000 }. The ForgetPromise.ts timeout race (lines ~103-113) only calls onCancel and timeoutHandler and does not cancel the work. activeForgets (:26), active (:33) and awaitInactive(interval = 100, timeout?) (:45) exist. ForgetPromise.forget and ForgetPromiseNode.forget (:28-30) both merge globalThis.xy?.forget?.config. But the recommended example is wrong. onException does not fire when the forgotten promise rejects. A rejection is caught in promiseWrapper, logged through ForgetPromise.logger (console by default) and passed to `onComplete([undefined, error])`. onException is called only from the outer catch, around setup code that rarely throws, so `onException: e => logger.warn(e)` would never see a failed sendMetrics(). Note too that a promisable function passed in is invoked outside that try, so a synchronous throw reaches the caller.

findings.recommendation: In packages.md under `@ariestools/crypto-auth`, add a 2–3 line summary. findings.title: Auth-wrapping fetcher example spreads a Headers instance and silently drops every SDK header, including Content-Encoding: gzip
findings.current: fetch.md:39-40: `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) =>\n  globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers: { ...init?.headers, authorization: token } })`
findings.truth: fetchJson and FetchClient always pass a `Headers` instance to the fetcher: fetchJson.ts:40 and FetchClient.ts:174 use `buildHeaders()`, which returns `new Headers()` (fetchJson.ts:9-20, FetchClient.ts:60-71), and fetchCompress.ts:58-63 builds `new Headers(init.headers)` when it compresses. A Headers object has no own enumerable properties, so `{ ...init?.headers }` is `{}`. The wrapped request then loses Accept, Content-Type: application/json and, for gzip-compressed bodies (default for bodies over 1024 chars), Content-Encoding: gzip. The server receives gzip bytes with no encoding header.
findings.evidence: `node -e` on Node v26.9.0: spreading `new Headers({Accept,'Content-Type','Content-Encoding':'gzip'})` into `{...h, authorization:'tok'}` printed `{"authorization":"tok"}`. Rebuilding with `new Headers(init.headers); headers.set('authorization', ...)` kept all four headers. Source: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:9-20,38-41; FetchClient.ts:60-71,171-182; fetchCompress.ts:49,55-68. Test fetchJson.spec.ts:105 casts `call[1]?.headers as Headers`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with a version that keeps the existing headers: `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) => { const headers = new Headers(init?.headers); headers.set('authorization', token); return globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers }) }`. Add one sentence: init.headers reaching a fetcher is a `Headers` instance, so never object-spread it. For auth that does not need transport control, prefer client-level `headers` config.

verify.code: confirmed: I re-derived this from sdk-js v9.0.1 (HEAD 298fbb5bb, `git describe` = v9.0.1). fetchJson.ts:9-20 and FetchClient.ts:60-71 `buildHeaders()` return `new Headers()`, which is passed as init.headers at fetchJson.ts:40 and FetchClient.ts:174. The gzip path also passes a Headers instance (fetchCompress.ts:58-63), and the injected fetcher receives that init (fetchCompress.ts:50,60,68). On Node v26.9.0, `{...new Headers({Accept,'Content-Type','Content-Encoding':'gzip'}), authorization:'tok'}` printed `{"authorization":"tok"}`. Rebuilding with `new Headers(init.headers)` plus `.set()` kept all four headers. Following the example at fetch.md:39-40 therefore drops Accept, Content-Type: application/json and Content-Encoding: gzip. Bodies over 1024 chars are gzip-compressed by default (fetchCompress.ts:49), so the server gets gzip bytes it cannot decode. High is justified because it is a silent wrong request.
verify.skill: confirmed: The skill does contain the bad example at skills/ariestools-sdk/fetch.md:39-40, `{ ...init, headers: { ...init?.headers, authorization: token } }`. In the SDK source the fetcher always receives a Headers instance. fetchJson.ts:40 and FetchClient.ts:174 pass buildHeaders(), which returns `new Headers()` (fetchJson.ts:9-20, FetchClient.ts:60-71). fetchCompress.ts:58-68 then either forwards init unchanged or builds `new Headers(init.headers)` and sets Content-Encoding: gzip, with compressMinLength defaulting to 1024 at :49. I reproduced the loss on Node v26.9.0: `{...new Headers({Accept,'Content-Type','Content-Encoding':'gzip'}), authorization:'tok'}` gives `{"authorization":"tok"}`, while `new Headers(h); h2.set(...)` keeps all four headers. Following the example therefore drops Accept and Content-Type on every request, and sends gzip bodies with no Content-Encoding header. That is a broken request, so high is right. The fix is correct. The client-level `headers` alternative also works because buildHeaders merges config headers, though per-request headers replace client headers (finding 5).

findings.title: HTTP-status semantics missing: fetchJson never throws on non-2xx, while FetchClient throws FetchClientError per validateStatus
findings.current: fetch.md:30 lists only `FetchError`, `isFetchError`, `toFetchError`, `classifyFetchError`. fetch.md:117 warns only about retries and caching. The file never says which entry points throw on HTTP error statuses.
findings.truth: fetchJson and the fetchJson* helpers resolve on 4xx/5xx with `status` set. `data` is the best-effort parsed body, or null when it is malformed. They throw FetchError only for transport, parse-on-success and policy failures. FetchClient, FetchJsonClient and fetchJsonClient throw `FetchClientError` (a FetchError subclass with type 'http-status', `.response` and `.config`) when `validateStatus` rejects the status. The default accepts 200-299. A custom function overrides it, and `validateStatus: null` never throws. FetchClientError is exported but not mentioned.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:43-45 (non-ok -> tryParseJson, no throw); parseJson.ts:60-82; FetchClient.ts:16-21,34-58,197-211; index.ts:2 exports FetchClientError. Tests: fetchJson.spec.ts:81-86 ('does not throw for a non-JSON error body (returns null)', status 500); FetchClient.spec.ts:264-307 (FetchClientError, validateStatus null and custom).
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Errors and HTTP status' subsection. Use fetchJson* when you want to branch on `status` yourself and check `status`/`response.ok`; it never throws for HTTP status. Use FetchClient/fetchJsonClient for Axios-style throw-on-non-2xx, catching `FetchClientError` (or `isFetchError(e) && e.type === 'http-status'`). Document `validateStatus` (function or null). Add `FetchClientError` to the list at line 30, and extend line 117 to: do not assume fetchJson throws on non-2xx.

FetchClient.ts:197-211 throws FetchClientError when validateStatus rejects the status. The default is 200-299; `null` disables the check and a function overrides it. FetchClientError is a FetchError with type 'http-status' plus .response and .config (FetchClient.ts:34-58). It is exported at index.ts:2. FetchJsonClient extends FetchClient (FetchJsonClient.ts:15). The tests agree: fetchJson.spec.ts:81-86 gives status 500 with data null and no throw, and FetchClient.spec.ts:264-307 covers FetchClientError, validateStatus null and a custom function. fetch.md:30 and :117 omit all of this. findings.title: Bounded, cancellable response reads (maxResponseBytes, timeout, signal, readResponseText) shipped in v8.2.0 but are absent
findings.current: absent. The file predates the feature: its only commit is 8a7d4f0 (2026-07-31).
findings.truth: Since sdk-js b86f3a024 (2026-08-27, first in v8.2.0, present in v9.0.1), fetchJson, FetchClient and FetchJsonClient accept `maxResponseBytes`. It must be a positive safe integer and is validated before any I/O (RangeError otherwise). It counts decoded stream bytes incrementally and applies to non-2xx bodies too. FetchClient also takes `timeout` (ms; 0 disables), which composes with the caller `signal` (first abort wins). The signal stays active through body consumption. Failures are FetchError with type 'response-too-large', 'aborted' or 'timeout'. When a cap or signal is set, non-2xx read errors propagate instead of becoming `data: null`, and `validateStatus: null` does not disable this. `readResponseText(response, { maxResponseBytes, signal })` is exported for text bodies, with `ReadResponseTextOptions` available from `@ariestools/sdk/fetch/model`. The README also notes the SDK adds no SSRF, redirect or credentials policy, so callers should set `redirect: 'error'` and `credentials: 'omit'` when required.

findings.title: Injected-fetcher contract missing: non-WHATWG bodies (node-fetch, cross-fetch, RN polyfills) fall back to buffered text() (v9.0.1 fix)
findings.current: fetch.md:32-45 ('Injecting a fetcher') only shows how to pass a FetchFunction. It says nothing about what the returned Response must support.
findings.truth: sdk-js 158476cd7 (2026-09-18, merged 2026-09-24 as 'claude/fetch-non-stream-bodies', shipped in v9.0.1) changed readResponseText. When a cap or signal is set, a response whose body lacks getReader() is now read with response.text() instead of throwing. That covers the Node Readable from node-fetch/cross-fetch, the undefined body of whatwg-fetch/React Native polyfills, and Response-like test doubles. With this fallback, abort rejects promptly but cannot cancel the body, and maxResponseBytes is checked only after the whole body is buffered, against the UTF-8 byte length. Injected fetchers must also honor the provided signal while acquiring the response.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/readResponseText.ts:129-146 (isReadableStream / readBufferedText), 156-161 (doc comment), 173-180; README.md:169-170 ('Injected fetchers must honor the provided signal...'), 201-206. Commit 158476cd7 message; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 158476cd7 v9.0.1` succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Inside the 'Bounded reads and cancellation' section added for finding 3, add one or two caveat lines. An injected fetcher must pass `init.signal` through (spreading `...init` does this). maxResponseBytes only bounds memory, and abort can only cancel the body, when the fetcher returns a native Response with a WHATWG ReadableStream body. With node-fetch, cross-fetch, whatwg-fetch/React Native polyfills or Response-like mocks, the body is read through response.text(): the whole body is buffered before the cap is checked, and abort only stops waiting. Skip the version-history note, or keep it to a parenthetical '(>= 9.0.1)'.

In that case abort only stops waiting and the cap is checked after buffering, against the UTF-8 byte length. findings.title: Request-side behavior undocumented: default gzip of bodies over 1024 chars, data/body serialization, baseURL resolution, shallow-merged client defaults
findings.current: fetch.md:7 names `fetchCompress` without explaining it. fetch.md:24-25 shows only `baseURL`, and fetch.md:28 lists the method helpers without saying how they treat request bodies.
findings.truth: (1) By default, compression is on for every helper: any request body whose string form exceeds `compressMinLength` (default 1024) is gzip-compressed and sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, so the server must accept gzip request bodies. Raise `compressMinLength` to opt out. (2) fetchJson's `body` is a native BodyInit sent as-is (pass a JSON string). fetchJsonPost/Put/Patch(url, data, options) and client.post/put/patch(url, data) JSON.stringify `data`. (3) FetchClient resolves `url` against `baseURL` with WHATWG `new URL(path, base)`, so `/item` against `https://api.example.com/v1` yields `https://api.example.com/item`; this differs from Axios-style joining. (4) Instance defaults are shallow-merged beneath per-request config, so a per-request `headers` or `params` replaces the client's rather than merging. Other config: `params`, `timeout`, `validateStatus`, `fetcher`, plus native RequestInit fields.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchCompress.ts:15-26,47-68 (default 1024 at :49); FetchJsonClient.ts:8-13; methods.ts:13-37; FetchClient.ts:9-32,73-83,97,152,178-180; FetchClient.spec.ts:193-199 (instance params {a} + request params {b} -> '?b=2'). `node -p "new URL('/item','https://api.example.com/v1').href"` -> https://api.example.com/item.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact 'Request options' table: baseURL (WHATWG resolution; use a trailing slash and a relative path to keep a base path), params, headers, timeout, validateStatus, compressMinLength (default 1024; gzip on by default), fetcher, maxResponseBytes. Add a note that per-request config shallow-replaces client defaults, including headers and params. Add one line that fetchJson takes a string `body` while the method helpers and client methods take `data`.

verify.code: confirmed: Each point checks out. (1) fetchCompress.ts:49 defaults compressMinLength to 1024. Lines 55-65 gzip any body whose string length exceeds it and set Content-Encoding: gzip, and every helper and client path goes through fetchCompress (fetchJson.ts:38, FetchClient.ts:182). (2) fetchJson sends `body` as-is apart from compression (fetchJson.ts:38-41). methods.ts:13-37 and FetchClient.ts:178-180 call JSON.stringify on `data`. (3) FetchClient.ts:73-83 resolves the URL with `new URL(path, base)`. On Node, `new URL('/item','https://api.example.com/v1')` gives https://api.example.com/item, and 'item' against 'https://api.example.com/v1/' gives /v1/item. (4) FetchClient.ts:97,152 shallow-merges `{...this.defaults, ...config}`, and FetchClient.spec.ts:193-199 shows request params {b} replacing instance params {a}. Config fields are listed at FetchClient.ts:9-32, and fetch.md:7,24-28 leaves all of this out.
verify.skill: confirmed: None of these behaviors appear anywhere in skills/ariestools-sdk/ (grep for compressMinLength, gzip, params, timeout and validateStatus found no hits). fetch.md:7 names fetchCompress without describing it. Each claim checks out in the source. (1) compressMinLength defaults to 1024 and applies to every helper; bodies whose string length exceeds it are gzipped with Content-Encoding: gzip (fetchCompress.ts:49,55-65; FetchJsonClient.ts:10). (2) fetchJson passes `body` through, while methods.ts:13-37 and FetchClient.ts:178-180 JSON.stringify `data`. (3) buildURL uses `new URL(path, base)` (FetchClient.ts:73-83), and `node -p "new URL('/item','https://api.example.com/v1').href"` prints https://api.example.com/item. (4) Defaults are merged with `{ ...this.defaults, ...config }` (FetchClient.ts:97,152), so per-request headers or params replace the client's (FetchClient.spec.ts:194-199). Gzip-by-default can break requests to third-party APIs that reject gzip request bodies, and shallow merging can silently drop a client auth header. That makes this materially incomplete, so medium is right.

findings.title: Undici guidance drops the README's 'compatible Undici release' qualifier for the global-dispatcher path
findings.current: fetch.md:49: 'If you need caching in Node, the **consumer** installs Undici and supplies a fetcher or global dispatcher.'
findings.truth: The SDK README says the Node app should install 'a compatible Undici release'. For `setGlobalDispatcher` to drive Node's built-in globalThis.fetch, the installed major should match Node's bundled undici. The SDK requires Node >= 26, which bundles undici 8.x. The API used in the snippets (Agent().compose, interceptors.cache, cacheStores.MemoryCacheStore {maxSize,maxCount,maxEntrySize}, type 'shared'|'private') is valid in both undici 7.29.1 and 8.10.2, so the snippets themselves are correct.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/README.md:33-36; packages/sdk/package.json engines `{ node: '>=26' }`; `node -p process.versions.undici` on Node v26.9.0 -> 8.10.2; `npm view undici dist-tags` latest 8.11.2, seven 7.30.0. The types in node_modules/.pnpm/undici@{7.29.1,8.10.2}/node_modules/undici/types/cache-interceptor.d.ts:13,40,118-162 and interceptors.d.ts:80 match the skill's usage.
findings.recommendation: Change fetch.md:49 to say the consumer installs a current Undici release compatible with the running Node's built-in fetch, for example undici 8.x on Node 26 (check `process.versions.undici`). Add a short note: with the global-dispatcher path, an outdated undici can have setGlobalDispatcher silently not affect globalThis.fetch, while a module-local fetcher using undici's own `fetch` is unaffected. Optionally add README.md:111-113: install the global dispatcher once, before normal requests, and include any proxy, TLS, retry or tracing behavior in it.

verify.code: adjusted: The omission is real. README.md:33-36 says 'install a compatible Undici release', and fetch.md:49 drops the qualifier. The engines field is node>=26, and Node v26.9.0 bundles undici 8.10.2. The snippet APIs match undici 7.29.1 and 8.10.2 (cache-interceptor.d.ts:40,122-162; interceptors.d.ts:80). However, the claim that the installed major should match Node's bundled undici is overstated. undici 7.29.1 lib/global.js sets both Symbol.for('undici.globalDispatcher.2') and '.1', the same as 8.10.2. I tested it on Node v26.9.0: an interceptor composed onto an undici 7.29.1 Agent and installed with its setGlobalDispatcher was hit by built-in globalThis.fetch (status 200, hits 1), and the same was true for 8.10.2. So 'undici 8 for Node 26' is not a requirement. The real point is that the installed release must share the global-dispatcher contract with Node's bundled undici, which 7.x and 8.x both do on Node 26.
verify.skill: adjusted: Real, but the reasoning in 'truth' (the major must match) is too strict. fetch.md:49 drops the README's 'compatible Undici release' qualifier (README.md:33-36). I tested it on Node v26.9.0, which bundles undici 8.10.2. Built-in fetch uses a dispatcher stored at Symbol.for('undici.globalDispatcher.2') (the test hit the fake dispatcher). It ignores one stored only at 'undici.globalDispatcher.1' (the request went to the real network and got ECONNREFUSED). So an older undici whose setGlobalDispatcher writes only the v1 symbol would silently fail to install the cache for globalThis.fetch. However, undici 7.29.1's lib/global.js:5-6,19-31 writes both symbols, so a current 7.x also works. Compatibility depends on the Dispatcher API symbol, not on matching majors exactly. A plain `pnpm add undici` today installs 8.x, and the module-local fetcher path is unaffected. Consequence: caching is silently skipped rather than the code failing, so low is right.

findings.title: Checklist calls OTel and zod 'optional peers, install only when used', but the root barrel requires both
findings.current: conventions.md:58 "3. Install optional peers (`zod`, OTel) only when used."

findings.title: Import style should say the root barrel loads every peer; subpaths are what keep peers optional
findings.current: conventions.md:5-6 "Prefer **named exports** from `@ariestools/sdk/<module>` or the root barrel." / "Prefer **subpath imports** for clarity and smaller mental graphs … when only a few symbols are needed." and :17 "Bundlers can drop unused modules when you import subpaths or when the root barrel is tree-shakeable."
findings.truth: The root barrel is one pre-bundled file per platform that statically imports zod/mini, zod/v4/core, @ariestools/telemetry (and through it @opentelemetry/api) and async-mutex. In Node, without a bundler, tree-shaking does not apply, so every one of those must resolve no matter which symbol you import. Subpaths keep the runtime graph small: only /hex, /object and /zod need zod; only /telemetry and /telemetry-exporter need OTel; /creatable needs async-mutex; the rest import no external packages. Libraries should prefer subpaths for a functional reason, not just readability.

findings.title: Tree-shaking omits that each subpath bundle has its own copy of shared classes, so instanceof fails across entries
findings.current: conventions.md:17 "Subpath exports map one-to-one with modules. Bundlers can drop unused modules when you import subpaths…"
findings.truth: @ariestools/sdk builds with the monolith default `moduleLinkage: 'bundle'`, which copies every referenced module into each entry. Shared code is duplicated, and object identity does not hold between subpaths or between a subpath and the root. For example, FetchError is defined separately in dist/neutral/api.mjs, fetch.mjs and the root index.mjs, and Base in base/creatable/events and the root. `err instanceof FetchError` therefore fails when the error comes from the copy in a different entry. The SDK ships `isFetchError` (a marker-based check) to cover this.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/xy.config.ts sets no moduleLinkage. toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/MonolithConfig.ts:155-166 ("`bundle` (default) … shared code is duplicated across entries so object identity does not hold between subpaths"; released since 78175963c 2026-07-06). dist: `var FetchError = class` at neutral/api.mjs:73, neutral/fetch.mjs:51, node/index.mjs:84. `var Base = class _Base` at neutral/base.mjs:20, creatable.mjs:34, events.mjs:20, node/index.mjs:1374. src/modules/fetch/FetchError.ts:35,149,202 (marker `'$$xylabs-fetch-error'` used by isFetchError).
findings.recommendation: Add: "Each subpath is self-contained, and shared classes are duplicated across entries. Do not use `instanceof` with SDK classes across different entry points. Use the provided guards (`isFetchError`, etc.), or import a given class from one entry point consistently, and do not mix root and subpath imports of the same class."

Toolchain MonolithConfig.ts:155-166 (current main 812b27a91, unchanged since 78175963c, 2026-07-06) documents `bundle` as the default and says "shared code is duplicated across entries so object identity does not hold between subpaths". In dist, `var FetchError = class` appears at neutral/api.mjs:73, neutral/fetch.mjs:51 and node/index.mjs:84, and `var Base = class _Base` appears at neutral/base.mjs:20, creatable.mjs:34, events.mjs:20 and node/index.mjs:1374. isFetchError (src/modules/fetch/FetchError.ts:196-203) falls back to the `$$xylabs-fetch-error` marker, which shows the SDK knows that cross-copy instanceof fails. findings.title: Testing-consumers note omits the Vitest 5 coupling and the side-effect matcher registration in @ariestools/testing
findings.current: conventions.md:51 "Add `@ariestools/testing` when you need shared matchers or extended helpers."
findings.truth: @ariestools/testing 9.0.1 lists `vitest ~5.0.1` as a direct dependency, and its module augmentation targets Vitest 5's `Assertion<R, T>`. A consumer on another Vitest major can end up with two Vitest copies and broken typings. Importing the package root or `/extended` calls `expect.extend(matchers)` as a side effect (declared in `sideEffects`), so it belongs in a Vitest setup file. `/matchers` exports the matchers without registering them.

findings.truth: Since 10.0.0 (published 2026-09-05; the skill was written 2026-09-01) the toolchain ships `xy plan lint` (experimental, `xyex plan lint` preferred, not part of `xy check`). It enforces a fixed layout. Required root files are AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md, and each must be a regular file, not a symlink. `papers/` may hold only README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and an optional GREEN-PAPER.md; any other file is an error, and `--fix` moves it into `notes/`. `docs/README.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md` and `notes/README.md` are required. CLAUDE.md must `@AGENTS.md`, and AGENTS.md must not use `@path` imports. docs/repo-docs.md also says "Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages." The reference repo (toolchain) follows this layout: papers/{README,WHITE-PAPER,YELLOW-PAPER}.md, a flat docs/ with ROADMAP.md, notes/README.md, and a regular-file CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md.

findings.title: The 'docs/ not called docs/' advice does not account for `xy plan lint` requiring docs/README.md and docs/ROADMAP.md
findings.current: structure.md:91 "...if the generated-API dump owns `docs/`, keep prose in the other directory and apply every convention here to it unchanged."
findings.truth: The repos are described accurately: sdk-js and sdk-react gitignore `/docs` for TypeDoc and keep prose in `documents/`, and arietrouw/6502-wasm uses `tech-doc/`. However, `xy plan lint` always requires regular files docs/README.md and docs/ROADMAP.md, and its links rule requires links into `docs/`. In a repo where docs/ is gitignored, the lint's fixer would create those files in an ignored directory.
findings.evidence: ariestools/sdk-js/.gitignore:4 (`/docs`, as reported by git check-ignore); ariestools/sdk-react/.gitignore:11; `ls` of sdk-js/documents and sdk-react/documents; arietrouw/6502-wasm/tech-doc; toolchain plan/lint.ts:33-36 and rootDocs.ts:80-102.
findings.recommendation: Add a caveat to structure.md:91. The toolchain lints only docs/, papers/ and specs/, both in the stable `xy agent lint` (part of `xy check`) and in the experimental `xyex plan lint`. It walks gitignored directories and never looks at documents/ or tech-doc/. In a repo where a generated dump owns docs/, the prose root is unchecked, and `xy check` reports docs.index-current and docs.front-matter against the dump. Recommend moving the dump out of docs/ (for example to a dist/ or build/ output path, which the walker skips), or else tuning `commands.agentLint.rules` in xy.config.ts. Warn never to run `xy check --fix` or `xy agent lint --fix` while the dump sits in docs/, because it writes front matter into generated files and creates docs/README.md there.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue is real, and 10.1.1 makes it worse. The evidence holds: sdk-js/.gitignore:4 `/docs` and sdk-react/.gitignore:11 `docs` cover the TypeDoc output (typedoc.json `out: docs/typedoc`), prose lives in documents/, and 6502-wasm has tech-doc/. The bigger problem is the stable `xy agent lint`, which `xy check` now runs (checkCommand.ts:49-50). It hard-codes `docs/`, `papers/` and `specs/` (agent/context.ts:16-23) and walks the filesystem without honouring .gitignore (agent/walk.ts:6-38 skips only node_modules, dist, build, .git and .claude). A read-only run of 10.1.1 `xy agent lint --json` in sdk-js reports 'docs/typedoc/media/typedoc-validation-*.md is missing front matter' (warn) and 'docs/README.md does not match the index generated from front matter' (error). The --fix or `xy agent index` path would write docs/README.md into the ignored dump (docsIndex.ts:24-28), while documents/ prose is never linted or indexed. So the skill's advice to keep prose in the other directory and 'apply every convention here to it unchanged' does not work with the shipped tooling. This applies once sdk-js and sdk-react move from ~10.0.x to 10.1.1. CI runs only `xy build`, so nothing breaks yet, which makes this medium rather than high. Plan lint also hard-codes docs/, but it is experimental.
verify.skill: adjusted: 10.1.1 makes this more serious and changes the target. The finding blamed the experimental plan lint. The stable `xy agent lint`, which `xy check` now runs, also hard-codes docs/, papers/ and specs/ (agent/context.ts:16-23). It walks the filesystem, not git, and skips only node_modules, dist, build, .git and .claude (walk.ts:6), so gitignored dumps are included. A read-only `xy agent lint --json` in ariestools/sdk-js (where `/docs` is gitignored per .gitignore:4) reported two docs.front-matter warnings on the generated docs/typedoc/media/*.md files. It also reported the error "docs/README.md does not match the index generated from front matter" (docs.index-current). The prose that structure.md:91 says to keep in documents/ is never linted. `xy check --fix` passes fix to agentLint (checkCommand.ts). It would then write `kind: doc` front matter into TypeDoc output (rules.ts:230-233) and create docs/README.md inside the ignored directory. So the setup the skill endorses gives a failing `xy check` whenever the dump exists locally. That is medium.

findings.title: Package-level AGENTS.md conflicts with toolchain policy and is not loaded "on demand" the way the skill claims
findings.current: agents-md.md:91: "Package-specific instructions → `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md`, which loads on demand." agents-md.md:130-136: "A package gets its own `AGENTS.md`... Codex composes root toward leaf. Claude Code loads a nested `CLAUDE.md` on demand..."
findings.truth: (1) The toolchain's documented contract (10.1.0) says: "Keep agent instructions at the repository root. Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages." (2) Claude Code reads AGENTS.md directly, including a subdirectory's AGENTS.md, only when no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or any directory above it. The root `@AGENTS.md` adapter that this same skill mandates suppresses that, and in this workspace CLAUDE.md always counts. So a lone `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` never loads in Claude Code; only a nested CLAUDE.md that imports it does. (3) Codex builds its chain once at startup, from the Git root down to the current working directory. A package AGENTS.md is invisible to a Codex session started at the repo root.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16 (also present at v10.1.0); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, "When Claude Code reads AGENTS.md": the "Count, so Claude reads them instead of AGENTS.md" list and "As Claude works in subdirectories: a subdirectory's AGENTS.md... [only] when none count"; Codex docs (developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md → learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md): "Starting at the project root... Codex walks down to your current working directory" and "builds an instruction chain when it starts"; CLAUDE.md exists above every repo.
findings.recommendation: Keep the nested tier; the stable `xy agent lint` rule agents.nested-delta-only now supports it. Remove "which loads on demand" from agents-md.md:91. In Nested files (lines 130-136), and in structure.md:24, say that a package delta is a pair: `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` plus a `packages/<pkg>/CLAUDE.md` containing only `@AGENTS.md`. Claude Code loads that pair when it reads, writes or edits a file in the directory. A lone package AGENTS.md is skipped whenever any CLAUDE.md exists at the root or above it. Codex sees the package file only when launched in that package. Separately, flag toolchain docs/repo-docs.md:16 as contradicting `agents.nested-delta-only`.

verify.code: adjusted: The loading mechanics are right. Claude Code docs: a subdirectory's AGENTS.md is read only 'When none count', and a CLAUDE.md/.claude/CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above counts. CLAUDE.md exists, and the skill itself requires a root `@AGENTS.md` adapter, so a lone packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md is never read by Claude. Codex docs: Codex 'builds an instruction chain when it starts' and 'stops searching once it reaches your current directory'. So 'which loads on demand' (agents-md.md:91) is wrong for both tools. The 'conflicts with toolchain policy' part is weaker in 10.1.1, and the high severity no longer holds. The stable `xy agent lint` now recognizes nested packages/*/AGENTS.md files: context.ts:22,33 collects them, and agents.nested-delta-only (warn, rules.ts:180-194) checks that they 'add a delta and do not restate the root'. That supports the skill's nested tier. Only docs/repo-docs.md:16 still says not to add them, and that line is unenforced and unchanged. The toolchain contradicts itself, so the skill does not violate enforced policy. The original recommendation's option to 'drop the nested-file tier' now conflicts with the shipped linter.
verify.skill: adjusted: The loading claim holds. code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, section "When Claude Code reads AGENTS.md", says that by default Claude reads AGENTS.md, including a subdirectory's, only when there is no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or any directory above it. The root `@AGENTS.md` adapter that the skill requires (structure.md:7), and the parent CLAUDE.md, both suppress that. So a lone packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md never loads in Claude Code, and agents-md.md:91 ("which loads on demand") is wrong. Codex docs confirm the chain is built once at startup, from the project root down to the cwd. The policy half of the finding is outdated in 10.1.1. The stable `xy agent lint` now explicitly supports package deltas: context.ts:22 and :33 collect `packages/*/AGENTS.md`, and the `agents.nested-delta-only` rule (warn) at rules.ts:180-194 accepts them. I checked this: a package AGENTS.md in a scratch repo produced no diagnostic. That doc is now the outlier, so "drop the tier" is no longer the right fix. Following the skill fails silently rather than breaking a command, so medium, not high.

findings.title: Adapter guidance for Copilot and Gemini does not reflect their current native AGENTS.md and import support

findings.truth: GitHub Copilot reads AGENTS.md natively, from anywhere in the repo with the nearest file winning, and also accepts a root CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md. Its link-only template (templates.md:83-92) is the kind of prose pointer that agents-md.md:118 calls "not good enough". Gemini CLI does not read AGENTS.md by default. GEMINI.md can import it with `@./AGENTS.md` (Memory Import Processor, recursive, default depth 5), or `context.fileName` can list AGENTS.md. So the import pattern used for CLAUDE.md works for GEMINI.md too.
findings.evidence: docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions (AGENTS.md "stored anywhere within the repository"; "the nearest AGENTS.md file in the directory tree will take precedence"; "Alternatively, you can use a single CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md file stored in the root"); geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md and geminicli.com/docs/reference/memport (context.fileName; @file imports).

findings.title: Size budget omits Codex's 32 KiB combined cap

findings.title: Authority table does not mention the toolchain's machine-readable authority index (`.xy/plan.json`)
findings.current: absent. agents-md.md:25-37 defines the authority table as the only routing mechanism, apart from docs/README.md.
findings.truth: Toolchain 10.1.0 ships the Plan Manifest v1 schema and experimental `xyex plan init`. A reviewed `.xy/plan.json` is described as "a curated authority and topology index" that routes agents to governing Markdown and states each document's lifecycle and authority level. Where a repo has one, the AGENTS.md authority table should agree with it, and the manifest's authority rules (source/tests > reviewed manifest for plan > xy work for task state) match this skill's intent.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:1-9 (purpose), :17-27 (authority boundaries), :50-70 (`xy plan init`, experimental); stability.ts:60-62; `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xyex.mjs plan init --help`; schema at toolchain/packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json.
findings.recommendation: After agents-md.md:37, add a short note: "If the repository has a reviewed `.xy/plan.json` (Plan Manifest v1, created with the experimental `xyex plan init`), keep this table consistent with the manifest's document catalog; never contradict it. A `status: bootstrap` manifest is a candidate inventory, not authority. Because this convention keeps lifecycle in YAML front matter (see lifecycle.md), set the manifest's per-document `metadata.source` to `front-matter` and do not duplicate state, review date or supersession in the manifest." Optionally add a one-line cross-reference in lifecycle.md's front-matter section with the same single-owner rule.

findings.title: The skills repo that publishes xy-agent breaks its own adapter rule (AGENTS.md is a prose pointer to CLAUDE.md) and omits xy-agent
findings.current: AGENTS.md:1-7 (repo root): `# AGENTS.md` / "Same guidance as [CLAUDE.md](./CLAUDE.md). Prefer that file..." / "This repo owns: `xy-development`, `xy-toolchain`, and `ariestools-sdk`". CLAUDE.md is a separate 70-line full document titled `# CLAUDE.md`.
findings.truth: agents-md.md:98, 118 and 140 say AGENTS.md is canonical, that a prose pointer is "not good enough", and that the H1 must not be the filename. This repo inverts the pattern: CLAUDE.md is canonical, AGENTS.md points at it in prose, and both titles are filenames. AGENTS.md also omits the fourth skill, xy-agent. Codex and Copilot users of this repo get only the 7-line pointer.
findings.evidence: ariestools-skills worktree AGENTS.md:1-7; CLAUDE.md:1-3 (`wc -l`: AGENTS.md 7, CLAUDE.md 70; CLAUDE.md is a regular file, not an import); skills/xy-agent/agents-md.md:98, 118, 140.
findings.recommendation:
1. Make AGENTS.md the canonical file, titled after the repo (for example `# ariestools-skills agent guidance`), and move CLAUDE.md's content into it.
2. Restructure it into the five sections that agents-md.md requires and that `xy agent lint` checks (`agents.required-sections`): Orient before acting, Which document is authoritative, Repository map, Commands you will actually need, and What NOT to do.
3. List all four skills, including xy-agent, in both the owned-skills statement and the skill-layer listing. CLAUDE.md:35 currently says "those three skills".
4. Replace CLAUDE.md with the toolchain adapter template: `<!-- Canonical agent instructions live in AGENTS.md. Claude Code imports that file. -->` followed by `@AGENTS.md`, as in plan/templates.ts:30-31.
5. To verify, run `xy agent lint` once the repo can run the toolchain. It should report no findings for `agents.adapter-thin`, `agents.h1-not-filename` or `agents.required-sections`.

findings.title: Generated docs/README.md index has no generator, and conflicts with the hand-written index that xy plan lint scaffolds
findings.current: lifecycle.md:106-108 "`docs/README.md` is generated from front matter and never hand-edited ... change the source, regenerate, and never edit the output." Also :84 "4. Regenerate the index.", :100 "regenerate the index", and :56 "or let the generated index cover it".
findings.truth: No index generator ships in @ariestools/toolchain 10.1.0 or in unreleased main. `xy --stability --json` lists no agent, docs, or index command. `xy agent` (lint/init/audit/index/archive) is still an open work item (XYW-20260901-263436, status open). The shipped experimental `xy plan lint` requires docs/README.md (rule plan.docs.required-files, fixable), and its --fix writes a hand-written index containing only a Roadmap link (templates.ts:54-63). The toolchain's own reference docs/README.md is hand-curated, and no workspace repo has a generated docs/README.md. An agent that follows the skill gets a step it cannot carry out ("regenerate"), and templates.md:210 names a command that does not exist (`pnpm xy agent index`).
findings.evidence: toolchain: `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs --stability --json` shows only plan, plan init, plan lint, repo, work (no agent/docs); .xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json title "Add xy agent: lint, init, audit, index, and archive ..." status "open"; packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:33-36 REQUIRED_DOC_PATHS ['docs/README.md','docs/ROADMAP.md']; packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/templates.ts:54-63 (docs/README.md template, no front matter, hand-written Contents list); toolchain docs/README.md:1-11 hand-curated; `for f in */*/docs/README.md` with a head-3 grep for 'generated' across the workspace found nothing; skills/xy-agent/auditing.md:9 already says "There is no `xy agent` command yet".

In 'The generated index': regenerate with `pnpm xy agent index`, or `pnpm xy agent lint --fix`; `xy agent archive` refreshes it automatically. Describe the actual output: a `# Docs` heading, then one row per docs/**/*.md except docs/README.md, with columns Document (relative link), Kind, and Status. Status shows front-matter `status` if present, otherwise `state`. There is no date or title column. Note that `docs.index-current` is an error in `xy agent lint` and in `xy check`, and it is an exact-text match. Keep 'Regenerate the index' in Supersession step 4 and in Archiving, and name the command. In templates.md, replace the docs/README.md sample with the generator's literal output: drop the `<!-- Generated -->` comment, the product heading, the intro paragraph and the Date/Title columns, any of which would fail the exact match. Because the Status column renders `status`, advise keeping `status` short and free of `|`. Optionally file a toolchain issue if date and title columns are wanted.

findings.title: Front-matter state vocabulary and field names do not match the toolchain's Plan Manifest v1 document-metadata contract
findings.current: lifecycle.md:11 `state: normative  # draft|active|normative|superseded|retired`; state table :29-35 (normative lives in `papers/`, `specs/`); :14 `reviewed:` "required for kind: runbook" only; :17 `supersededBy: docs/plans/NEW.md`.
findings.truth: The toolchain ships plan-manifest.v1.schema.json. Its documentMetadata keeps two axes separate: `lifecycle` (accepted|active|archived|deprecated|draft|proposed|superseded) and `authorityLevel` (descriptive|evidentiary|informative|normative). It requires `lastReviewed` on every reviewed document, and `supersededBy` is a manifest document id. docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34 lets a repo with a shared front-matter contract set `metadata.source: front-matter`; front matter then owns lifecycle, authority level, review date, and supersession. The skill's single `state` field mixes lifecycle with authority (`normative`), which goes against its own advice at :37-39 to keep those axes apart. It has `retired`, which has no manifest equivalent (the manifest uses archived/deprecated). It has no accepted/proposed, although decision records are "immutable once accepted" (:45). It requires `reviewed` only for runbooks. Within the skill, decisions are `state: normative` and live in docs/decisions/ (templates.md:100-101, 222), but the table says normative documents live only in papers/ and specs/.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-420 (documentMetadata oneOf: source manifest with lifecycle enum :343-353, authorityLevel enum :355-362, lastReviewed :364-367, supersededBy localId :368-370; source const front-matter :413-420); docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34; schema :436 planRole is "distinct from a generic file kind in front matter" (so `kind:` itself is compatible); skills/xy-agent/templates.md:100-101.
findings.recommendation: Keep the field names `state`, `reviewed`, `supersededBy`, `kind` and `status`, because the stable `xy agent` (10.1.1) reads them. Do not rename them to the manifest names. Changes to make: (1) Add `archived` to the state vocabulary, or say that `xy agent archive` sets `state: archived` and replaces superseded/retired. Decide whether `retired` stays as a separate value. (2) Say that `kind: doc` is the placeholder `xy agent lint --fix` inserts, and that it must be replaced with a real kind. (3) Say that `supersededBy` is resolved relative to the document file, which is how `xy agent` resolves it (for example `../plans/NEW.md`), and update the example at :17. Alternatively, file a toolchain issue to accept repo-relative paths. In either case, report the inverted archive check in docs.superseded-archived (rules.ts:271-273) upstream. (4) Add `docs/decisions/` to the normative 'Where it lives' cell. (5) Optionally add a short mapping note for repos that set `.xy/plan.json` `metadata.source: front-matter`: draft→draft, active→active, normative→accepted plus authority normative, superseded→superseded, retired/archived→archived/deprecated, reviewed→lastReviewed.

verify.code: adjusted: The schema facts are accurate (plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-411: lifecycle enum, authorityLevel enum, lastReviewed, supersededBy as a localId). The premise that the skill's front matter must match those names for `metadata.source: front-matter` to work is not supported. That branch is just `{source: 'front-matter'}` with additionalProperties false (:412-423), and the manifest defines no front-matter field names. Nothing in the toolchain checks front matter against the manifest enums: outside actions/agent no code reads front matter, and plan lint does not read .xy/plan.json (plan-manifest.md:116). 10.1.1 also makes the proposed rename harmful. The stable `xy agent` reads the skill's own names: `state` (rules.ts:265, 361; docsIndex.ts:17), `reviewed ?? date` (rules.ts:302), `supersededBy` (:266), `amends` (:285), `kind`, `status`. Renaming to lifecycle/lastReviewed would trigger decisions.naming 'has no state', skip docs.stale and docs.superseded-archived, and leave the index Status column blank. The claim that the skill breaks its own advice at :37-39 is a stretch: that passage separates authority from evidence tier, not lifecycle from authority. What is real: (a) `xy agent archive` writes `state: archived` (mutate.ts:26), a value missing from the vocabulary at :11 and :29-35. (b) Decisions are `state: normative` in docs/decisions/ (templates.md:100-101), but the table lists only papers/ and specs/ for normative. (c) xy agent resolves `supersededBy` relative to the document's own directory (rules.ts:44-48, 267), so the repo-root form `supersededBy: docs/plans/NEW.md` at :17 fails docs.superseded-archived.
verify.skill: adjusted: The finding is partly a misreading and partly overtaken by 10.1.1. (a) lifecycle.md:37-39 asks readers to keep authority separate from *evidence*. It does not ask for lifecycle to be kept separate from authority, so `state: normative` does not contradict it. (b) The Plan Manifest gives no front-matter field names. docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34 only says that a repo with "a shared document-front-matter contract" may set `metadata.source: front-matter`, and nothing in src/actions/plan reads front matter (a grep for frontMatter/front-matter finds nothing). So nothing in the toolchain checks front matter against `lifecycle`/`authorityLevel`/`lastReviewed`. (c) The stable `xy agent` in 10.1.1 reads the skill's own field names: `state` (rules.ts:265, :361), `reviewed ?? date` (rules.ts:302), `supersededBy` (rules.ts:266), and `kind`, `status` and `amends`. The recommended rename to `lifecycle`/`lastReviewed` would therefore break docs.stale, docs.superseded-archived and decisions.naming. What is still true or newly true: the normative row (:33) omits docs/decisions/ even though decisions use `state: normative` (templates.md:101). There are also new mismatches with 10.1.1. `xy agent archive` writes `state: archived` (mutate.ts:26), a value outside the skill's vocabulary, and it overwrites superseded/retired. `xy agent lint --fix` inserts `kind: doc` (rules.ts:231), a value outside the kind list at :10. And docs.superseded-archived resolves `supersededBy` relative to the document's directory (rules.ts:267 via linkExists, :44-48), so the skill's repo-relative example `supersededBy: docs/plans/NEW.md` (:17, :81) reports "superseded without a resolvable supersededBy". That rule also requires the *successor* to be under archive/ (rules.ts:271-273). This is the reverse of the skill and of the work-item spec, and it is a toolchain bug.

findings.title: The claim that front-matter workItems is the 'only structured connection' to xy work is inaccurate
findings.current: lifecycle.md:114 "Nothing in `xy work` links back — `WorkAnchor` supports only `kind: 'file'`, and there is no document or URL anchor kind — so this front-matter field is the only structured connection between the two"
findings.truth: WorkAnchor does support only kind 'file', with no document or URL kind; that part is correct. But a file anchor accepts any repo-relative path, including a document, through `xy work add --file docs/plans/X.md [--line N]`, so work items can point at documents. Separately, the shipped Plan Manifest v1 links documents and roadmap phases to work items in a structured way. Roadmap phases carry `workItems: [{id, relation: blocks|implements|tracks|verifies}]`, and a `planned` paper slot must list at least one work id. Work id prefixes are configurable (default XYW), and imported issues may use GH-*. `xy work` is experimental (`xyex work` is preferred).
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/schema.ts:17-21 (WorkAnchor), :181 (kind must be file), :81 (idPrefix 'XYW'); helpers.ts:16-23 normalizeAnchor; store.ts:134-147 pathInsideRepo (any in-repo path); `xy.mjs work add --help` shows "--file  Repo-relative file anchor", "--line", and "(experimental — prefer xyex)"; plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:158-186 (workItemId, workReference relations), :620-645 (plannedPaper.workItems minItems 1); docs/plan-manifest.md:129, 232-246, 283.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite :114 as follows. `xy work` items can point at a document through a file anchor (`xyex work add --file docs/plans/X.md [--line N]`). There is no document-aware or URL anchor kind, so the tool does not interpret that anchor. Front-matter `workItems:` is the document-side link. In a repo with a reviewed `.xy/plan.json`, roadmap phases (relation blocks/implements/tracks/verifies) and planned paper slots also reference work ids. findings.title: Evidence rules do not cover machine-readable (JSON) and dated-directory evidence, the dominant form in real repos
findings.current: lifecycle.md:60 "Name it `docs/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md`"; :65 "`commit:` in front matter, and the exact command in the body".
findings.truth: Workspace repos mostly record evidence as JSON reports, which cannot carry YAML front matter. Some use dated directories that contain only JSON; others pair *_EVIDENCE.md with *_REPORT.json. lifecycle.md gives an agent no rule for where commit and command metadata go for JSON artifacts, or how immutability and front matter apply to a directory bundle.
findings.evidence: ls XYOracleNetwork/xyo-chain/docs/evidence/2026-10-01-mainnet-durability/ → 10 *.json, no .md; XYOracleNetwork/chain-event-service/docs/evidence/2026-10-08-current-graph/ → CES-CURRENT-GRAPH-PUBLIC.json, runtime-qualification-public.json; ariestools/actor-kit/docs/evidence/*.json; XYOracleNetwork/dapp-kit/docs/evidence/*.json; XYOracleNetwork/crypto-cards/docs/*_EVIDENCE.md + *_REPORT.json pairs (e.g. ACTOR_PROVIDER_ENGINE_CATALOG_2026_09_18_EVIDENCE.md / _REPORT.json).
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Evidence bundles' rule. Machine-readable artifacts may live in a dated directory `docs/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/`. Pair the directory with a sibling `docs/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md` that carries the front matter (kind: evidence, commit), the exact command, and the tier statement, and that links each artifact. Prefer a sibling .md over a README.md inside the directory, because `xy agent lint` skips front-matter checks on README.md files and only checks immutability for .md files. JSON reports should embed their source commit and command (for example `sourceCommit`, as xyo-chain's source-bundle.json does). The immutability rule covers every file in the bundle, even though only the .md is machine-checked today.

findings.title: 'Pass an explicit stable id' cannot be done: xy work add has no --id flag, the library has no runtime entry, and ids are random per call
findings.current: auditing.md:102 "**Use a deterministic id.** `createWorkId` embeds today's date, so a re-derived id changes daily and every run creates a duplicate. Pass an explicit stable id derived from the check and the path, and check existence before adding."
findings.truth: `xy work add` / `xyex work add` has no `--id` option. Only the internal `workAdd()` function takes `id`, and @ariestools/toolchain ships no runtime JS entry: the package has only a `types` field, with no main or exports. yargs strict-option mode is not on, so an agent that passes `--id` has it silently ignored and still gets a new id. `createWorkId` also appends 3 random bytes of entropy, so the id changes on every call, not just once a day. Ids must match ^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]*[A-Z0-9]$, max 250 chars, so a raw path cannot be used. An existing id is overwritten without warning. No CLI command checks whether an item exists without creating the store.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/work/addCommand.ts:25-80 (options: description, area, tag, file, line, inline, acceptance, verify, impact, urgency, effort, risk, confidence; no id) and :85-104 (handler never passes id); `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xyex.mjs work add --help` lists no --id; actions/work/index.ts:104 `id?: string`, :171 `const id = options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`; actions/work/id.ts:13-17 (assertSafeWorkId regex), :20 `entropy = randomBytes(3)...`, :32 `${prefix}-${date}-${entropy}`; store.ts:92-95 writeWorkItem overwrites; packages/toolchain/package.json:30 only `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"` (`npm view @ariestools/toolchain@10.1.0 main exports module types` → only ./dist/index.d.ts); `grep -rn '.strict()\|strictOptions' packages/toolchain/src/xy` → no hits
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the bullet. Work ids are generated on every call as `<prefix>-<YYYYMMDD>-<6 random hex>`. `xy(ex) work add` has no `--id` flag: an unknown flag is silently ignored, and an existing item file with the same id would be overwritten. To dedupe, anchor each item to the document with `--file <doc path>` and give it a fixed tag (for example `--tag docs-audit`). If `.xy/work/config.json` already exists, run `pnpm xyex work list --json` and match on `anchors[].path` plus the tag, then use `pnpm xyex work update <id> ...` instead of adding a second item. If the store does not exist, do not run `work list` or `add` without operator consent, because both create the store with GitHub dual-write on (see the dual-write bullet). Delete the 'explicit stable id' advice, and do not cite XYW-20260901-263436: it is done and did not add id support.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim holds at 10.1.1. findings.title: Orphan-check script's git pathspec skips every top-level docs/*.md file

findings.truth: Without `:(glob)` magic, git treats `docs/**/*.md` as an fnmatch pattern that requires a '/' after `docs/<something>`. Files directly under docs/ never match. The script therefore silently reports no orphans for top-level docs, and they are also left out of the set of files it searches for links.

findings.title: Front-matter, staleness and supersession checks ignore .xy/plan.json, which can own document lifecycle metadata
findings.current: auditing.md:46-50 assumes front matter is the only metadata source (front matter present, `state: superseded` ⇒ `supersededBy`, `reviewed`/`date` staleness)
findings.truth: The toolchain ships Plan Manifest v1 (`.xy/plan.json`, created via `xyex plan init`). Its per-document `metadata.source` is either `manifest` or `front-matter`. With `manifest`, the lifecycle, authorityLevel, lastReviewed and supersededBy fields live in the manifest, and the schema says to 'never maintain both'. In such a repo, flagging missing front matter is a false positive, and adding front matter would break the manifest's single-owner rule.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-421 (documentMetadata oneOf; description at :335 'never maintain both'); docs/plan-manifest.md:28-33; `xyex plan --help` (plan init, plan lint); stability.ts:60-62
findings.recommendation: Add one caveat before the Documents checks. If the repo has a reviewed `.xy/plan.json` whose documents use `metadata.source: manifest`, take state, review dates and supersession from the manifest. Expect `docs.front-matter` warnings from `xy agent lint`, and do not run `xy agent lint --fix` or `xy check --fix`, which would insert front matter and break the manifest's single-owner rule. Lower `commands.agentLint.rules['docs.front-matter']` instead, and link to the toolchain's docs/plan-manifest.md.

verify.code: adjusted: The schema facts are right: plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-421 has documentMetadata as a oneOf of manifest and front-matter, with 'never maintain both' at :335, and docs/plan-manifest.md:28-33 matches. But the plan manifest is experimental (stability.ts:61-63 plan, plan init and plan lint are all experimental). No repo in the workspace has a `.xy/plan.json` (`ls */.xy/plan.json */*/.xy/plan.json` finds none). The stable 10.1.1 `xy agent lint` ignores the manifest entirely: actions/agent has no reference to plan.json, and docs.front-matter warns on any docs/, papers/ or specs/ file without front matter (rules.ts:222-243). The skill is consistent with the stable tool. The conflict arises only if a repo opts into the experimental manifest with metadata.source manifest, and in that case the toolchain itself conflicts. Real, but an edge case.
verify.skill: adjusted: The schema conflict is real: plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:335 says 'never maintain both', and docs/plan-manifest.md:28-33 describes metadata.source set to manifest or front-matter. findings.title: Work-item guidance names fields but not the flags or item type to use

State that the type positional is required, that setting any one priority flag fills the others with 3, and that --acceptance and --verify are repeatable. Note that the CLI has no --id flag, so the stable-id advice at line 102 cannot be done through `work add` today (either drop that advice or point to the gap).

findings.title: 'Do not claim work there' conflicts with the xy work claim flow taught in xy-toolchain and the toolchain's xy-work skill

Add the same one-line caveat next to `work next --claim` / `work claim` in skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md (~185-199) so the two skills agree. verify.code: adjusted: The core issue is real, but the evidence overstates commands.md. claimItem (helpers.ts:56-69) is a plain writeWorkItem. It rejects only done/wontfix (line 57), so `xy work claim <id>` overwrites an item that is already claimed, even within one checkout. `next` skips claimed items only in the local snapshot (queue.ts:44,161), and items are committed files (the work.store-not-gitignored rule, work/lint.ts:158-172), so claims cannot coordinate across worktrees or clones. verify.skill: confirmed: auditing.md:109 does say "Queue work there; do not claim work there." Its technical basis checks out. helpers.ts claimItem is a plain writeWorkItem overwrite with no lease, compare-and-swap, or already-claimed check, and nothing in it changed in 10.1.1. Even so, xy-toolchain/commands.md:185-186,199 presents `pnpm xy work next --claim` and `pnpm xy work claim <id>` as normal lifecycle steps with no caveat. The toolchain's local .agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:22 and :146-149 tell agents to claim before starting work, and the toolchain itself uses that flow: item XYW-20260901-263436 has claimedAt 2026-10-08T18:01:33Z. So the blanket ban is broader than its rationale, and the pack gives conflicting guidance. Narrowing it to "claims are advisory and not exclusive across worktrees or clones" keeps the valid point. findings.title: Front-matter templates use a single `state` / `reviewed` vocabulary that does not map onto the toolchain's published document-metadata model
findings.current: Decision template: templates.md:98-105 (`state: normative`, with acceptance only in prose `status: "accepted YYYY-MM-DD"`). Evidence template: templates.md:131-138 (`state: active`). Runbook template: templates.md:162-169 (`reviewed:`). Vocabulary from lifecycle.md:11 (draft|active|normative|superseded|retired).
findings.truth: The toolchain's plan-manifest schema, shipped in @ariestools/toolchain 10.1.0, defines document metadata on two separate axes. The first is `lifecycle` (accepted, active, archived, deprecated, draft, proposed, superseded). The second is `authorityLevel` (descriptive, evidentiary, informative, normative). It also has `lastReviewed` and `supersededBy`. A repo may hand ownership of exactly these fields to front matter (`metadata.source: front-matter`). The skill's single `state` field merges the two axes: a decision cannot be both `accepted` and `normative`, and evidence cannot be marked `evidentiary`. The field names (`reviewed` vs `lastReviewed`) also differ. So the templates' front matter cannot serve as that owner without translation. There is also an internal inconsistency: lifecycle.md:33 says `normative` lives in `papers/`, `specs/`, yet the decision template and index example (templates.md:221) mark `docs/decisions/` normative.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-390 (documentMetadata: lifecycle, authorityLevel, lastReviewed, supersededBy). toolchain docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34 ("Document lifecycle metadata has exactly one owner... may set `metadata.source` to `front-matter`"), 315. skills/xy-agent/lifecycle.md:7-35.
findings.recommendation: Do not adopt the plan-manifest field names; keep `state`/`reviewed`/`status`, which the stable `xy agent` lint reads. In lifecycle.md: add `docs/decisions/` to the 'Where it lives' column of the `normative` row (line 33), and add `archived`, the value `pnpm xy agent archive` writes, to the state vocabulary at line 11. Alternatively, record a toolchain item to make archive write superseded/retired instead. No change to the templates.md front-matter blocks is needed.

But the recommended direction is now wrong. The stable 10.1.1 `xy agent` tooling reads exactly this skill's vocabulary. `docs.stale` reads `reviewed ?? date` (rules.ts:302). `decisions.naming` requires `state` (rules.ts:361). `docs.superseded-archived` reads `state` and `supersededBy` (rules.ts:265-266). The index uses `status ?? state` (docsIndex.ts:17), and `docs.evidence-immutable` reads `amends` (rules.ts:285). No code in src/actions/plan reads front matter (grep returns nothing); 'front-matter consistency' appears only as a planned semantic-lint item (plan-manifest.md:315). Renaming to lifecycle/authorityLevel/lastReviewed would break the stable linter. What remains real is internal. lifecycle.md:33 places `normative` in papers/ and specs/, yet the decision template (templates.md:101) and the index example (templates.md:221) mark docs/decisions as normative. Acceptance is recorded only as prose in `status`. And `xy agent archive` writes `state: archived` (mutate.ts:26), a value missing from lifecycle.md:11.

findings.title: The canonical tree contradicts the toolchain's `xyex plan lint` layout; its `--fix` moves xy-agent-style papers into notes/
findings.current: The canonical tree at structure.md:5-27 has `papers/`, `specs/`, `docs/{README,decisions,runbooks,plans,evidence,archive}`, `references/` and `prototypes/`. It has no `notes/`, no `docs/ROADMAP.md`, and no root CHANGELOG.md or CONTRIBUTING.md. structure.md:29 says "Not every repository needs every tier… an empty `papers/` directory is a lie", and :50 sets the naming as `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`.
findings.truth: `xyex plan lint` (experimental, shipped in 10.1.0) enforces a different canonical layout, with every rule at error level. It requires root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md. It requires papers/README.md, papers/WHITE-PAPER.md and papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md, allows only GREEN-PAPER.md besides those, and flags any other file (error `plan.papers.unexpected-files`). It also requires docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/README.md. `--fix` relocates unexpected paper files into notes/. A repository that follows xy-agent (for example `ACME_WHITE_PAPER.md` or `ACME_LIGHT_PAPER.md`, and no notes/) therefore fails plan lint, and the fix moves its papers.
findings.evidence: packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-37 (required and optional path lists), :477-512 (rules with defaultLevel 'error'; "fixes flatten other regular files into notes/"). `xy.mjs plan lint --help`: "Create missing required files and relocate unexpected regular paper files to notes/". The toolchain CHANGELOG [Unreleased] says canonical planning documents now use papers/WHITE-PAPER.md, papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md and docs/ROADMAP.md. stability.ts:60 marks plan as experimental.
findings.recommendation: Keep xy-agent's tree. It is the layout enforced by stable `xy agent lint`, which runs in `xy check` from 10.1.1. In structure.md, add a short note covering three points. (1) `pnpm xy agent lint` / `init` / `index` check and scaffold this layout. (2) The experimental `pnpm xyex plan lint` enforces a different layout: papers/WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and optional GREEN-PAPER.md only, required docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/README.md, and root CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. (3) plan lint's `--fix` moves product-prefixed or LIGHT papers into notes/, so do not run it on a repository that follows this skill. Separately, file a toolchain work item to reconcile `plan lint` with `agent lint`, either by accepting the `<PRODUCT>_*_PAPER.md` names and specs/ or by making the papers allowlist configurable through commands.planLint, before plan is promoted.

findings.title: The release commands `xy deploy` and `xy publish` (including `--tag`) are not documented
findings.current: Absent. The skill never mentions `deploy` or `publish`; the router in SKILL.md only says "validating publish surfaces".
findings.truth: Both commands are stable. `xy deploy [patch|minor|major|prerelease]` bumps lockstep versions, runs `xy clean` and `xy build`, then applies the version. `xy publish` publishes to npm and accepts `--tag <dist-tag>` (prereleases should use next or canary so latest stays on stable) and `--chunk-size <n>` (pnpm only; each chunk triggers a separate 2FA prompt).
findings.evidence: src/xy/stability.ts:34-35. src/actions/deploy.ts:7-18. `xy.mjs deploy --help` (choices patch/minor/major/prerelease, default patch). `xy.mjs publish --help` (--tag, --chunk-size). docs/STABILITY.md:26-32 ("pnpm xy publish --tag next"). Toolchain README.md:107-109.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Release' subsection. Cover: `pnpm xy deploy [patch|minor|major|prerelease]` (bumps every lockstep package, then runs `xy clean` and `xy build`, then applies the version). `pnpm xy publish [--tag next|canary] [--chunk-size n]` (use a non-latest dist-tag for prereleases; with chunking, each chunk triggers a separate 2FA prompt). Since 10.1.1, publish and deploy run the toolchain implementation even when the root package.json defines a same-named script; pass `--defer` to run that script instead. Add `--defer` to the global flag table next to `--no-defer`. Note that repositories using release-please or CI publishing follow their own workflow, and that publishing and deploying are owner actions an agent should not take unasked.

findings.title: The global-flag table has the wrong `--jobs` default and omits `-v`, `-i` and the environment-variable equivalents
findings.current: commands.md:21: "`--jobs <n>` | Limit parallel work; default is 16". The table at :19-27 has no `--verbose` or `--incremental`, and no `XY_STRICT` or `XY_NO_DEFER`. The `--no-defer` row says only "Bypass a same-named local package script".
findings.truth: The `--jobs` default is `availableParallelism()`; it shows 16 only on a 16-core machine. Other global flags are `-v/--verbose` and `-i/--incremental`; the latter defaults to on for compile, build and lint, and `--no-incremental` disables it. `XY_STRICT=1` equals `--strict` and `XY_NO_DEFER=1` equals `--no-defer`. Deferral applies only to a root package.json script with the same name, and only when no subcommand is given.
findings.evidence: src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:58, :61 and :88-100 (`default: availableParallelism()`). src/lib/tryRunLocalScript.ts:13-37. src/xy/build/buildCommand.ts and compileCommand.ts (`incremental: argv.incremental !== false`).
findings.recommendation: In commands.md:19-27, change the `--jobs` default to "available CPU parallelism (os.availableParallelism())". Reword `--no-defer` as: do not delegate to a same-named root package.json script (also `XY_NO_DEFER=1`); delegation applies only to a top-level command with no subcommand. Add a `--defer` row: since 10.1.1, `xy publish` and `xy deploy` run the toolchain implementation even when a same-named root script exists, unless `--defer` is passed. Optionally add `-v/--verbose`. Skip the `-i` row and the XY_STRICT note, which toolchain.md:108 and eslint.md:96 already cover.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claims hold. The jobs default is `availableParallelism()` (src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:88-93); help shows 16 only because this machine reports 16 CPUs. -v/--verbose and -i/--incremental are global options (:94-104). XY_STRICT=1 is read at :58 and XY_NO_DEFER=1 at :61 and tryRunLocalScript.ts:16. Deferral happens only when there is exactly one positional (:63) and a matching root package.json script exists (tryRunLocalScript.ts:35-43). Incremental defaults to on for build, compile, lint and also publint (`argv.incremental !== false` in buildCommand.ts:17, compileCommand.ts:23, lint/runCommand.ts:124, publintCommand.ts:73). 10.1.1 (b75077b16) changes the right fix: there is a new global `--defer` flag, and `deploy`/`publish` no longer defer to a same-named root script unless `--defer` is passed (tryRunLocalScript.ts:13 and :45-50, xyParseOptions.ts:126-130).

Help only shows 16 because this machine's availableParallelism() is 16. Several other parts of the finding overreach.
