findings.title: The `xy publint` check-selection and pack flags are undocumented
findings.current: commands.md:129-131 describes only `--fix`.
findings.truth: `xy publint` also accepts `-e/--exclude` and `--include`, each a comma-separated list of checks: compileTargets, defaultExportOrder, files, importsMatchExports, importToDefault, main, module, neutralToDefault, peerDeps, platform, publint, resolutions, rootSource, rootTypes, sideEffects, source and types. peerDeps runs only on all-workspace runs. `--fresh` clears the incremental snapshot, and `--pack` (default true) packs before checking. The `pub.importsMatchExports` and `pub.platform` rules default to error.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs publint --help`. `xy.mjs --rules --json` (publint pub.* levels).
findings.recommendation: Add one line to commands.md under `xy publint` covering `--include/--exclude <checks>` (comma-separated pub.* check names; peerDeps runs only on all-workspace runs), `--fresh` (clears the incremental snapshot) and `--no-pack` (skips the pre-check pack, and so skips published-files verification; do not use it as a gate). Note that three rules default to error: pub.importsMatchExports and pub.publint, which `--fix` cannot fix, and pub.platform, which `--fix` can partially fix.

verify.code: adjusted: The flags are real: -e/--exclude, --include, --fresh and --pack in publintCommand.ts:22-39; the check list comes from ALL_PUBLINT_CHECKS; peerDeps runs only on all-workspace runs; pack defaults to true via `pack ?? config.pack ?? true` at actions/publint.ts:179. The rule claims are wrong, though. Three rules default to error, not two: ERROR_BY_DEFAULT_PUBLINT_RULES = importsMatchExports, platform and publint (actions/package/publintRules.ts:51). pub.platform is also in FIXABLE_PUBLINT_RULES (:35-44), and `xy publint --rules` shows Fix=yes for it. So saying the error rules 'cannot be auto-fixed' is wrong for pub.platform. Unchanged in 10.1.1.
verify.skill: adjusted: The gap is real. commands.md:129-131 documents only `--fix`, while `xy.mjs publint --help` shows -e/--exclude and --include (with the same check list as the finding; peerDeps runs only on all-workspace runs), --fresh and --pack (default true). The recommendation is wrong about the error-level rules, though. publintRules.ts:51 defines `ERROR_BY_DEFAULT_PUBLINT_RULES = ['importsMatchExports', 'platform', 'publint']`, which is three rules, not two. `xy publint --rules` shows pub.platform with Fix=yes, because 'platform' is in FIXABLE_PUBLINT_RULES (publintRules.ts:36-49). Only pub.importsMatchExports and pub.publint are not fixable. The skill already says `--fix` "cannot fix every upstream publint error" (:131). Recommending `--no-pack` for quick local runs also needs a caveat, because it skips verification of the packed file set.

findings.title: The validation section omits the native compiler (`xyex enable ts-native`) and `xyex tsc-validate`
findings.current: compilation.md:84-93 covers `compile.validate`, the package-compile flags and `compile.validator`, but never mentions `compile.compiler` or the tsc-validate command.
findings.truth: `compile.compiler: 'native'` (TypeScript 7 / Go) is an experimental surface enabled with `pnpm xyex enable ts-native [--no-install]`, and it is incompatible with the shared validator. `xyex tsc-validate [package]` runs the shared-host engine as a standalone command. Public examples must not require the native compiler.
findings.evidence: src/xy/stability.ts:20 and :49. EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_SURFACES entries compile.compiler.native and compile.validator.shared (stability.ts, around line 140). `xy.mjs enable ts-native --help`. docs/ROADMAP.md D4.
findings.recommendation: Add two bullets: `compile.compiler: 'native'` is experimental, is set up via `xyex enable ts-native`, does not combine with `validator: 'shared'`, and should not appear in public templates. `xyex tsc-validate` is the standalone form of the shared validator.

verify.code: confirmed: stability.ts:20 marks tsc-validate experimental. EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_SURFACES (stability.ts:137-152) lists compile.validator.shared ("Same engine as `xyex tsc-validate`. Incompatible with `compile.compiler: 'native'`") and compile.compiler.native ("Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`... public examples must not require it"). `xy enable ts-native --help` shows `--no-install`. `xyex tsc-validate [package]` exists. At runtime, actions/compile.ts:351-352 warns and falls back to per-package validation when shared is requested with native. ROADMAP.md:53 (D4) keeps native experimental. compilation.md:84-93 mentions neither. Unchanged in 10.1.1.
verify.skill: confirmed: compilation.md:80-93 covers compile.validate, the package-compile flags, and `compile.validator` per-package/shared. A grep of skills/ finds no mention of `compile.compiler`, 'native', `tsc-validate` or `xyex`. stability.ts:20 lists `'tsc-validate': 'experimental'` and :50 lists `'enable': 'experimental'`. In EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_SURFACES (stability.ts:137-151), compile.validator.shared says "Same engine as `xyex tsc-validate`. Add `xy agent lint` to the policy table: AGENTS.md entry point, adapters, docs index and front matter, included in `xy check` since 10.1.1. findings.title: The `package-*` hook guidance conflicts with STABILITY.md and the hook list is incomplete
findings.current: toolchain.md:68-90 tells agents to "Use `package-*` binaries as per-package hooks" and lists seven hooks plus the `-only` variants. compilation.md:103-108 tells agents to run `package-sync-layout` by hand.
findings.truth: STABILITY.md calls the `package-*` bins an implementation detail of `xy` and asks docs and automation to prefer the `xy` CLI. The package also ships package-copy-assets-cjs, package-copy-assets-esm, package-lint-verbose, package-relint (the counterpart of the deprecated relint) and run-or-exec. `xy compile` already re-syncs the monolith layout, so manual `package-sync-layout` is needed only for `--check` drift detection.
findings.evidence: docs/STABILITY.md:53. packages/toolchain/package.json bin map. src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileMonolith.ts:157 (calls syncMonolithLayout during compile). src/bin/package/sync-layout.ts:11 (`--check`).
findings.recommendation: In skills/xy-toolchain/compilation.md:103-108, say that `xy compile` regenerates the monolith layout automatically. Running `package-sync-layout` by hand is needed only to sync without compiling, and `package-sync-layout --check` is the drift check for CI. Optionally add half a sentence to toolchain.md:68 saying the `package-*` bins are implementation details meant for package-script extension, with the `xy` CLI preferred in docs and CI (STABILITY.md). Do not expand the hook table with the additional bins.

verify.code: adjusted: Verified: docs/STABILITY.md:53 says the `package-*` bin scripts are an "Implementation detail of `xy`; prefer the `xy` CLI in docs and automation". The package.json bin map also has package-copy-assets-cjs, package-copy-assets-esm, package-lint-verbose, package-relint and run-or-exec. packageCompileMonolith.ts:157 calls syncMonolithLayout before validation whenever the compile emits, and sync-layout.ts:11 handles `--check`. One part of the recommendation contradicts itself: it says the hooks are not for direct CI use, then names `package-sync-layout --check` as the CI drift check. No `xy` command wraps the sync-layout check (grep of src finds only bin/package/sync-layout.ts), so that bin is a real exception. Unchanged in 10.1.1.
verify.skill: adjusted: Most of this finding overstates the problem. toolchain.md:68 already scopes `package-*` binaries to "per-package hooks invoked by root orchestration or package scripts", and the surrounding text (:80-90) is about extending package scripts without recursion. That is consistent with STABILITY.md (Config stability table), which calls them an "Implementation detail of `xy`; prefer the `xy` CLI in docs and automation". The bin map does include package-copy-assets-cjs/esm, package-lint-verbose, package-relint and run-or-exec (packages/toolchain/package.json). Listing those implementation details would cut against STABILITY.md, so the incompleteness is not worth fixing. The one real improvement is in compilation.md:103-108, which tells agents to run `package-sync-layout` by hand. packageCompileMonolith.ts:155-160 already syncs the monolith layout on every emitting compile. The toolchain offers no `xy` equivalent of `package-sync-layout --check` (bin/package/sync-layout.ts:11-37), and its own CHANGELOG.md:21 and papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md:284 and :405 document that bin. The `--check` form therefore remains the right drift check. The change belongs in compilation.md, not toolchain.md.

findings.title: The work section omits the triage and anchor flags and the `.xy/work`-tracked / `.xy/cache`-ignored rule
findings.current: commands.md:177-201 shows `work add <type> <title>` with no `--area`, priority, `--acceptance`, `--verify`, `--file`/`--line`/`--inline` or list filters. Git policy at :158 says only "LF settings and case sensitivity".
findings.truth: `work add` and `work update` accept --area, --tag, --impact, --urgency, --effort, --risk, --confidence (each 1-5), --acceptance and --verify (both repeatable), and --file/--line/--inline; an item missing these counts as untriaged. `work list` accepts --status, --type and --sort created|priority, and `work queue` accepts --name, --limit and --status. `work.store-not-gitignored` (error) requires `.xy/work` to stay tracked, while `git.ignore-toolchain-cache` expects `**/.xy/cache/` to be ignored in every package.
findings.evidence: `xyex work add|list|queue|update --help`. Toolchain-local .agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:24-56 and :146-150. `xy --rules --json` (work.store-not-gitignored error; git.ignore-toolchain-cache warn). src/actions/gitlintIgnore.ts:7-9 (`'**/.xy/cache/'`, "never .xy/work, which is tracked").
findings.recommendation: In commands.md's `xy work` section, add a capture example with triage fields, using the same invocation as the rest of the section (or switch the whole section to `xyex`, since `xy work` reports itself as experimental). For example: `pnpm xy work add bug "…" --area x --impact 4 --urgency 2 --effort 1 --risk 2 --confidence 3 --acceptance "…" --verify "pnpm xy build"`. Note that the anchor flags --file, --line and --inline exist only on `work add`. State the untriaged rule: an open item missing area, priority, acceptance or verification. Add the `work list --status/--type/--sort priority` and `work queue --name/--limit/--status` filters. Add the gitignore rule: ignore `**/.xy/cache/` (git.ignore-toolchain-cache) and never ignore `.xy/work`, which work.store-not-gitignored treats as an error.

verify.code: adjusted: Most claims check out. `xyex work add --help` lists --area, --tag, --file, --line, --inline, --acceptance, --verify and --impact/--urgency/--effort/--risk/--confidence. `work list` has --status, --type and --sort created|priority. `work queue` has --name, --limit and --status. `xy --rules --json` gives work.store-not-gitignored as error (not fixable) and git.ignore-toolchain-cache as warn (fixable). gitlintIgnore.ts:7-9 holds '**/.xy/cache/' and the 'never .xy/work, which is tracked' comment. Two details are wrong. (1) `work update --help` has no --file, --line or --inline; only `work add` takes the anchor flags. (2) Triage status depends on fewer fields than stated: actions/work/list.ts:173-180 treats an item as untriaged only when it is open and lacks a priority, an area, acceptance criteria or verification, so anchors and tags do not count. Nothing in the work code changed in 10.1.1.
verify.skill: adjusted: The gap is real, but one detail is wrong. commands.md:177-201 shows `work add <type> <title>` with no triage or anchor flags, and :201 mentions gitignore only as "store health". `xyex work add --help` shows --area, --tag, --file, --line, --inline, --acceptance and --verify (both repeatable), and --impact, --urgency, --effort, --risk and --confidence. `work update --help` has the triage and priority flags but no --file, --line or --inline, so the finding is wrong that update accepts anchors. `work list --help` shows --status, --type and --sort created|priority. `work queue --help` shows --name, --limit and --status. The untriaged criterion is `status === 'open'` plus a missing priority, area, acceptance or verification (actions/work/list.ts:172-178); anchors play no part. `work lint --rules` shows work.store-not-gitignored at error, and `git lint --rules` shows git.ignore-toolchain-cache at warn and fixable. gitlintIgnore.ts:7-9 holds the `**/.xy/cache/` entry and the "never .xy/work, which is tracked" comment. Partial coverage already exists: commands.md:231 names priority, acceptance and verification, and xy-agent/auditing.md:104 states the untriaged rule. The finding's example uses `pnpm xyex work`, while the skill uses `pnpm xy work` throughout. Both work: `xy work --help` runs and labels it "experimental — prefer xyex". The new example should match the section's invocation, or the section should switch as a whole.

findings.title: Compile config does not deep-merge root into package; nearest xy.config wins for compile.*
findings.current: compilation.md:29 "Root configuration cascades to packages under that root. Package-level configuration overrides or deep-merges the applicable root settings."
findings.truth: Only `commands.*` merge root + workspace (loadWorkspaceCommandConfig). `xy compile` spawns `package-compile` in each workspace directory, and packageCompile loads config with a cosmiconfig search from that directory, so the nearest config file wins. A package xy.config.ts replaces the root `compile` block completely (shared fields such as `compiler` must be repeated). A package with no config of its own inherits the root file unchanged. `compile.validator`, and the native check that goes with it, is read from the root config only. The publint expected-output check deep-merges root + package, so it can disagree with what compile actually emits.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/compile.ts:16-19 (packageCompile → loadConfig(inConfig) from cwd); lib/loadConfig.ts:52-59,61-93 (cosmiconfig search() from process.cwd(); loadConfig = deepMerge(nearestConfig, params)); lib/loadConfig.ts:195-207,229-245 (only command configs merge root+workspace); pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:180-188 (`pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec package-compile` runs in the package dir); actions/compile.ts:348-355 (validator from root config only); actions/package/expectedCompileOutputs.ts:83-88 (publint deep-merges root+pkg, which is inconsistent with compile). Real-world corroboration: sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 sets `compile: { compiler: 'native' }` yet every sdk-js packages/*/xy.config.ts (crypto-auth:2, crypto, eth-address:2, express, meta:2, pixel, sdk) repeats `compiler: 'native'`. Toolchain docs/xy-config.md:15 makes the same inaccurate deep-merge claim.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 29 with: "`commands.*` settings cascade: root and package configs merge (arrays concatenate, maps merge, `rules` replace per rule id). `compile` does not merge. Each package compiles with the nearest xy.config file, so a package xy.config.ts replaces the root `compile` block. Repeat shared compile fields such as `compiler` in every package config that exists. Set `compile.validator` at the root only." Also file a toolchain issue to make compile and publint's expectedCompileOutputs agree, and to fix docs/xy-config.md:15.

verify.code: confirmed: Re-derived from code, and 10.1.1 does not change it (loadConfig.ts and compile.ts are not in the 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91 diff). How it works: packageCompile (actions/package/compile/compile.ts:16-19) calls loadConfig(inConfig). loadConfig (lib/loadConfig.ts:90-93) is deepMerge(root search result, params). The search is getExplorer().search() from process.cwd() (lines 52-58, 69). `xy compile` spawns `package-compile` per workspace through pm.runInWorkspaceByName, which is `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec package-compile` (pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:185-188; actions/compile.ts:117-125, 416-445), so cwd is the package directory and the nearest xy.config wins. Only loadWorkspaceCommandConfig/mergeCommandConfig (loadConfig.ts:195-245) merges root with workspace config, and only for `commands.*`. resolveCompileValidator reads the root config only (actions/compile.ts:345-353). expectedCompileOutputs.ts:83-88 deep-merges root + package for publint, which is inconsistent with what compile uses. Real-world corroboration: sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 sets compiler 'native', and every sdk-js package config repeats `compiler: 'native'`. docs/xy-config.md:15 still says 'Package config deep-merges'. Following compilation.md:29 silently drops root compile settings (compiler, targets, mode) in any package that has its own xy.config.ts, which is a wrong config, so high is right.
verify.skill: confirmed: Still true at 10.1.1 (loadConfig.ts and compile code did not change after 7eb43c3c2). The skill says at compilation.md:29 that package config 'overrides or deep-merges' root settings. In practice `xy compile` spawns `package-compile` per workspace through `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec` (pnpmPackageManager.ts:185-188, compile.ts:417-425). Each spawn calls packageCompile, which calls loadConfig(inConfig) (package/compile/compile.ts:16-19), and loadConfig is deepMerge(cosmiconfig search() from the package cwd, params) (loadConfig.ts:52-59, 90-93). The nearest file wins and the root is never merged in. Only commands.* merge root and workspace (loadConfig.ts:195-245). Validator selection reads only the root config (compile.ts resolveCompileValidator). expectedCompileOutputs.ts loadMergedWorkspaceConfig does deep-merge root and package, so publint expectations can disagree with what compile emitted. sdk-js shows the real effect: the root sets compile.compiler 'native', and every packages/*/xy.config.ts repeats `compiler: 'native'`. docs/xy-config.md:15 still says 'Package config deep-merges'. High severity is justified: a root `compile.node: true` plus a package `compile: {entryMode...}` builds neutral only, and the merged publint expectation then fails.

findings.title: `commands.dependabot.rules` fails typecheck in a typed XyConfig (key missing from CommandsConfig)
findings.current: commands.md:150 "raise levels under `commands.dependabot.rules` to gate" (the skill's standard pattern is `const config: XyConfig = {...}`)
findings.truth: At runtime, `xy secure dependabot` reads `commands.dependabot`. The published 10.1.0 `CommandsConfig` type has no `dependabot` key, and no `workLint` key either. A typed object literal with `commands: { dependabot: ... }` is rejected with TS2353. Full-package validation and editors then fail.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:655-678 (CommandsConfig keys: apiExposure, clean, dead, deplint, gitLint, gitlint, license, lintLint, lintlint, nodeLint, npmOrgLint, packman, planLint, publint, repoLint, skillsLint; there is no dependabot or workLint key); same in published dist/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.d.ts:598-621; lib/ruleCommandRegistry.ts:48-53,125-130 (configKey 'dependabot' / 'workLint'); actions/secure/dependabot.ts:111-117. Scratch check with toolchain tsc 7.0.2 against the dist types: `check.ts(5,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'dependabot' does not exist in type 'CommandsConfig'.` (same for workLint). The spread form `commands: { deplint: {}, ...{ dependabot } }` typechecks.
findings.recommendation: State that `commands.dependabot` (and `commands.workLint`) work at runtime but are missing from the `XyConfig` `CommandsConfig` type through @ariestools/toolchain 10.1.1. 10.1.1 added `agentLint` and `updo` but not these two. In a typed `const config: XyConfig`, spread a hoisted object into `commands` alongside at least one typed key, e.g. `const dependabot = { rules: { 'dependabot.high': 'error' as const } }` and then `commands: { deplint: {}, ...{ dependabot } }`. File a toolchain fix that adds `dependabot?: { rules?: RuleLevelConfigMap }` and `workLint?: { rules?: RuleLevelConfigMap }` to CommandsConfig, then drop the workaround once that ships.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue is confirmed and still present in 10.1.1. 10.1.1 added `agentLint` and `updo` to CommandsConfig (XyConfig.ts:682-707 on main; dist/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.d.ts:626,649), but there is still no `dependabot` or `workLint` key. Both are read at runtime: RULE_COMMANDS.dependabot/workLint in lib/ruleCommandRegistry.ts, actions/secure/dependabot.ts:109-117 (loadWorkspaceCommandConfig with configKey 'dependabot'), and actions/ruleCatalog.ts:213-216 for workLint. I reproduced this with toolchain tsc 7.0.2 against the rebuilt 10.1.1 dist types in a scratch file. `commands: { dependabot: {...} }` gives `TS2353 ... 'dependabot' does not exist in type 'CommandsConfig'`, and the same error appears for workLint. The spread form `commands: { deplint: {}, ...{ dependabot } }` typechecks. `xy secure dependabot --rules` confirms the defaults (critical/high warn, medium/low off). Only the version label in the recommendation needs correcting: the gap exists in both 10.1.0 and 10.1.1.
verify.skill: confirmed: Still unresolved at 10.1.1. The diff 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91 added only agentLint and updo to CommandsConfig (XyConfig.ts:682-707). There is still no dependabot or workLint key, while ruleCommandRegistry.ts:54-56 and 131-133 register both and dependabot.ts:109-112 reads commands.dependabot at runtime. findings.title: Document experimental `compile.compiler: 'native'` / `nativePackage` and `xyex enable ts-native`
findings.current: absent: compilation.md covers `validator` (lines 84-93) but never mentions `compile.compiler` or `nativePackage`
findings.truth: `compile.compiler` is 'typescript' (the default) or 'native', which uses TypeScript 7 Go. It is an experimental config surface. `nativePackage` defaults to 'typescript-native', installed as the alias `npm:typescript@~7.0.2`. The supported setup is `xyex enable ts-native`, which adds the alias, sets the field, and clears a shared validator. `validator: 'shared'` with `compiler: 'native'` silently falls back to per-package validation. The flagship @ariestools/sdk-js sets `compiler: 'native'` in the root config and every package config, and 21 xy.config.ts files in the workspace use `compiler:`.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:142-157,171-177; xy/stability.ts:147-151 (id compile.compiler.native: 'Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`... public examples must not require it'); actions/package/compile/resolveTscBin.ts:22,29,34; actions/compile.ts:348-355 (shared+native → warn, per-package); `node dist/bin/xy.mjs enable --help` → "pnpm xy enable ts-native ... (experimental — prefer xyex)"; sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 and sdk-js/packages/*/xy.config.ts.
findings.recommendation: Add a "Compiler implementation (experimental)" subsection under Type validation. Cover: `compile.compiler: 'typescript' | 'native'` and `compile.nativePackage`. Enable with `pnpm xyex enable ts-native` rather than editing by hand. TS7 exports no compiler API. It cannot combine with `validator: 'shared'`, which falls back to per-package. It is listed under `xy --stability`. Do not require it in public examples. Because of the compile cascade rule, set it in every package config that exists.

verify.code: confirmed: Verified on 10.1.1. XyConfig.ts:142-157 defines `compiler?: CompilerImplementation` ('native' | 'typescript', default typescript; native is incompatible with a shared validator; prefer `xy enable ts-native`) and lines 171-177 define `nativePackage` (default 'typescript-native'). resolveTscBin.ts:15,22,29,34 sets the default alias spec `npm:typescript@~7.0.2`. xy/stability.ts EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_SURFACES lists id compile.compiler.native ('Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`... public examples must not require it'), and `xy --stability --json` prints it. resolveCompileValidator (actions/compile.ts:345-353) warns and falls back to per-package when shared is combined with native. `xy enable --help` shows '(experimental — prefer xyex)', and `xyex enable ts-native` exists. The skill never mentions `compiler`, `nativePackage`, `ts-native`, xyex or --stability (grep of skills/). Workspace count: 21 of 485 xy.config.ts files use `compiler:`. Medium/add is appropriate.
verify.skill: confirmed: Grepping all of skills/ finds no mention of `compiler`, `nativePackage`, `ts-native` or `xyex`. The only mention of experimental is the shared validator at compilation.md:90. Source at 10.1.1: XyConfig.ts:142-157 (compiler, which says prefer `xy enable ts-native`) and 171-177 (nativePackage, default typescript-native = npm:typescript@~7.0.2). stability.ts lists the EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_SURFACES entry compile.compiler.native ('Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`... public examples must not require it'). compile.ts resolveCompileValidator warns and falls back to per-package when shared and native are combined. The flagship sdk-js uses it in every config. Medium is right, and the recommendation correctly keeps it labelled experimental and ties it to the compile cascade rule from [0].

findings.title: entryMode semantics are wrong or incomplete (`auto` is a no-op alias of `single`; custom entries location; monolith rejects entryMode)
findings.current: compilation.md:58-64 "`single` targets the normal package entry... `platform` uses platform entry files. `custom` accepts explicit `{ in, out }` entries. `auto` lets the compiler derive the applicable shape."
findings.truth: buildEntries has no `auto` branch, so `auto` falls to the default `['index.ts']`, the same as `single`. `platform` means exactly `index-node.ts` + `index-browser.ts`. `custom` starts empty and uses only the per-target `entry` list (`compile.<node|browser|neutral>: { src: { entry: [...] } }`). That list takes string paths or `{in,out}`, and `{in,out}` throws unless entryMode is 'custom'. In other modes, `entry` items are appended to the defaults. `transpile` defaults entryMode to 'all'. Monolith mode throws if `compile.entryMode` is set. `compile.esbuild.options` is the esbuild passthrough, and `compile.tsup` is deprecated but still honored.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/buildEntries.ts:17-48; packageCompileEsbuild.ts:131-138 ("{in, out} entries require entryMode 'custom'"); resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts:90-93; packageCompileMonolith.ts:20-21 ('monolith mode computes entries; remove compile.entryMode'); resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:17 (`true` → `{ src: {} }`); XyConfig.ts:35,224-239,253-272. Usage: sdk-js/packages/crypto/xy.config.ts and packages/pixel/xy.config.ts (`entryMode: 'custom'` with `browser: { src: { entry: ['./index.ts', './model.ts'] } }`).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the entryMode list. `single` (default): `src/index.ts`. `all`: every source file except specs, stories and .d.ts (default for `transpile`). `platform`: `src/index-node.ts` + `src/index-browser.ts`. `custom`: only the `entry` array under `compile.<target>.src`, as strings or `{in,out}`. Say `auto` currently behaves like `single` and should not be used. Add that monolith rejects `entryMode`, and that extra `entry` items append in non-custom modes. Mention `compile.esbuild.options` for esbuild overrides, and `tsup` as deprecated.

verify.code: confirmed: buildEntries.ts:17-48 (unchanged in 10.1.1). The switch handles only 'platform' (['index-node.ts','index-browser.ts']), 'all' (all inputs minus spec/story and .d.ts), and 'custom' ([]). Everything else, including 'auto', falls to the default ['index.ts'], so `auto` is identical to `single`. Per-target `options.entry` is appended in every mode (lines 46-48). packageCompileEsbuild.ts:131-138 throws `{in, out} entries require entryMode 'custom'` in non-custom modes. resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts:90-93 makes transpile default to 'all'. packageCompileMonolith.ts:20-21 throws 'monolith mode computes entries; remove compile.entryMode'. XyConfig.ts:258 (`esbuild.options`) and 268-270 (`tsup` @deprecated, still honored) confirm the esbuild passthrough. compilation.md:64's 'auto lets the compiler derive the applicable shape' is false, and line 63 omits that custom also takes string entries from `compile.<target>.src.entry` (as sdk-js packages/crypto and pixel use).
verify.skill: confirmed: compilation.md:60-64 is wrong about `auto` and incomplete elsewhere. buildEntries.ts:25-44 has no 'auto' case, so it falls to default ['index.ts'], the same as single. platform is exactly index-node.ts plus index-browser.ts. custom starts empty and options.entry is appended in every mode (46-48). packageCompileEsbuild.ts createEsbuildEntryPoints throws "{in, out} entries require entryMode 'custom'". resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts resolveEffectiveEntryMode makes transpile default to 'all'. packageCompileMonolith.ts throws 'monolith mode computes entries; remove compile.entryMode'. In XyConfig.ts, esbuild.options is the passthrough and tsup is @deprecated. sdk-js crypto and pixel use `entryMode: 'custom'` with string `entry` arrays under the target `src`. Medium is proportionate.

findings.title: Stable command configs missing: commands.publint, apiExposure, license, packman
findings.current: absent: commands.md:129-131 (publint), 125-127 (api-exposure), 137-139 (license: 'against the configured allowlist') and 159 (packman) say nothing about how to configure them, and the 'Configuration and automation' example (293-317) shows only dead/deplint
findings.truth: `commands.publint` takes `{ include | exclude: <check names>, pack (default true), rules: { 'pub.<check>' | '<check>': level } }`. The `boolean` form is accepted by the type but ignored, because booleans normalize to `{}`. `commands.apiExposure` takes `packages[name].classification`, `peerForwarding` (default 'when-exposed'; 'always' or 'when-used'), `peerWithDefault`, `rules`, `thresholds` (39/79/119/179) and `treeShaking` (default true). It also feeds deplint under classifier aei/aei-next. `commands.license` takes `allow`, `allowOnly`, `deny` and `ignorePackages`. `commands.packman` takes `minimumReleaseAge` (default 1440 minutes) and `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`. The excludes are checked against imported scopes; the type's JSDoc default `["@xylabs/*","@xyo-network/*"]` is not what the lint enforces.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/PublintConfig.ts:6-23,79-105; actions/publint.ts:96-98 (typeof value === 'object' ? value : {}), 124 (pack ?? true); actions/package/compile/ApiExposureConfig.ts:13-19,26-43,49-58,93-121; actions/deplint/engine.ts:137; lib/licenseCheck/checkLicenses.ts:57-85; XyConfig.ts:566-581; lib/pnpmConfig/readMinReleaseAge.ts:12; actions/packman/lint.ts:41-46,216-234,342-347. Usage: publint in 12 and apiExposure in 6 workspace xy.config.ts files, e.g. sdk-js/xy.config.ts:5 (`apiExposure: { peerForwarding: 'when-used' }`) and XYOracleNetwork/plugins/packages/payloadset/xy.config.ts:13-27 (`apiExposure.packages.*.classification`, `publint.rules['pub.platform']: 'off'`).
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Command settings reference' table under Configuration and automation, with fields, defaults and a one-line example for each command. Rows: `publint` (`include` | `exclude` check names, `pack` default true, `rules` keyed `pub.<check>`); `apiExposure` (`packages[name].classification`, `peerForwarding` default 'when-exposed' | 'always' | 'when-used', `peerWithDefault`, `rules`, `thresholds` 39/79/119/179, `treeShaking` default true; also read by deplint under classifier aei/aei-next); `license` (`allow`, `allowOnly`, `deny`, `ignorePackages`); `packman` (`minimumReleaseAge` default 1440 min, `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`; the lint requires exactly the @ariestools/@xylabs/@xyo-network scopes the repo imports, whatever the type JSDoc says). Add an `updo` row for toolchain ≥10.1.1: `ignoreDeps`, exact package.json keys or positive globs like `@vendor/*`, where root and package lists add together. findings.title: `nodeTrack` ('current' | 'lts') for repoLint/nodeLint undocumented; repo.engines-lts errors by default
findings.current: absent: commands.md:160-161 describe `xy repo lint` (engines) and `xy node lint` (Volta pin) but give no configuration
findings.truth: `commands.repoLint.nodeTrack` and `commands.nodeLint.nodeTrack` choose which Node release `repo.engines-lts` and `node.volta-node-latest` compare against. The default is 'current'. `repo.engines-lts` is an error-level rule in `xy repo lint`, and therefore in `xy check`. A repo pinned to the LTS line fails unless both are set to 'lts'. Added 2026-09-16, after the skill's last edit.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:586-608; actions/package-lint.ts:306-307 (repoLintRule level = 'error'), 403-408 (repo.engines-lts uses nodeTrack); actions/package-lint-engines.ts:199 (result.errors.push); actions/node-lint.ts:172-175 (warn); `xy repo lint --rules` → `error │ repo.engines-lts`; docs/xy-config.md:47-56; git a2b5c6ea3 2026-09-16.
findings.recommendation: Under Repository policy, add this: repos that deliberately track Node LTS set `commands: { repoLint: { nodeTrack: 'lts' }, nodeLint: { nodeTrack: 'lts' } }`. With the default 'current' track, `repo.engines-lts` (error) fails when an `engines.node`/`engines.npm` range excludes the latest Current release. Both `repo.engines-lts` and `node.volta-node-latest` warn when `volta.node` is older than Current, which blocks CI under `--strict`. `xy node lint --fix` will bump an LTS `volta.node` pin to the latest Current release.

verify.code: adjusted: The undocumented surface is real. XyConfig RepoLintConfig/NodeLintConfig define `nodeTrack` ('current' default | 'lts'), repo.engines-lts is error level (`xy repo lint --rules`), and `xy check` includes repo lint. No workspace xy.config.ts sets nodeTrack, and the skill never mentions it. The failure claim is overstated, though. checkVersionsIncludeLts (actions/package-lint-engines.ts:176-224) pushes an error only when an `engines.<tool>` range excludes the track's latest version (line 198-201). An older `volta` pin is only a warning (lines 207-216), and warnings map to level 'warn' (package-lint.ts:300-302). node.volta-node-latest is warn level (node-lint.ts:170-176). So an LTS Volta pin with an open range like `>=24` does not fail `xy check` by default. It fails only under `--strict`, or when engines.node is upper-bounded (e.g. `^24`). There is also a hazard the finding missed: under the default track, `xy node lint --fix` rewrites root `volta.node` to the latest Current release (node-lint.ts:95-99). That matters more for LTS repos than the error does.

findings.title: Skills-lint config (`commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`, package.json `xy.skills`) missing, plus the cosmiconfig shadowing hazard
findings.current: commands.md:171 "Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills" and nothing else about configuration
findings.truth: `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills` adds required skills on top of the detected profile. Root and workspace lists are unioned, and unknown names are config errors. Packages can recommend skills through package.json `xy.skills` (`[{ name, source? }]`), enforced by the error-level `skills.package-recommended`. Hazard: cosmiconfig('xy') puts `package.json` first in its search places and reads its `xy` property as config. A package.json with an `xy` key therefore becomes that directory's entire xy config, and a sibling xy.config.ts (compile, commands) is silently ignored.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:634-647; actions/skills/packageSkills.ts:159-170; docs/xy-config.md:62-101; `xy skills lint --rules` → `error │ skills.package-recommended`; lib/loadConfig.ts:52-57 (cosmiconfig('xy') with default searchPlaces); node_modules/cosmiconfig@10.0.1 dist/defaults.js:5-28 ('package.json' first) and Explorer.js:115-121 (reads packageProp = moduleName). Empirical probe in scratch: dir containing package.json {"xy":{"skills":[...]}} plus xy.config.ts → search() returned filepath package.json, config {"skills":[...]}, and xy.config.ts was ignored. No current repo uses a top-level `xy` key, so the hazard is latent. Added 2026-09-08 (a4cd25cdc) and 2026-09-25 (881eede39).
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Skills lint configuration' subsection to commands.md (Skills and work tracking). Cover `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills` (adds required skills to the detected profile; root and workspace lists union; unknown names are config errors). Cover the toolchain 10.1.1+ field `commands.skillsLint.skills: { '<name>': { presence: 'required' | 'allowed' | 'off' } }`, which overrides the profile per skill (`allowed` suppresses `skills.unnecessary`, `off` drops a profile requirement), and `pnpm xy skills pick`, which installs from the catalog and writes that presence (non-TTY: `--skill <name>`). Cover package.json `xy.skills: [{ name, source? }]`, enforced by the error-level `skills.package-recommended`. Warn that a package.json `xy` key is read by cosmiconfig before xy.config.ts and becomes that directory's whole xy config, so do not put `xy.skills` in a package that has an xy.config.ts until the toolchain restricts searchPlaces. Raise that toolchain issue (exclude package.json from searchPlaces, or use a non-colliding packageProp).

findings.truth: In `bundle` mode `bundlePackages` defaults to `{ all: true }`. Vendor mode also takes `vendorDir` (default `_pkg`), `vendorBarrel` (`runtime` default src/index.ts, `model` default src/model.ts), `vendorSyncExports` (default true) and `vendorPackages.exclude` / `conditionalSubpaths`.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:98-133 (VendorPackagesConfig/VendorBarrelConfig), 136-140 (bundle default { all: true }), 201-216 (vendorBarrel, vendorDir default _pkg, vendorPackages, vendorSyncExports default true).
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence on the bundle default, and a small vendor field table with the defaults above. Keep the existing example.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked against 10.1.1 (toolchain main 812b27a91, `xy.mjs --version` prints 10.1.1). The bundle default is real: resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts:77 returns `{ all: true, ...bundlePackages }` when mode is 'bundle' and no all/workspace/scopes rule is set (hasBundlePackageRules, lines 42-47). XyConfig.ts:137-140 documents the same default. The vendor defaults are also real: packageCompileVendor.ts:55 sets `vendorDir ?? '_pkg'`, :58 sets `vendorBarrel ?? {}` and :61 sets `vendorSyncExports ?? true`. vendorCompileInternals.ts:109-110 defaults the barrels to runtime 'src/index.ts' and model 'src/model.ts'. vendorCompile.ts:95 reads `vendorPackages.exclude` and :124 reads `conditionalSubpaths`. The types are at XyConfig.ts:101-133 and 201-216. The skill matches the finding: compilation.md:76 names the bundlePackages controls with no default, and compilation.md:116-128 shows only scopes/selfScope. A grep of skills/ finds no vendorDir, vendorSyncExports, vendorBarrel, _pkg or `all: true`. The 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91 diff does not touch these fields.
verify.skill: confirmed: The gap is real and 10.1.1 does not change it. The only bundle mention in the whole skill is compilation.md:76, which lists the bundlePackages controls with no defaults. The vendor section (compilation.md:116-130) shows only scopes and selfScope. A grep of skills/ finds no vendorDir, vendorBarrel, vendorSyncExports, conditionalSubpaths or exclude. Source confirms every default, and `git diff 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91` shows no CompileConfig changes. The defaults live in: XyConfig.ts:98-133 and 135-140; packageCompileVendor.ts:55-61 (`vendorDir ?? '_pkg'`, `vendorBarrel ?? {}`, `vendorSyncExports ?? true`); vendorCompileInternals.ts:109-110 (runtime default src/index.ts, model default src/model.ts); vendorCompile.ts:95 and 124 (exclude, conditionalSubpaths). One detail for the wording: resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts:42-48 and 77 apply `{ all: true }` whenever no positive rule is set (all, workspace or scopes). So a bundle config that sets only `external` still bundles everything else. Low severity is right: these are optional fields with safe defaults.

findings.title: Typed but inert XyConfig fields (dev, liveShare, dynamicShare, bundleTypes, outDirAsBuildDir)
findings.current: absent
findings.truth: `dev.*` (`dev.build.*`, `dev.compile`), `liveShare`, `dynamicShare`, `compile.bundleTypes` and `compile.outDirAsBuildDir` appear in the XyConfig type, but no toolchain code reads them. Configs that rely on them are silently ignored. For example, XYOracleNetwork/xyo-chain/packages/cli puts its compile entry and esbuild `define` under `dev.compile`, so neither is applied.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:141,181,692-693,712-727; `grep -rn` over packages/toolchain/src for dev/liveShare/dynamicShare/bundleTypes/outDirAsBuildDir readers found no uses outside XyConfig.ts; XYOracleNetwork/xyo-chain/packages/cli/xy.config.ts:22-35 (dev.compile with tsup define); liveShare appears in 4 workspace xy.config.ts files.
findings.recommendation: In compilation.md under Configuration, add: "`dev` (including `dev.compile` and `dev.build.*`), `compile.bundleTypes` and `compile.outDirAsBuildDir` type-check but no xy command reads them. Put compile settings under `compile`." Add a separate sentence: "Top-level `liveShare` and `dynamicShare` are not read by xy either. They are pass-through settings for @xylabs/meta-server, which reads them from a build/xy.config.json that some apps generate with a `copy-config` script. Do not remove them as dead config." Optionally tell the xyo-chain owners that packages/cli/xy.config.ts sets its entry and esbuild `define` under the ignored `dev.compile`.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim holds. XyConfig.ts types bundleTypes (:141), outDirAsBuildDir (:181), dynamicShare and liveShare (:721-722 in 10.1.1; the cited 692-693 has shifted because 10.1.1 added agentLint) and `dev.{build,compile,verbose}` (:741-756). Grepping packages/*/src (non-dist, non-spec) finds no readers outside XyConfig.ts. The only `.dev` hits are fs.Stats device comparisons in actions/plan/lint.ts:81,349. lib/loadConfig.ts:90-93 only deep-merges the config and gives `dev` no special handling. The xyo-chain example is overstated, though. Its config does put `define` under dev.compile (xyo-chain packages/cli/xy.config.ts:22-34). But packages/cli/package.json maps package-compile to `pnpm package-compile-bundles` → `rolldown -c rolldown.config.mjs`, and rolldown.config.mjs:133-136 already sets `__VERSION__`/`__GIT_HASH__`. So that xy.config block is dead config, and the build is not broken. The liveShare count is right: 4 main checkouts, not counting .claude worktrees. Low severity fits.
verify.skill: adjusted: Real for `dev`, `compile.bundleTypes` and `compile.outDirAsBuildDir`. At 10.1.1 the only references in packages/toolchain/src are the type declarations: XyConfig.ts:141 and 181, and 741-756 (the `dev` block; the lines moved after the agent and updo config was added). Grepping for dev?., dev.build, dev.compile and destructured dev finds no readers; the only hits are fs-stat `.dev` in plan/lint.ts. build.ts does not read dev.build.* either. XYOracleNetwork/xyo-chain/packages/cli/xy.config.ts:22-34 does put its entry and define under `dev.compile`, so nothing applies them. However, the claim that `liveShare` and `dynamicShare` are silently ignored is wrong outside the toolchain. They are pass-through settings for @xylabs/meta-server: sdk-meta-server-nodejs/src/model/XyConfig.ts:52-63 types top-level liveShare and dynamicShare (marked deprecated in favor of metaServer.*), and liveShareHandlers.ts:61 loads them via loadXyConfig from build/xy.config.json. Apps produce that file from xy.config: XYOracleNetwork/app-explore.xyo.network-react/scripts/config.mjs:5-14 runs as `copy-config` in ci-build (package.json:13 and 16), and xylabs/web-xylabs.com-react has the same `copy-config` script (package.json:16). The proposed skill sentence would lead an agent to delete working liveShare config, so it must be split. Low severity and compilation.md (Configuration section) are still the right target.

findings.title: `any` escape hatch says a TODO comment is enough, but `any` is a lint error at every tier
findings.current: "5. **Only then: `any`** — with a `// TODO: [reason alternatives don't work]` comment explaining the constraint." (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17)
findings.truth: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` is `error` at every tier, type-checked or not, because it comes from typescript-eslint `flat/recommended`. Code that follows step 5 fails `xy lint` / `xy build` unless a disable directive is added. Workspace policy also says 'no `any` (use `unknown` + guards)'.
findings.evidence: Effective config computed via ESLint calculateConfigForFile on toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/index.ts with eslint-config-flat dist 10.1.0: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any error` at tier 0 (isTypeChecked false), tier 2, tier 3 and tier 4. Source: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:185-203 (scopes flatConfigs['flat/recommended'] and 'flat/recommended-type-checked', with no override for no-explicit-any). CLAUDE.md:45 says "no `any` (use `unknown` + guards)".
findings.recommendation: Rewrite step 5 to say `any` is lint-forbidden (`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` = error). The last resort becomes a scoped `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- <why unknown/generics/overloads fail>` on the single line, never a file-level disable. Keep the containment advice in lines 19-21.

verify.code: confirmed: I recomputed the effective config with ESLint 10.12.0 calculateConfigForFile against the rebuilt 10.1.1 eslint-config-flat dist (recommendedConfig at tiers 0, 0tc, 1tc, 2tc, 3, 3tc and 4tc). `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` is `error` at every tier, with or without type checking. The source is eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:182-197, which scopes flat/recommended and recommended-type-checked, and createCorrectnessOverride (lines 93-113) does not touch no-explicit-any. Nothing in eslint-config-flat/src changed between 7eb43c3c2 and 812b27a91. So step 5 in skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17 (`any` plus a TODO comment) fails `xy lint` and `xy build`. It also contradicts CLAUDE.md:45. One supporting detail: `unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable` is `error` at tier 2 and above, so a bare `eslint-disable` is rejected as well. The recommended rule-scoped next-line disable is the correct form.
verify.skill: confirmed: skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17 says step 5 is `any` "with a `// TODO: ...` comment". Nothing else in the skills mentions no-explicit-any or eslint-disable (grep across skills/). I recomputed the effective config with calculateConfigForFile against the eslint-config-flat dist (unchanged by 10.1.1: `git diff 7eb43c3c2..812b27a91` touches only its package.json). `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` is `error` at t0, t1tc, t2tc, t3, t3tc and t4tc. It comes from flat/recommended (src/typescript/index.ts:185-203) and nothing overrides it. Code that follows step 5 therefore fails `xy lint`. That matches the definition of high, and it also contradicts CLAUDE.md:45. findings.title: `xy lint init` is described as automatic; it is interactive and offers deprecated or nonexistent SDK barrels
findings.current: "It detects React, installs the applicable config package and ESLint, generates `eslint.config.ts`, includes repository `.gitignore` behavior when the file exists, and derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels." (eslint.md:22). Also "Add `configReactStorybook` explicitly only when Storybook files need that layer" (eslint.md:70) while eslint.md:28 says "Use the generator's output as canonical."
findings.truth: lint-init asks readline y/N questions: whether to replace an existing eslint.config.ts/.mjs, plus one question per barrel. The 7 offered barrels are @xylabs/sdk-js (deprecated, use @ariestools/sdk), @xylabs/sdk-react (deprecated, use @ariestools/sdk-react), @xyo-network/sdk-js (deprecated, use @xyo-network/sdk), @xyo-network/react-chain (npm E404), and three live @xyo-network barrels. @ariestools/sdk is not offered. Answering y to a barrel that is not installed adds it as a devDependency at 'latest' and runs install. The generator always adds `...configReactStorybook` for React repos, ignores `**/*.md`, and writes `eslint: '^10.0.0'`, which is below the config package peer `^10.3`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:60-68 (BARREL_DESCRIPTORS), :76-82 (eslint '^10.0.0'), :107-114 and :130 (React always imports and spreads configReactStorybook), :129 (ignores include '**/*.md'), :201-215 (ensureBarrelInstalled adds `latest` and installs), :244-253 (replace prompt), :262-268 (per-barrel prompts). `npm view @xylabs/sdk-js deprecated` returns 'Use @ariestools/sdk instead…'. `npm view @xylabs/sdk-react deprecated` returns 'Use @ariestools/sdk-react instead…'. `npm view @xyo-network/sdk-js deprecated` returns 'Use @xyo-network/sdk instead…'. `npm view @xyo-network/react-chain` returns E404. eslint-config-flat/package.json:71-73 sets peer eslint ^10.3.
findings.recommendation: State that `xy lint init` is interactive (replace prompt plus one y/N per barrel), so an agent must answer the prompts or run it where a human can. Tell agents to decline the deprecated @xylabs/* and @xyo-network/sdk-js barrels, since accepting installs them at `latest`, which conflicts with SKILL.md:12. Note that @ariestools/sdk barrel restrictions are not generated. Make line 70 match the generator, which always adds configReactStorybook for React (remove it if there are no stories), or say plainly that the generator differs from the README's opt-in stance. Raise the toolchain issue separately.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked against toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts at 10.1.1, which is unchanged since the baseline. askConfirmation (lines 21-29) uses readline for y/N questions. There is a replace prompt when eslint.config.ts or .mjs exists (lines 243-253), and one prompt per barrel (lines 262-268). BARREL_DESCRIPTORS (lines 60-68) lists @xylabs/sdk-js, @xylabs/sdk-react, @xyo-network/sdk-js, xl1-sdk, chain-sdk, react-chain and react-sdk, with no @ariestools/sdk. One detail to correct: React repos see all 7, but non-React repos see only the 4 'js' barrels (lines 84-90). ensureBarrelInstalled (lines 201-215) adds a missing barrel as `latest` and runs a real `pm install` through lib/shouldRunInstall.ts. React output always imports and spreads configReactStorybook (lines 107-114 and 130). Generated ignores include '**/*.md' (line 129), and eslint is set to '^10.0.0' (line 80) while the package peer is `^10.3` (eslint-config-flat/package.json). `xy lint init --help` shows no non-interactive or --yes flag. `npm view` today: @xylabs/sdk-js, @xylabs/sdk-react and @xyo-network/sdk-js are deprecated, @xyo-network/react-chain returns E404, and xl1-sdk, chain-sdk and react-sdk are live. eslint-config-react-flat/README.md:36 says Storybook is opt-in, which conflicts with the generator. SKILL.md:12 forbids installing retired @xylabs/* names.
verify.skill: confirmed: eslint.md:22 says lint init "derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels". lint-init.ts shows otherwise. It prompts to replace an existing config (:244-253) and asks y/N for each barrel (:262-268) through readline (repo-init/prompts.ts:5-18). findings.title: Tier severity description is stale after the unicorn v77 staging in 10.1.0
findings.current: "Tier 3 and 4 additions commonly begin as warnings. Use `pnpm xy lint --strict` … Use tier 4 for evaluation" (eslint.md:96). The table row reads "4 | Experimental/canary rules for migration testing" (eslint.md:94).
findings.truth: Moving from tier 2 to tier 3 turns 38 rules into errors (29 off→error, 9 warn→error) and adds only 22 new warnings. The errors include the unicorn opinionated preset, `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions`, `unicorn/filename-case`, and `workspaces/no-relative-imports` / `require-dependency`. Moving from tier 3 to tier 4 adds 68 warnings (unicorn v67/v69/v72) and promotes 22 unicorn v77 rules from warn to their upstream `error`. In 10.1.0 the v77 rules are off at tier 2, warn at tier 3, and error at tier 4.
findings.evidence: Computed with ESLint calculateConfigForFile against eslint-config-flat dist 10.1.0: tier 2→3 {"off->error":29,"warn->error":9,"off->warn":22}; tier 3→4 {"off->warn":68,"warn->error":22}. `unicorn/no-leading-empty-lines` and `unicorn/no-invalid-dom-token` are off/warn/error at tiers 2/3/4. Source: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/tier-builder.ts:87-110; src/tiers/opinionated.ts:72-77 (opinionated preset at 'error'), :134-148 (v77 warn at tier 3, unicornDefaultRules at tier 4); src/unicorn/index.ts:243-277 (v77 queue), :332-338 (default severity = recommended = 'error'). Commit a499070cc (2026-10-06), released in v10.1.0 (tag at 3320116a4).
findings.recommendation: Replace line 96 with an accurate summary. Tier 3 (the default) promotes a set of rules to errors, including strict-boolean-expressions, the opinionated unicorn preset, filename-case and the workspaces rules, and stages the newest unicorn rules (v77) as warnings. Tier 4 adds older queued unicorn rules as warnings and enables v77 rules at upstream error severity, so moving to tier 4 can fail lint without `--strict`. Point to `xy lint --analyze` to preview the impact before changing tier.

verify.code: confirmed: I recomputed the effective config from the 10.1.1 dist, and the eslint-config-flat src is unchanged since 10.1.0. Tier 2tc to 3tc gives 29 off→error, 9 warn→error, 22 off→warn, plus 1 error→off (no-extra-boolean-cast, which strict-boolean-expressions takes over). Tier 3tc to 4tc gives 68 off→warn and 22 warn→error, and all 22 are v77 unicorn rules (for example no-leading-empty-lines and no-invalid-dom-token are off, warn and error at tiers 2, 3 and 4). Source: tiers/tier-builder.ts opinionatedLayersForTier, where tier 3 pushes opinionatedUnicornV77LayerConfig and tier 4 pushes experimentalUnicornV77LayerConfig. In tiers/opinionated.ts, the v77 rules are 'warn' at tier 3, unicornDefaultRules applies at tier 4, and the preset is at 'error'. Commit a499070cc is an ancestor of the 10.1.0 deploy 3320116a4. `xy lint --help` lists `--analyze` ('runs ESLint at tier 4'). So 'Tier 3 and 4 additions commonly begin as warnings' (eslint.md:96) is misleading. Moving to tier 4 can fail without --strict.
verify.skill: confirmed: eslint.md:96 says 'Tier 3 and 4 additions commonly begin as warnings.' I recomputed severities at tiers 2, 3 and 4 with type checking. From tier 2 to 3: off->error 29, warn->error 9, off->warn 22, error->off 1. Tier 3 is mostly errors, including strict-boolean-expressions, unicorn/filename-case, workspaces/no-relative-imports and workspaces/require-dependency, member-ordering and prefer-export-from. From tier 3 to 4: off->warn 68, warn->error 22. The 22 are v77 unicorn rules such as unicorn/no-leading-empty-lines and no-invalid-dom-token (off at tier 2, warn at 3, error at 4). The cause is tier-builder.ts:87-110, where tier 3 adds opinionatedUnicornV77LayerConfig and tier 4 the experimental layers. eslint-config-flat src is unchanged in 10.1.1. The statement is materially wrong for the default tier, so medium fits. `xy lint --analyze` is already listed at eslint.md:120, so pointing to it fits.

findings.title: No list of the high-impact enforced rules agents hit when writing code
findings.current: absent. eslint.md:84-111 describes tiers and plugin families only, and skills/xy-development/typescript.md:5 defers lint-enforced opinions to ESLint.
findings.truth: At the default tier 3 with type checking, these rules are errors: strict-boolean-expressions (nullable string/number/boolean in conditions; this is why toolchain code writes `isVerbose === true`), no-explicit-any, consistent-type-definitions (interface), unicorn/import-style and prefer-node-protocol (`import PATH from 'node:path'`), unicorn/prefer-export-from, `no-restricted-imports` of `./index.ts` barrels and of another package's `src/`, complexity 18, max-depth 6, max-lines 512, max-statements 32, member-ordering (alphabetical), unicorn/filename-case (camel/kebab/pascal), workspaces/no-relative-imports and require-dependency, no-floating-promises, and no-misused-promises. These stay warnings: enum ban via no-restricted-syntax, consistent-type-imports (separate `import type`), simple-import-sort, @stylistic/max-len 200, and explicit-member-accessibility (no-public).
findings.evidence: Computed effective tier-3 config (calculateConfigForFile, eslint-config-flat dist 10.1.0) shows each severity listed. Source: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:46-58, 64-131, 149-152; src/rules/index.ts:8-56 (index.ts and src/ import bans); src/typescript/index.ts:117-170.
findings.recommendation: Add a short section, 'Rules you will hit at the default tier (3)'. List the stable errors with a one-line fix for each. strict-boolean-expressions: compare explicitly, e.g. `if (value !== undefined)` or `isVerbose === true`. no-explicit-any. consistent-type-definitions: use `interface`. unicorn/import-style and prefer-node-protocol: `import PATH from 'node:path'`. prefer-export-from. no-restricted-imports: no `./index.ts` barrels and no other package's `src/`. complexity 18, max-depth 6, max-lines 512 and max-statements 32: split functions and files. member-ordering. filename-case: camel, kebab or pascal. workspaces/no-relative-imports and require-dependency. no-floating-promises and no-misused-promises. Put consistent-type-imports (separate `import type`), simple-import-sort, @stylistic/max-len 200, explicit-member-accessibility (no-public) and the enum ban in a 'fix these too' list without stating their severity. The catalog intends them as tier-3 errors, but they currently resolve to warn because of `options ?? severity` in rule-catalog/index.ts:61, so a later fix will promote them. Tell agents to run `xy lint --rules` for current effective levels. Add one cross-reference sentence in skills/xy-development/typescript.md. Raise the managed-rules severity bug with the toolchain separately.

These are warnings: no-restricted-syntax (enum), consistent-type-imports (separate-type-imports), simple-import-sort/imports, @stylistic/max-len 200, and explicit-member-accessibility no-public. eslint.md:84-111 has no such list. verify.skill: adjusted: The gap is real. No skill mentions strict-boolean-expressions, max-lines, filename-case and so on (grep across skills/). The effective tier-3 type-checked config confirms these errors: complexity 18, max-depth 6, max-lines 512, max-statements 32, no-restricted-imports (./index.ts paths plus the `**/src/**` patterns), consistent-type-definitions, unicorn/import-style, prefer-node-protocol, prefer-export-from, filename-case (camel/kebab/pascal), member-ordering, the workspaces rules, no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises and no-explicit-any. The 'stays a warning' half is fragile, though. findings.title: Node types in non-node packages fail publint, but the skill frames it as advice with an escape clause
findings.current: "Keep browser and neutral packages free of Node types unless the source genuinely requires them. The compiler resolves platform-specific types when producing browser, neutral, and node targets." (typescript.md:82)
findings.truth: Compile does strip `node` from `types` for non-node platforms. Separately, `xy publint` (and therefore `xy build`) has a `platform` rule that is error by default. In a package with no node export target, it fails when the root tsconfig `compilerOptions.types` contains "node", when a portable export imports a Node builtin, or when its declarations expose Node ambient types. The 'unless the source genuinely requires them' clause leads to a failing build.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/platformPublint.ts:387-397 (collectTsconfigDiagnostics: skipped only when a node target exists), :434-436 (message 'non-node package tsconfig.json should not include compilerOptions.types "node"'), :459-463 (every diagnostic increments errors). src/actions/package/publintRules.ts:51 (`platform` is ERROR_BY_DEFAULT). src/actions/package/compile/resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 (compile-time stripping).
findings.recommendation: Replace typescript.md:82 with text along these lines. `xy publint` (run by `xy build`) has a `platform` rule that errors by default. A package with exports but no node export target must not list `node` in its root tsconfig `compilerOptions.types`. Separately, and even when a node target also exists, every browser or neutral export must not import `node:*` builtins and must not expose Node ambient types in its declarations. If the code really needs Node, make it a node target (`compile: { node: true }` in xy.config.ts, see compilation.md). Then `types: ["node"]` is allowed, and only the neutral or browser entry points must stay Node-free. Keep the note that compile strips `node` from `types` for non-node platforms.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim is correct at 10.1.1, since platformPublint.ts is unchanged. publint.ts:328 runs checkPlatform unless the rule is off. publintRules.ts puts 'platform' in ERROR_BY_DEFAULT_PUBLINT_RULES. checkPlatform increments `errors` for every diagnostic. collectTsconfigDiagnostics reports 'non-node package tsconfig.json should not include compilerOptions.types "node"' for a package with export targets but no node target. resolvePlatformTypes.ts strips 'node' for non-node compile platforms. Two details need correcting. First, the builtin-import and Node-ambient-type scans (shouldScanForNodeUsage, scanFileGraph) run on every browser or neutral export even when the package also has a node target. Only the tsconfig `types` check is skipped when a node target exists, or when there are no exports at all. Second, the recommendation's 'add a node export instead of adding types' is misleading: a node-targeted package still needs `types: ["node"]` (typescript.md:66-80), and having a node target is what makes that allowed.
verify.skill: confirmed: typescript.md:82 says 'Keep browser and neutral packages free of Node types unless the source genuinely requires them.' platformPublint.ts:387-397 checks the root tsconfig `compilerOptions.types` for 'node' in any package that has export targets but no node target and is not node-only. :434-436 renders the 'non-node package tsconfig.json should not include compilerOptions.types "node"' diagnostic, and :459-463 counts every platform diagnostic as an error. Node-builtin imports and node-ambient-type leaks are also errors. publintRules.ts:51 makes `platform` error by default. The 'unless the source genuinely requires them' escape clause therefore leads to a failing `xy publint`/`xy build`. The right path is a node export target via `compile.node: true`, which compilation.md:48 and project-profiles.md:45 already describe. 10.1.1 does not touch platformPublint.ts. Medium, as filed, is proportionate because only the escape-clause path fails.

findings.title: Install command pulls TypeScript 7, which the toolchain does not support

findings.truth: `typescript@latest` on npm is now 7.0.2, the Go native compiler, which exports no compiler API. @ariestools/toolchain peers on `typescript: ^5.9 || ^6.0`, and ESLint, deplint, dead and api-exposure all load the API from `typescript`. The toolchain's own scaffold pins `typescript: ~6.0.3`, and `xy updo` will not offer a 6→7 bump. TS7 is supported only side by side, as `typescript-native: npm:typescript@~7.0.2` plus `compile.compiler: 'native'` (`xyex enable ts-native`, experimental).

Commit c2b9db449 (2026-08-10, v9.0.0). toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:48 "typescript": "~6.0.3". toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/enable/tsNative.ts:144-147.

findings.title: New-project baseline misses the policy gates `xy check` enforces
findings.current: toolchain.md:110-124: 'Require Node.js 22 or newer', install packages, `type: module`, configs, `xy lint init`; toolchain.md:124 'Use `xy repo init cli` only after inspecting its generated output and passing an explicit scope.'; toolchain.md:96-104 root scripts use `"test": "vitest run"`.
findings.truth:
A baseline that passes `xy check` also needs:
- Node via root `volta` only, with no `engines` on the root or private packages, and libraries declaring an open range such as `>=22` that includes current Node (26.x). A capped range like `^22` is an error.
- root `private: true`.
- pnpm `minimumReleaseAge`, `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` (packman lint, error).
- a README.md in every package.
- `.xy/cache` ignored in every package.
Since 9.2.0, `xy repo init` is interactive when the template is omitted, defaults to scope @ariestools, MIT and pnpm, and takes --pm, --monorepo, --react, --skills-tier and -y. Its root scripts are build, compile, lint, fix, test and check, all via xy ("test": "xy test").
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs repo lint --rules`, `xy.mjs packman lint --rules`, `xy.mjs git lint --rules` (git.ignore-toolchain-cache). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint-engines.ts:71-87, 194-202. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/latestVersions (nodeCurrent 26.8.2). `xy.mjs repo init --help`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl scripts block. toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:58.
findings.recommendation: Extend the baseline checklist and split it by topology. All repos: pin pnpm and set pnpm minimumReleaseAge, minimumReleaseAgeExclude and verifyDepsBeforeRun (packman lint errors). Run `pnpm xy agent init` (stable, 10.1.1) for a root AGENTS.md with the required sections, and keep CLAUDE.md as a bare `@AGENTS.md` import, because `xy check` now runs agent lint. Ignore `.xy/cache` (git lint warning). Monorepos only, since repo lint skips single-package repos: root `private: true`; Node pinned via root `volta` only; no `engines` on the root or private packages; libraries declare an open `engines.node` such as `>=22` that includes the current Node track (set `nodeTrack: 'lts'` for LTS repos); a README.md in every workspace package, listed in `files` for publishable ones. End with `pnpm xy check --fix`, then `pnpm xy check`. Update the repo-init sentence with the real defaults (@ariestools scope, MIT, pnpm, interactive when the template is omitted) and flags (--scope, --pm, --monorepo, --react, --skills-tier, -y), and keep the advice to inspect the output and pass an explicit scope. Align the root-scripts example with the scaffold: build, compile, lint, fix, `test: xy test`, check.

verify.code:
adjusted: The core gap is real. toolchain.md:110-124 has no policy-gate items, toolchain.md:103 has `test: vitest run`, and the repo-init sentence is stale. `xy.mjs repo init --help` shows the interactive wizard, --scope (default @ariestools), --license (default MIT), --pm (default pnpm), --monorepo, --react, --skills-tier and -y. The template scripts are build, compile, lint, fix, test and check, all via xy. Three details need correcting.

(1) Repo lint runs only in monorepos: packageLintMonorepo returns early with 'Not a monorepo — skipping repo lint checks' (package-lint.ts:534-537). repo init also sets `private` only for monorepos (templateVars.ts:125, rootPrivate: monorepo ? 'true' : 'false'). So an unqualified 'root private: true / no root engines' would be wrong for a single-package published library.

(2) git.ignore-toolchain-cache is warn, not error (`xy.mjs git lint --rules`), so it does not block `xy check` without --strict.

(3) 10.1.1 changes the fix. Commit 8f2768dfd (tagged v10.1.1) adds agent lint to `xy check` (checkCommand.ts:14, 49-50) with no opt-in gate (actions/agent/lint.ts:14-26). Its error rules include agents.file-present, agents.required-sections, agents.links-resolve, agents.adapter-thin and agents.no-absolute-paths. A new repo without a conforming AGENTS.md therefore now fails `xy check`.
verify.skill: adjusted: The baseline gaps are real. toolchain.md:110-124 omits volta/engines placement, release-age settings and package READMEs. toolchain.md:103 uses `"test": "vitest run"`, while the scaffold uses `xy test` (package.json.tmpl:28-35). `repo init --help` confirms the interactive mode, the @ariestools/MIT/pnpm defaults and --pm/--monorepo/--react/--skills-tier/-y. The recommendation needs two corrections. (1) Repo lint is skipped for non-monorepos (package-lint.ts:534-537 prints 'Not a monorepo — skipping repo lint checks'). 'root private: true', 'no engines on root' and 'README per workspace package' are therefore monorepo requirements; applied to a single-package library, `private: true` would block publishing. Also, git.ignore-toolchain-cache is a warn, not an error. (2) 10.1.1 changes what `xy check` requires. Commit 8f2768dfd adds `agent lint` to `xy check` (checkCommand.ts diff) and makes `agent` stable. Its error rules agents.file-present, agents.required-sections and agents.adapter-thin are not --fix-able. A new repo therefore needs a root AGENTS.md with orient/authority/map/commands/failures sections and a CLAUDE.md that is only an @AGENTS.md import or a symlink, or `xy check` fails. The skill's caution about inspecting repo-init output and passing an explicit scope is still valid, because the default scope is @ariestools.

findings.recommendation:
Add a short 'Releasing (owner-directed)' subsection to skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md:

findings.title: zod is described as optional, but importing the root barrel or the hex/object/zod subpaths fails without it
findings.current: overview.md:40 "`zod` | **Optional peer** — install only if you use zod helpers (`@ariestools/sdk/zod`, hex zod helpers, etc.)"; overview.md:25 shows the root-barrel import `import { assertEx, delay, exists, fetchJson } from '@ariestools/sdk'` without that caveat; overview.md:43-45 "# Only if you use zod helpers from the SDK / pnpm add zod".
findings.truth: package.json does mark zod as an optional peer. However, the published 9.0.1 dist imports it with static top-level ESM imports in the root barrel (`dist/{neutral,node,browser}/index.mjs`) and in `dist/neutral/hex.mjs`, `object.mjs` and `zod.mjs`. Importing `@ariestools/sdk`, `/hex`, `/object` or `/zod` without zod installed therefore throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, even if the code never calls a zod helper. Subpaths such as `/assert`, `/fetch` and `/telemetry` load without zod. The sdk README repeats the same wrong claim (sdk-js packages/sdk/README.md:234).
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json:404-410 (zod peer optional). `grep -nE '^import .*zod' dist/neutral/hex.mjs` -> line 2 `import * as z from "zod/mini"`; dist/neutral/index.mjs:988,1010,... `import * as z from "zod/mini"`; dist/neutral/object.mjs:186,189; dist/neutral/zod.mjs:2. The installed 9.0.1 copy (sdk-react/node_modules/@ariestools/sdk) also has 9 zod/mini imports in index.mjs and 8 in hex.mjs. Runtime check in a scratch dir with sdk 9.0.1 + async-mutex + @ariestools/telemetry + @opentelemetry/api but no zod, run with `node --preserve-symlinks --input-type=module -e "await import(spec)"`: `@ariestools/sdk` -> "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'zod' imported from .../@ariestools/sdk/dist/node/index.mjs"; `/hex`, `/object`, `/zod` -> ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; `/assert`, `/fetch`, `/telemetry` -> ok. Source: src/modules/hex/zod.ts:1 and hex/address/*, hex/hash/*, object/JsonObject.ts import zod.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the zod row as: "`zod` — declared an optional peer, but in practice required whenever you import the root barrel `@ariestools/sdk`, or `@ariestools/sdk/hex`, `/object` or `/zod`. Only consumers who use zod-free subpaths exclusively (for example `/assert`, `/delay`, `/fetch`, `/promise`) can omit it." Change the install snippet comment to match, and add a note under the root-barrel example at line 25 that the root import requires zod.

findings.title: fetchJson example treats the return value as the DTO, but it is a FetchJsonResponse wrapper
findings.current: fetch.md:22 "const data = await fetchJson<MyDto>('https://api.example.com/item')"
findings.truth: `fetchJson<T>` returns `Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>`, an object `{ data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }`, not `T`. `data` can be null, including for non-2xx responses with malformed JSON.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:31 `export async function fetchJson<T>(url: string, options: FetchJsonOptions = {}): Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>`; src/modules/fetch/types.ts:10-21 (FetchJsonResponse fields; `data: T | null`). README.md (packages/sdk) lines ~172-175: "Non-2xx malformed JSON still produces `data: null`".
findings.recommendation: Change the example to `const { data, status } = await fetchJson<MyDto>(url)` and add a line explaining that `data` is `MyDto | null`, so callers must check `status` and null before use. Also say that `fetchJson` does not throw on non-2xx responses, while `FetchClient`/`FetchJsonClient` throw `FetchClientError` (a FetchError of type 'http-status') unless `validateStatus` allows the status.

verify.code: confirmed: src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:31 returns Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>, and types.ts:10-21 defines { data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }. fetchJson never checks status. For non-2xx it calls tryParseJson (malformed body gives null, as in README 'Non-2xx malformed JSON still produces data: null'). For 2xx, parseJsonResponse (parseJson.ts:28-57) returns null on an empty body and throws a 'parse' FetchError on malformed JSON. FetchClient throws FetchClientError (type 'http-status') when validateStatus rejects (FetchClient.ts:15-20, 34-57). So fetch.md:22 `const data = await fetchJson<MyDto>(...)` mislabels the wrapper as the DTO. The recommendation is accurate; it could also note that a malformed 2xx body throws a parse FetchError.
verify.skill: confirmed: fetch.md:22 assigns `const data = await fetchJson<MyDto>(...)`. src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:31 returns Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>, and types.ts:10-21 defines `{ data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }`. fetchJson.ts:43-45 uses tryParseJson for non-ok responses, so it does not throw on non-2xx. findings.title: retry example hides that retry defaults to 0 retries and does not retry on thrown errors
findings.current: modules.md:79 "await retry(async () => doWork(), { /* options per package API */ })"
findings.truth: `retry(func, config?)` retries only when `complete(result)` is false; by default that means the result is `undefined`. The defaults are `retries = 0` (no retries), `interval = 100` and `backoff = 2`. There is no try/catch, so a thrown error propagates immediately with no retry. When retries run out it resolves `undefined` instead of throwing.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/retry/retry.ts:5-12 (RetryConfig with defaults documented: backoff 2, interval 100, retries 0), :15-18 (`complete`), :26-41 (implementation: `const result = await func()` with no catch; returns undefined when retries <= 0).
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with `const value = await retry(() => tryFetchOrUndefined(), { retries: 3, interval: 100, backoff: 2 })`. Add a note: retries happen on `undefined` (or on a custom `complete` returning false), not on exceptions, so wrap a throwing call to return `undefined`. The result is `T | undefined` once retries run out, and the default is 0 retries.

verify.code: confirmed: src/modules/retry/retry.ts:5-12 documents the defaults backoff 2, interval 100 and retries 0 (no retries). Line 28 sets the default `complete` to `value !== undefined`. Lines 30-36 run `await func()` with no try/catch and return undefined when retries <= 0, so a thrown error propagates immediately and an exhausted retry resolves undefined. modules.md:79 uses a placeholder options object and a doWork() that returns void, so it would never retry. The recommendation is accurate.
verify.skill: confirmed: modules.md:79 is only a placeholder: `retry(async () => doWork(), { /* options per package API */ })`. retry.ts:26-40 shows the actual behavior. The defaults are retries=0, interval=100 and backoff=2, and completion defaults to `value !== undefined`. There is no try/catch, so a thrown error propagates without a retry. When retries run out, the function returns undefined. An agent copying the example with defaults gets no retries and no retry on exceptions, a common wrong assumption. Medium is fine, and the recommended example and note are correct.
