findings.title: Fetcher-injection example spreads a Headers instance and silently drops the SDK's Accept/Content-Type/Content-Encoding headers
findings.current: fetch.md:39-40 `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) => globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers: { ...init?.headers, authorization: token } })`
findings.truth: fetchJson and FetchClient always pass `init.headers` to the fetcher as a `Headers` instance, built by buildHeaders(). fetchCompress also creates `new Headers(init.headers)` and sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` when a body exceeds compressMinLength (1024). Object-spreading a Headers object yields `{}`. The skill's wrapper therefore sends only `authorization`. JSON requests lose Content-Type/Accept, and gzip-compressed bodies arrive without Content-Encoding, so servers receive bodies they cannot decode.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:9-20 (buildHeaders returns new Headers()), :40; FetchClient.ts:60-71, :174; fetchCompress.ts:49 (compressMinLength = 1024), :57-63 (new Headers + Content-Encoding: gzip). Command: `node -e "const h=new Headers({'content-type':'application/json',accept:'x'}); console.log(JSON.stringify({...h, authorization:'t'}))"` -> `{"authorization":"t"}`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with a Headers-safe merge, for example: `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) => { const headers = new Headers(init?.headers); headers.set('authorization', token); return globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers }) }`. Add a note that init.headers is a Headers object and that injected fetchers must forward `signal`.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked. fetchJson.ts:9-20 builds a `new Headers()`, and :40 passes it into fetchCompress. FetchClient.ts:60-71 does the same, and :174 sets it on init. fetchCompress.ts:47-68 forwards init.headers, still a Headers instance, to the injected fetcher. On the gzip path (:57-63, default compressMinLength 1024 at :49) it builds a new Headers with Content-Encoding: gzip. Running `node -e "const h=new Headers({'content-type':'application/json',accept:'x'}); console.log(JSON.stringify({...h, authorization:'t'}))"` on Node 26.9.0 prints {"authorization":"t"}. So the fetch.md:39-40 wrapper drops Accept and Content-Type. For bodies over 1024 chars, which FetchClient.post gzips by default, it also drops Content-Encoding. The skill example therefore produces broken requests.
verify.skill: confirmed: fetch.md:39-40 spreads `init?.headers` into an object literal. Both fetchJson (fetchJson.ts:9-20 buildHeaders returns `new Headers()`, passed at :40) and FetchClient (FetchClient.ts:60-71, :174) always pass a Headers instance to the fetcher. fetchCompress.ts:57-63 also replaces the headers with `new Headers(init.headers)` plus `Content-Encoding: gzip` for bodies over 1024 characters (:49). Running `node -e "const h=new Headers({'content-type':'application/json',accept:'x'}); console.log(JSON.stringify({...h, authorization:'t'}))"` prints `{"authorization":"t"}`. The documented wrapper therefore drops Accept, Content-Type and Content-Encoding. It still type-checks, so the failure is silent and the server receives gzip bodies it cannot decode. High severity is proportionate, and the Headers-based merge in the recommendation is correct.

findings.title: fetchJson returns a {data,status,...} envelope and does not throw on non-2xx; FetchClient throws FetchClientError. The skill implies neither
findings.current: fetch.md:22 `const data = await fetchJson<MyDto>('https://api.example.com/item')`; fetch.md:24-25 FetchClient get; fetch.md:28-30 lists helpers and error classes with no result or throw semantics
findings.truth: fetchJson and the fetchJsonGet/Post/Put/Patch/Delete helpers resolve to `FetchJsonResponse<T>` = { data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }. They do NOT throw on HTTP error statuses: non-2xx bodies are best-effort parsed (malformed gives data: null). Empty bodies give data: null. FetchClient and FetchJsonClient (plus the `fetchJsonClient` singleton) return the same envelope but throw `FetchClientError` (a FetchError of type 'http-status' that carries `config`) when `validateStatus` rejects. The default accepts 2xx and `validateStatus: null` disables the check. Transport and parse failures throw FetchError (types: timeout, aborted, http-status, parse, response-too-large, network).
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/types.ts:10-21 (FetchJsonResponse); fetchJson.ts:31,43-53 (non-ok -> tryParseJson, returns envelope); parseJson.ts:60-82 (tryParseJson returns null on malformed); methods.ts:7-40; FetchClient.ts:17-21 (validateStatus doc), :39-58 (FetchClientError), :197-205 (default 2xx check, throw); FetchJsonClient.ts (subclass + `fetchJsonClient` singleton); FetchError.ts:19-31 (FetchErrorType union).
findings.recommendation: Change the example to `const { data, status } = await fetchJson<MyDto>(url)` and add a short 'Result and error semantics' section: fetchJson* returns the envelope and does not throw on 4xx/5xx (check `status`/`response.ok`); FetchClient/FetchJsonClient throw FetchClientError unless validateStatus allows the status; list the FetchErrorType values and FetchClientError/isFetchError usage.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked. types.ts:10-21 defines FetchJsonResponse<T> = { data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }. fetchJson.ts:43-53 returns that envelope. For non-ok responses it calls tryParseJson, which never throws for an HTTP status: parseJson.ts:65-82 returns null on malformed or empty bodies and rethrows only when a byte cap or signal is set and the read fails. methods.ts:7-42 wraps fetchJson. FetchClient.ts:197-211 applies the default 2xx validateStatus, and `null` disables it (:21, :201). On rejection it throws FetchClientError, which is a FetchError of type 'http-status' carrying config (:39-58). FetchJsonClient.ts subclasses FetchClient and exports the fetchJsonClient singleton. FetchError.ts:19-32 defines the FetchErrorType union. That union also includes dns, connection-refused, connection-reset, connection-timeout, tls, unreachable and unknown, so a list in the skill should be complete or point to the type. fetch.md:22 names the envelope `data`, which tells the reader fetchJson returns MyDto, and the skill never says that 4xx/5xx do not throw for fetchJson* but do throw for FetchClient.
verify.skill: confirmed: fetch.md:22 assigns the fetchJson result to `data`. In fact fetchJson.ts:31 returns `Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>`, an envelope of { data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText } (types.ts:10-21). Non-ok responses go through tryParseJson (fetchJson.ts:43-45), which returns null on malformed or unreadable bodies when no cap or signal is set (parseJson.ts:65-81), so nothing is thrown on 4xx/5xx. FetchClient throws FetchClientError, a FetchError of type 'http-status', when validateStatus rejects; the default is 2xx and null disables the check (FetchClient.ts:17-21, :39-58, :197-211). FetchJsonClient and the fetchJsonClient singleton subclass it (FetchJsonClient.ts:15-31). fetch.md says nothing about these result or throw semantics anywhere. Code that follows the example either fails to type-check (`data.field` on the envelope) or silently treats error bodies as success, so high severity is reasonable. When listing the error types, use the full FetchErrorType union from FetchError.ts:19-32 (it also includes dns, connection-*, tls, unreachable and unknown).

findings.title: Bounded/cancellable response reads (8.2.0) and the non-stream body fallback (9.0.1) are not covered
findings.current: absent. fetch.md:1-117 covers only fetcher resolution and Undici caching; no mention of maxResponseBytes, timeout, signal, readResponseText, FetchJsonClient options or response-too-large
findings.truth: 8.2.0 (b86f3a024, 2026-08-27) added `maxResponseBytes`, a positive safe integer validated before the request and applied to 2xx and non-2xx bodies. It also added client `timeout`, composed with the caller `signal` through body consumption (first abort wins), the `response-too-large` FetchError type, and the public `readResponseText(response, { maxResponseBytes, signal })` with `ReadResponseTextOptions` in `@ariestools/sdk/fetch/model`. With a cap or signal set, non-2xx read errors propagate instead of resolving to null. 9.0.1 (158476cd7, 2026-09-18) changed bodies that are not WHATWG streams (node-fetch/cross-fetch Readable, React Native whatwg-fetch, test doubles) to fall back to `response.text()`. Abort still rejects promptly, but the body cannot be cancelled, and the cap is checked after buffering against UTF-8 byte length. Before this fix these cases threw `body.getReader is not a function`.

findings.title: crypto-auth API, versioned PBKDF2 and native-base64 runtime constraint are undocumented
findings.current: packages.md:83-91 "Self-contained password and seed-phrase encryption/decryption (vault-style crypto)." plus an install line and a note about logging secrets
findings.truth: Since 8.1.5 and 8.1.6 (2026-07-22 to 07-27), the package exposes `SeedPhraseVault(store: SeedPhraseStore, walletKind?, crypto: VaultCrypto = defaultVaultCrypto)`, with the storage and crypto backend both injected. Key methods: addSelfDescribingPhrase (returns { key, record }), openSeedPhrase, verifyPasswordForRecord, upgradeRecordKdf, deriveKeyForRecord, static recordNeedsRehash/resolveRecordKdf, plus `SeedPhraseDecryptError`. Supporting exports: `Pbkdf2AesGcmVaultCrypto`, `PasswordKey`, deriveKeyFromPassword/deriveKeyFromValues/deriveKeyAndValues/verifyPassword/needsRehash, encryptSeedPhrase/decryptSeedPhrase, and bytesToBase64/base64ToBytes. Records are self-describing (salt + keyMetadata { algorithm: 'PBKDF2', params.iterations }). New keys use DEFAULT_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 600_000, legacy records without metadata are read at LEGACY_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 100_000, and keys are non-extractable. findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:56 "Rewrite an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email (keeping its tree, parents, message, and dates); ask before force-pushing one that is already pushed." XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills/CLAUDE.md:65-74 (same merge policy and rationale).
findings.recommendation: Keep the append-only principle and its rationale, and add one carve-out: "Exception: when repo or workspace instructions explicitly require it (for example, correcting commit identity), you may rewrite an unpushed local commit while keeping its tree, parents, message and dates. Never force-push a shared branch (main/develop), and ask before force-pushing anything already pushed." Optionally note that squash merges done by the hosting platform under the repo's merge policy are not covered by this rule.

(2) The finding cites xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:65-74 but leaves out xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:62, which still says "Never rewrite git history (no amend, rebase, or force push)". ESLint does not enforce this (explicit-module-boundary-types is off; explicit-function-return-type is unset), so it is exactly the kind of rule a linter can't catch, which this file exists to cover. findings.title: Workspace style conventions that no linter enforces are missing
findings.current: typescript.md:86 covers only "PascalCase for types and interfaces, camelCase for variables and functions". Named exports, function style, boolean prefixes, file naming and Node built-in imports are absent.
findings.truth: The workspace requires these, and none are enforced by an ESLint rule: named exports over default; `function` declarations at top level with arrows only for callbacks; booleans prefixed is/has/should/can; camelCase module files and PascalCase component or class files; Node built-ins imported via `node:` with a default import (`import PATH from 'node:path'`); no `import * as X`. The toolchain itself renamed its `typeChecked` option to `isTypeChecked`, applying the boolean-prefix rule to its own public API.

Default exports are allowed only where a tool requires them: eslint.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, Storybook *.stories.tsx. Also add: top-level `function` declarations with arrows only for callbacks; boolean names prefixed is/has/should/can; module files in camelCase and component or class files in PascalCase (lint accepts camel, kebab and pascal); `node:`-prefixed built-ins with a default import for path-style modules (`import PATH from 'node:path'`, lint-backed by unicorn/prefer-node-protocol and unicorn/import-style); no `import * as X`. Mark which items are lint-backed (filename-case, prefer-node-protocol, import-style) and which are review-only. findings.title: Advice to add dependencies at the 'latest published version' ignores the repos' pnpm supply-chain policy and tilde-range convention

findings.title: Advice to pass an explicit stable work-item id cannot be followed from the CLI
findings.current: auditing.md:102 "Use a deterministic id. createWorkId embeds today's date... Pass an explicit stable id derived from the check and the path, and check existence before adding."
findings.truth: `xy work add` has no --id flag. Its options are description, area, tag, file, line, inline, acceptance, verify, impact, urgency, effort, risk, confidence and the workspace flags. workAdd() accepts `options.id` only as an internal API, and the command handler never passes it, so every CLI-created item gets `<PREFIX>-<YYYYMMDD>-<random>`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/work/addCommand.ts:12-105 (no 'id' option; handler at :85-104 does not pass id). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/index.ts:171 `const id = options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`. id.ts:19-35. Command: `xy.mjs work add --help` lists no --id.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bullet. Since ids cannot be chosen from the CLI, dedupe by content: before adding, search existing items (`xyex work list --json`, or read .xy/work/items/*.json) for a stable key placed in the title or a tag (for example `--tag audit:<check>:<path>`), and update the existing item rather than adding a new one. Add an explicit --id only after the toolchain ships one (track it as a toolchain work item).

The handler (about lines 85-104) never passes `id`, and `xy.mjs work add --help` lists no --id. actions/work/index.ts:171 `options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`, and id.ts:19-35 builds PREFIX-YYYYMMDD-<random 3-byte hex>, so ids differ even within the same day. The yargs builder sets no strict options, so a `--id` an agent adds is silently ignored and creates a duplicate. findings.title: Hand-run audit scripts miss Markdown links and top-level docs, giving false negatives and false positives
findings.current: auditing.md:58-60: the link check greps only backtick code spans (`` `...\.(md|json|ts...)` ``). auditing.md:76-79: the orphan scan iterates `git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'`.
findings.truth: (1) The link check ignores Markdown links, which are exactly what the toolchain convention requires (plan.root.docs-index). It also resolves package-relative prose paths against the repo root, producing false MISSING results. (2) Without `:(glob)` magic, git pathspec `docs/**/*.md` needs an extra path segment and silently skips every top-level docs/*.md file.
findings.evidence: Command in toolchain: the code-span grep finds only CLAUDE.md, packages/toolchain/src/bin/xy.ts, packages/toolchain/src/xy/stability.ts and src/bin/xyex.ts, and reports "MISSING src/bin/xyex.ts" (a false positive: the path is relative to packages/toolchain). All 9 Markdown link targets in toolchain/AGENTS.md (./docs/README.md, ./papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md, ...) go unchecked. `git -C toolchain ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'` returns 0 files, while `':(glob)docs/**/*.md'` returns docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md and the rest. In crypto-cards, `'docs/**/*.md'` returns 331 files against 560 with `:(glob)`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hand-run block with `pnpm xy agent lint` (stable in 10.1.1; also run by `xy check`; `--rules`, `--json`, `--strict`, `--fix`) and `pnpm xy agent audit` for stale, orphaned, superseded and mutable-evidence documents. Keep a hand-run fallback only for toolchains older than 10.1.1, with both bugs fixed: (1) extract Markdown link targets (`grep -oE '\]\([^)#]+' AGENTS.md | sed 's/^](//'`), resolve them relative to the file, and keep the code-span grep secondary; (2) change the orphan scan to `git ls-files ':(glob)docs/**/*.md'` (or `'docs/*.md'`). Note that `agents.links-resolve` checks Markdown links only, not backtick paths, so the skill's 'Every path and link resolves' row should say so.

The 9 unique Markdown link targets in AGENTS.md go unchecked. `git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'` returns 0, while `':(glob)docs/**/*.md'` and `'docs/*.md'` each return 11. findings.title: Moving AGENTS.md overflow into .claude/rules/ makes it Claude-only, contradicting "AGENTS.md is canonical"
findings.current: agents-md.md:88-94 tells agents to move over-budget content to ".claude/rules/*.md with paths: frontmatter". The 200-line budget (agents-md.md:84-86) is framed only in Claude terms.
findings.truth: Codex and Copilot do not read .claude/rules/. Copilot's equivalent is .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with `applyTo`. Codex has no path-scoped mechanism and caps combined AGENTS.md content at 32 KiB. The Claude claims themselves check out: target under 200 lines, path rules load on Read/Write/Edit of matching files, and block HTML comments are stripped.
findings.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file"; "Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude uses the Read, Write, or Edit tool on a file matching the pattern"; "Block-level HTML comments... are stripped". https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions (applyTo). https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md (project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB default).
findings.recommendation: Add a caveat: content moved to .claude/rules/ is invisible to other agents. Across workspace repos, webble, lifehash, service-kit, xyo-chain and others use <PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md, while only toolchain and one other repo use WHITE-PAPER.md. findings.title: Layer 1's root-barrel import rule contradicts ariestools-sdk's subpath guidance and relies on a downstream XYO pack
findings.current: typescript.md:64-78 tells agents to "Import from the root barrel package of each monorepo… Avoid — importing from sub-packages", with an `@xyo-network/sdk` example and "See the XYO and XL1 knowledge skills for the specific root barrel packages."

findings.evidence: xy-development/typescript.md:64-78; ariestools-sdk/overview.md:22-29, conventions.md:5-8,17; toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:56-67.

Where an SDK's own skill says otherwise (for example, deprecated umbrella re-exports), follow that skill.' Replace the @xyo-network example with a generic @scope/sdk and drop the XYO/XL1 pointer. These are different things; both import forms work and no lint enforces either for @ariestools/sdk. findings.recommendation: Move the operational `xy work` guidance into xy-toolchain's work section: claim semantics and the no-lease warning for multi-worktree use, deduplication, suppressing GitHub dual-write for machine-generated items, and the xyex channel. In xy-agent, keep a short pointer: "record findings in the repository's work tracker; in xy repos see xy-toolchain work tracking". Replace the stable-id advice with "search existing items by tag/file before adding", or file a toolchain request for `xy work add --id`.

It does not check for an existing claim, so the no-lease caveat is accurate, but Layer 2 never mentions it. createWorkId (work/id.ts:19-35) embeds formatWorkDate(now). work/index.ts:171 `options.id ?? createWorkId(...)` is the only way to set an explicit id. `xy.mjs work add --help` on 10.1.1 lists --description, --area, --tag, --file, --line, --inline, --acceptance, --verify, the five priority flags and the workspace flags, with no --id. GitHub dual-write can only be disabled in config: schema.ts:85 `github: { enabled: true }`, and there is no CLI flag. stability.ts:69 has 'work': 'experimental', and the help prints '(experimental — prefer xyex)'. lifecycle.md:114's WorkAnchor claim is accurate (schema.ts:17-21, kind 'file' only); the problem is placement. The new `xy agent audit` in 10.1.1 does not create work items (no 'work' references in actions/agent/*), so the right fix is unchanged.
verify.skill: confirmed: Checked against 10.1.1 / main 812b27a91 and the problem is still there. The contradiction is real: xy-agent/auditing.md:109 says "Queue work there; do not claim work there", while xy-toolchain/commands.md:185-186 tells agents to run `pnpm xy work next --claim` and `claim <id>`. The toolchain's local .agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:146-149 says "Claim the next item before starting implementation". A claim only sets claimedAt and status (actions/work/helpers.ts:56-69). The advice at auditing.md:102 cannot be followed from the CLI: `xy.mjs work add --help` (10.1.1) has no --id option, and an explicit id is only possible programmatically (actions/work/index.ts:171 `options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`). findings.title: xyo-skills install docs use `--all`, which overwrites canonical xy-development/xy-toolchain with redirect stubs
findings.current: xyo-skills/README.md:145-147 "npx skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --all" then "npx skills add XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills --all"; same pattern at :158 (-g) and :166 (--copy). README.md:23 calls ariestools-skills the "Required companion".
findings.truth: xyo-skills still ships skills/xy-development and skills/xy-toolchain as REDIRECT ONLY stubs (metadata.status: redirect, v1.1.38). Skills.sh installs each skill into `.agents/skills/<name>` after `cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir)`, so running the second command replaces the canonical ariestools copies with the stubs. skills-lock.json then records source XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills, and `xy skills lint` (part of `xy check`) fails `skills.migrated-source`. The xyo-skills marketplace renderers also copy the whole skills/ tree, so anyone with both plugins installed gets two skills each named xy-development and xy-toolchain. The toolchain's own `xy skills defaults` avoids this by using explicit `--skill` selectors for xyo-skills.
findings.evidence: xyo-skills/README.md:147,158,166; xyo-skills/skills/xy-development/SKILL.md:1-12 (status: redirect); toolchain/packages/toolchain/node_modules/skills/dist/cli.mjs:2274-2324 (installSkillForAgent -> cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir)); `xy skills --help`: "--all  Shorthand for --skill '*' --agent '*' -y"; toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/lock.ts:75-92 + lint.ts:364-388 (skills.migrated-source, defaultLevel error); defaults.ts:67-74 (xyo selector = explicit XYO_STACK_SKILLS); xyo-skills/scripts/marketplace-sync/build-claude.mjs:7-8 (copies all of skills/).
findings.recommendation: In xyo-skills/README.md, replace each `XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills --all` with explicit selectors (`--skill xyo-knowledge --skill xl1-knowledge --skill xl1-patterns --skill xl1-testing --skill xl1-dapp-kit --skill xl1-scaffold --skill xl1-build`) or with `xy skills defaults`. Also state the order rule: install ariestools-skills last. Longer term, retire the stubs. Every link into them uses an anchor that exists in canonical workflow.md (lines 63, 112, 124), so rewrite the xl1-* links to absolute ariestools-skills GitHub URLs, then delete the stubs and remove them from the stub allowlist in xyo-skills/scripts/validate-skills.mjs:70-73.

findings.truth: Toolchain 10.1.0 ships experimental `xy plan lint` (prefer `xyex plan lint`). Any other file in papers/ is an error, and `--fix` flattens it into notes/, so `<PRODUCT>_WHITE_PAPER.md` gets moved. The rules also require docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, and notes/README.md, scaffolding them from templates. toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16 says "Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages". repo-docs.md:22 requires CLAUDE.md to be a regular file, not a symlink. findings.title: Telling agents to prefer `@ariestools/sdk/<module>` subpaths creates duplicate class types when the code also uses actor-kit or sdk-react
findings.current: conventions.md:6 "Prefer **subpath imports** for clarity..."; conventions.md:17 "Prefer subpaths in libraries"; conventions.md:56 "Prefer `@ariestools/sdk` + subpath for neutral helpers"; overview.md:22 "subpaths are clearer and tree-shaking-friendly"; modules.md:3 "Prefer subpaths when the import set is small"; overview.md:40 says `zod` is an optional peer, needed only for zod helpers
findings.truth: In sdk 9.0.1 the root export resolves by platform (`node` -> dist/node/index.d.ts and a bundled dist/node/index.mjs), but every subpath resolves unconditionally to dist/neutral. The house tsconfig uses NodeNext, so the `node` condition is active. Mixing root and subpath imports therefore loads two separate declarations and two separate runtime copies of classes with private members. AbstractCreatable has `private _status`. actor-kit switched to root imports for exactly this reason. The rest of the ecosystem imports from the root: actor-kit 18 root / 0 subpath, sdk-react 115/0, browser-kit 1/0, ariestools 38/4. The root bundle also statically imports `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core`, so root importers need zod installed even though peerDependenciesMeta marks it optional.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json exports: '.' has node/browser/types/default conditions; './assert' and './creatable' have only types/default pointing at ./dist/neutral/*. Separate files exist at dist/node/modules/creatable/AbstractCreatable.d.ts and dist/neutral/modules/creatable/AbstractCreatable.d.ts (line 19 `private _status;`). toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json: "moduleResolution": "NodeNext". actor-kit commit 5299634 "fix: import @ariestools/sdk from the root barrel, not subpaths": "a program mixing an actor-kit package (subpath imports) with a root-importing consumer ... sees two nominally-incompatible AbstractCreatable declarations". `grep -oE 'from "zod[^"]*"' dist/node/index.mjs` returns zod/mini and zod/v4/core. peerDependenciesMeta: {zod:{optional:true}}. Import counts came from grep over each repo's packages/ directory, excluding node_modules and dist.
findings.recommendation: Reverse the guidance. Default to the root barrel `@ariestools/sdk`, which is the ecosystem norm and is required whenever a value or type crosses into actor-kit, cli-kit, browser-kit or sdk-react: AbstractCreatable, BaseEmitter, Creatable params, loggers. Never mix root and subpath imports in one program. Allow subpaths only in isolated leaf bundles that share no SDK class with other packages, and explain why: subpaths are neutral-only while the root is per-platform. In overview.md, say that a root import needs `zod` (^4.6) installed. Add a short 'Class identity' section to modules.md next to `creatable`.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked against source. sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json (9.0.1): '.' has node/browser/types/default conditions. The class is defined at runtime in both dist/node/index.mjs and dist/neutral/creatable.mjs (also dist/browser/index.mjs). Both dist/node and dist/neutral modules/creatable/AbstractCreatable.d.ts:19-20 declare `private _status; private _statusMutex;`, so the two copies are nominally incompatible. actor-kit 5299634 (2026-07-24) states this exact failure. `grep -oE` on dist/node/index.mjs finds `from "zod/mini"` and `from "zod/v4/core"`, while peerDependenciesMeta marks zod optional. findings.title: The toolchain's managed skill catalog leaves out xy-agent, so it cannot be required, declared without a source, or version-checked, and its source is resolved to xyo-skills
findings.current: skills/xy-agent/SKILL.md presents xy-agent as a first-class skill of this pack (released in 0.1.5 and listed in release-please extra-files), but the toolchain catalog does not know it
findings.truth: ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain'] (defaults.ts:13-17). XYO_SKILL_NAMES is built from that list (skillRules.ts:24). As a result: (a) `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills: ['xy-agent']` throws 'Unknown skills ...' (skillRules.ts:80-96); (b) a package.json `xy.skills: [{name:'xy-agent'}]` is reported as 'needs a source because it is outside the managed catalog' (packageSkills.ts:134-141); (c) xy-agent is never checked for being outdated; (d) skillSourceForName('xy-agent') returns XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills (defaults.ts:84-86), which has no xy-agent, so versions.ts:8-10 would fetch a URL that does not exist. Only `xy skills defaults` (`--all`) installs it. None of sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit or toolchain has xy-agent in skills-lock.json.
findings.evidence: toolchain defaults.ts:3-17, 84-86; skillRules.ts:24, 80-96, 126-128; packageSkills.ts:115-150; versions.ts:8-10. `ls XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills/skills` shows no xy-agent. The skills-lock.json files in the six repos list only ariestools-sdk, xy-development and xy-toolchain. The unreleased commits on toolchain main (e8bd980d1, 7eb43c3c2) do not touch actions/skills.
findings.recommendation: Add 'xy-agent' to ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS (defaults.ts:13-17), update the doc comment at defaults.ts:3-5, and add it to SKILL_ORDER after xy-toolchain (skillRules.ts:36-47). Do not put it in TIER_REQUIRED_SKILLS. Treat it as optional for every non-none tier, through optionalSkillsForTier or an equivalent list. You could also make it optional automatically when AGENTS.md exists, which is the same enablement signal `xy agent lint` uses. Either way, installing it must never trigger skills.unnecessary. Repos can then require it with the 10.1.1 `commands.skillsLint.skills: { 'xy-agent': { presence: 'required' } }` or with additionalSkills, and `xy skills pick` will list it with source ariestools/ariestools-skills. Apply the same pattern (catalog entry, optional list or detection set) to any new Layer-3 skills when they land.

verify.code: adjusted: Still true at 10.1.1 (812b27a91, published). ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS is unchanged at defaults.ts:13-17, and skillSourceForName at defaults.ts:84-86 still falls back to XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills, which has no xy-agent. Some evidence is out of date. The claim that 'unreleased commits do not touch actions/skills' is no longer true: b8653a52d (in v10.1.1) changed skillRules.ts, lint.ts and pick.ts without adding xy-agent. Line references moved: XYO_SKILL_NAMES is now skillRules.ts:32, and the additionalSkills throw is at :88-105. 10.1.1 also adds two new catalog-bound surfaces that exclude xy-agent: normalizeSkillPresence throws 'Unknown skill in commands.skillsLint.skills' (skillRules.ts:113-131), and `xy skills pick` lists only XYO_DEFAULT_SKILLS (pick.ts:34). The recommended fix has a gap. Once a skill is in the catalog, unnecessarySkillsForProfile (skillRules.ts:190-206) flags any installed catalog skill that is not required, optional or allowed. optionalSkillsForTier returns only XL1_OPTIONAL_SKILLS, and only for the xl1 tier. Adding xy-agent to the catalog and keeping it opt-in would therefore produce skills.unnecessary warnings in every repo where `xy skills defaults --all` installed it. Since 10.1.1 also ships a stable `xy agent` command, run by `xy check`, that implements this skill's convention, the catalog gap matters more.

The recommendation therefore needs the 10.1.1 presence mechanism and an explicit optional path.

findings.title: Skills are not reliably installed in the repos that need them: nothing uses the package.json `xy.skills` declaration, and the skill does not document it
findings.current: commands.md:163 `xy skills lint` | Required project skills, versions...; commands.md:171 "Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills". No mention of tier detection, `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`, or package.json `xy.skills`.
findings.truth: Since toolchain 10.0.8 (881eede39, 2026-09-25), packages can recommend skills to their consumers through `xy.skills` in package.json. findings.title: xy-agent's repository layout contradicts the toolchain's repo-docs contract and its `xy plan lint` rules, and never mentions `xy plan`
findings.current: structure.md:24 `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md delta only`; agents-md.md:91,130-136 recommend nested package AGENTS.md; agents-md.md:110-114 "A symlink works equally well ... ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md"; auditing.md:32 allows CLAUDE.md to be "an @AGENTS.md import, a symlink, or absent"; structure.md:46 paper names `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`; the tree in structure.md:5-27 has no notes/, docs/ROADMAP.md or .xy/plan.json; auditing.md:9 says the checks are "performed by hand today"
findings.truth: The toolchain is the stated reference implementation. Its contract says: (1) "Do not add AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inside packages". (2) CLAUDE.md must be a regular file containing `@AGENTS.md`; plan lint uses lstat and rejects symlinks. (3) Root CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and README.md are required. (4) papers/ may contain only README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and an optional GREEN-PAPER.md; `--fix` moves every other file, including `<PRODUCT>_WHITE_PAPER.md` and LIGHT papers, into notes/. (5) docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/README.md are required. (6) `.xy/plan.json` is the plan manifest that routes to papers, docs and `xy work`. `xy plan lint`/`init` exist in 10.1.0 (experimental; prefer xyex). `xy repo lint` (stable, part of `xy check`) enforces package READMEs. The `xy agent` command the skill predicts is still only an open work item (XYW-20260901-263436), and `xy plan` (2026-09-08) has since shipped an overlapping layout.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16, 22, 37-44; toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:89-94, 105; actions/plan/lint.ts:88-90 (`stat.isFile() && !stat.isSymbolicLink()`). `node xy.mjs plan lint --rules` lists 8 rules including plan.papers.unexpected-files and plan.root.claude-imports-agents. `xy.mjs --stability --json` reports plan/plan init/plan lint as experimental and repo as stable. `xy.mjs --help` has no `agent` command. toolchain/.xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json is still open.
findings.recommendation: Keep the skill's symlink and nested-AGENTS.md guidance, because they match the stable `xy agent lint` rules agents.adapter-thin and agents.nested-delta-only. Then: (1) Rewrite auditing.md 'Tooling status' (lines 7-21). `xy agent lint|init|audit|index|archive` ships stable in @ariestools/toolchain >=10.1.1 and runs inside `xy check`. Map each catalog row to its rule id (agents.*, docs.*, decisions.naming, papers.header). Document `--rules`, `--json`, `--strict` and `--fix`, plus `commands.agentLint.rules`. Keep the hand-run greps only as a fallback for older toolchains. (2) In structure.md and agents-md.md, recommend the `@AGENTS.md` import form by default, because it passes both `xy agent lint` and `xy plan lint`. Note that the experimental `xy plan lint` (not in `xy check`) is stricter: it wants CLAUDE.md as a regular file, no package AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, papers/ limited to README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and GREEN-PAPER.md, and requires docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/README.md. In repos with `.xy/plan.json`, follow plan's paper names and use notes/. (3) Make structure.md:7 and auditing.md:32 agree on whether CLAUDE.md may be absent. (4) In xy-toolchain commands.md, add `xy agent lint` to the Repository policy table and to the `xy check` row, and list `xy plan`/`xyex plan` as experimental with a pointer to xy-agent. (5) Upstream: reconcile toolchain docs/repo-docs.md and `xy plan lint` with `xy agent lint`.

verify.code: adjusted: 10.1.1 changes the right fix. 8f2768dfd (in v10.1.1) ships `xy agent lint|init|audit|index|archive`. `xy --stability --json` reports agent as stable, checkCommand.ts:5,49-50 runs agentLint inside `xy check`, and XYW-20260901-263436 is now status 'done'. So the finding's claim that 'the xy agent command is still only an open work item' is out of date. auditing.md:9 ('There is no `xy agent` command yet... do not tell a user to run a command that does not exist') is now wrong, and the 'Tooling status' section needs rewriting. The stable rule catalog (`xy agent lint --rules`) also mirrors the skill rather than the plan contract. agents.adapter-thin says 'Tool adapters import AGENTS.md, symlink to it, or are absent' (rules.ts:73-83,112). agents.nested-delta-only accepts packages/*/AGENTS.md as a delta (rules.ts:185-194). `xy agent init` scaffolds docs/{decisions,runbooks,plans,evidence,archive} and a generated docs/README.md (init.ts:7,55-72), matching structure.md:13-19. agent lint has no paper-name rule; papers.header checks only version, status and date. The finding's advice to drop the symlink/absent options and nested AGENTS.md would therefore make the skill contradict a stable, check-enforced command. On the other side is the stable `xy agent lint`. findings.title: `xy work` guidance is split across three places that disagree on whether agents should claim work items
findings.current: xy-toolchain commands.md:185-186 shows `pnpm xy work next --claim` and `pnpm xy work claim <id>` with no caveat. xy-agent auditing.md:109 says ".xy/work/ is a durable backlog, not a live coordination plane ... Queue work there; do not claim work there." toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:22,146-149 says to claim the next item before starting implementation. xy-agent auditing.md:102-103 tells agents to pass an explicit stable id and to suppress the GitHub dual-write per item.
findings.truth: claimItem is a plain overwrite of the item JSON with no lock, lease or compare-and-swap (helpers.ts:56-69), so xy-agent's warning is correct for concurrent worktrees. The CLI has no `--id` or per-item GitHub opt-out on `xy work add`; only the programmatic API takes `id` (work/index.ts:104,171), and dual-write is controlled only by `stores.github.enabled`. `xy work` is experimental: help says "(experimental — prefer xyex)" and the stability catalog reports {name:'work',stability:'experimental'}.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/helpers.ts:56-69; work/index.ts:104,171; `node xy.mjs work add --help` shows no --id or --no-github option; `node xy.mjs work --help`; `xy.mjs --stability --json` reports work as experimental. Skill lines are as quoted.
findings.recommendation: Make xy-toolchain commands.md#skills-and-work-tracking the single owner of xy work usage rules. Add the experimental status (`xyex work`), and a concurrency caveat: claim is non-atomic, so use it only in single-agent or single-worktree flows and queue rather than claim across worktrees. Move xy-agent's machine-generated-item rules there, rewritten to match the CLI: use config `stores.github.enabled:false` or the programmatic API for stable ids, since there is no `--id` flag. Then replace auditing.md:100-109 in xy-agent with a short link plus the documentation-specific batching advice.

verify.code: confirmed: No 10.1.1 commit touched actions/work. claimItem (helpers.ts:56-69) builds the claimed item and calls writeWorkItem (store.ts:92-95), which is validate plus writeJson with no lock, lease or compare-and-swap. The programmatic `id?: string` is at work/index.ts:104, and line 171 uses `options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`. `xy work add --help` on 10.1.1 shows no --id and no GitHub opt-out flag. GitHub dual-write is controlled only by stores.github.enabled, which defaults to true (schema.ts:85,230). The help text says '(experimental — prefer xyex)', and the stability catalog reports work as experimental. The quoted skill text matches: commands.md:185-186 has no caveat and commands.md has no 'experimental' or 'xyex' anywhere; xy-agent auditing.md:102-103,109; toolchain .agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:22,146-149.
verify.skill: confirmed: Verified at 10.1.1, which did not touch actions/work. The quoted lines are accurate. commands.md:185-186 shows claim with no caveat. xy-agent auditing.md:109 says 'do not claim work there'. The toolchain-local xy-work SKILL.md:22,146-149 says to claim before implementing. claimItem (helpers.ts:56-69) is a plain writeWorkItem overwrite with no lock or compare-and-swap. `xy.mjs work add --help` shows no --id and no per-item GitHub opt-out, so auditing.md:102-103 ('Pass an explicit stable id', 'Suppress the GitHub dual-write') is not doable from the CLI. `work --help` prints '(experimental — prefer xyex)', and no skill file mentions xyex or the experimental status of `work`. The new `xy agent audit` does not create work items, so the guidance still has to live in the skills. Medium is proportionate.

findings.title: The skill's path formats (code spans, task-first authority table) are invisible to agents.links-resolve and agents.authority-rows-resolve
findings.current: agents-md.md:17-21 and templates.md:21-22 give read-order paths as code spans; agents-md.md:29-33 and templates.md:30-32 define the table `| When the task touches | Authority | Status of that authority |` with code-span paths; auditing.md:36 calls 'Every path and link resolves' 'the single highest-value check'; :40 says 'Authority rows resolve ... whose kind matches the claim'.
findings.truth: links-resolve extracts only Markdown links `[text](target)`, so a missing path in a code span is never reported. authority-rows-resolve runs only under a `##` heading that starts with 'Authority'. It reads column 1 as the path and column 2 as the expected front-matter kind. With the skill's table, column 1 is a task class, so every row is skipped. A code-span path such as `papers/X.md`, or a linked path `[p](p)`, in column 1 is reported as missing even when the file exists, because the parser keeps the backticks or parentheses. Only a bare path works. The toolchain's own init template hits the parentheses case.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/agent/rules.ts:37-42 (markdownLinks), :146-155, :195-221 (:198 heading test, :202 column-1 target, :210 column-2 kind). Scratchpad fixture: a missing `docs/HANDOFF_2026_08_30.md` code span and a missing `papers/MISSING_YELLOW_PAPER.md` authority row were not reported; only "links to missing path docs/GONE.md" (a Markdown link) was. After retitling to `## Authority` and moving the path to column 1, an existing file in a code span still gave "Authority row `papers/MISSING_YELLOW_PAPER.md` does not exist". The init scaffold gives "Authority row (docs/README.md) does not exist".
findings.recommendation: Tell authors to write repository paths in AGENTS.md as Markdown links so the linter catches renames. Title the authority section `## Authority`. Document the column order the parser currently needs (path first, then kind, then status), or keep the task-first table and record that rows are not verified until the toolchain parses link and code-span cells and the third column. Keep the status column in either layout.

verify.skill: confirmed: markdownLinks at rules.ts:37-42 extracts only `[text](target)`. findings.title: Front-matter lint checks only that `kind` exists; `--fix` inserts `kind: doc` (outside the vocabulary) and needs a second pass to converge
findings.current: lifecycle.md:10 kind vocabulary 'paper|spec|decision|plan|runbook|evidence|handoff|research'; :12-17 fields 'required for kind: paper|spec / runbook / evidence'; auditing.md:46 'Front matter present and valid'; auditing.md:21 'Only index and archive are safe to automate as fixers' while also listing 'insert a missing front-matter key'.
findings.truth: docs.front-matter warns only when front matter or `kind` is missing. No rule validates kind or state values, or the per-kind fields version, reviewed and commit. `--fix` prepends `---\nkind: doc\n---` to every docs/, papers/ and specs/ file that has no front matter, runbooks and papers included. Lint loads its context once, so in the same pass the index fixer renders from the pre-fix front matter, and the next non-fix run fails docs.index-current with an error.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/agent/rules.ts:222-243 (:229 kind check, :231 'kind: doc'), :244-259; lint.ts:21 (context loaded once). Scratchpad run: pass 1 --fix gave 'fixed docs.front-matter x2', 'fixed docs.index-current x1', with docs/runbooks/deploy.md now 'kind: doc' and an empty Kind cell in the index. Pass 2 without --fix: "error docs.index-current - docs/README.md does not match the index generated from front matter".
findings.recommendation: Either add `doc` to the kind vocabulary or tell agents to replace `kind: doc` with the real kind after `--fix` (it is also inserted into runbooks and papers). State that kind and state values are not validated. Most per-kind fields are not checked: `version` for specs, `reviewed` for runbooks and `commit` for evidence. The exceptions are papers.header, which only checks that papers/ files mention version, status and date, and decisions.naming, which requires a `state` on decisions. After any front-matter fix, run `pnpm xy agent index` (or `--fix` a second time) before the clean verification run, because the index fixer renders from the front matter as it was before the fix. Bring auditing.md:21 and :122 into line with the two fixers that ship: docs.front-matter (insert-only, `kind: doc`) and docs.index-current.

findings.truth: (1) docs.superseded-archived checks that the successor is under archive/ rather than the superseded file (:271-273), and resolves paths relative to the document. (2) agents.authority-rows-resolve keeps backticks and parentheses in column 1 (:202), so the init scaffold's own linked row and any code-span path are reported missing; it also ignores the skill's three-column task-first table. findings.title: Document `xy skills pick` and per-skill `commands.skillsLint.skills` presence (required|allowed|off), new in 10.1.1
findings.current: commands.md:171 "`xy skills` wraps the bundled Skills.sh CLI and adds XY-aware defaults, linting, and updates. Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills; use `--offline` ..."; commands.md:163 row "`xy skills lint` | Required project skills, versions, and duplicate/unnecessary installations"; SKILL.md:3 and SKILL.md:34 say only "skills". The pack never mentions `pick` for skills (only `deplint pick`) or `commands.skillsLint.skills`.
findings.truth: 10.1.1 (commit b8653a52d) adds `xy skills pick [--skill <name> ...]`, which is stable because it inherits the `skills` parent's tier, and `commands.skillsLint.skills: Record<name, { presence: 'allowed' | 'off' | 'required' }>`. How presence works: `required` adds the skill to the required set after the profile and additionalSkills are applied, so `skills.required-installed` and `skills.required-current` both error and `lint --fix` installs it. `off` removes it from the required set even when the profile requires it. If an `off` skill is still installed it warns as `skills.unnecessary`, which fails `--strict`. `off` does not silence `skills.package-recommended`. `allowed` only stops the unnecessary warning on an extra install. It does not downgrade a skill the profile requires: a missing one still errors, so use `off` for that. An allowed skill is not version-checked. How pick works: it accepts only the 10 catalog names (not xy-agent) and validates all of them before installing anything. It installs each skill with `skills add <source> --skill <name> -y` and writes `xy.config.ts` in the current directory with every picked skill set to `required`. It cannot record `allowed` or `off`, and it replaces any existing `skills:` block. If the existing xy.config.ts has no `skills:` block, it rewrites the whole file (see the toolchain finding). Without a TTY it needs `--skill`, and `--help` does not print help. The toolchain's stability rubric requires stable config fields to be documented in xy-toolchain.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/skillRules.ts:22-30,107-145 (presence parse/apply), :190-206 (unnecessary uses allowed set only); src/actions/skills/lint.ts:474-479 (presence wired), :322-341 (package-recommended independent), :145-178 (only required are version-checked); src/actions/skills/pick.ts:110-131 (validate, install, write required only), :58-88 (write); src/xy/common/skills/index.ts:8,102-120 (pick, repeatable --skill); src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:652; docs/xy-config.md:97-99; src/xy/stability.ts:10-12 (subcommands inherit),67 ('skills': 'stable'),182 (rubric: 'Flags and xy.config.ts fields documented in xy-toolchain skills'); `node xy.mjs skills pick --help </dev/null` -> 'xy skills pick needs a TTY. Pass --skill <name> ...' exit 1; `npm view @ariestools/toolchain@10.1.1 version` -> 10.1.1.
findings.recommendation: In commands.md 'Skills and work tracking', add a 'Choosing skills' subsection with a presence table. `required`: added after the profile and additionalSkills are applied, so it must be installed and current (skills.required-installed and required-current, both errors), and `lint --fix` installs it. `off`: removed from the required set even when the profile requires it. If it is still installed it warns as skills.unnecessary, which fails --strict, unless it is tier-optional (xl1-dapp-kit, xl1-scaffold or xl1-build at the xl1 tier) or recommended by a package. `off` never silences skills.package-recommended. `allowed`: only suppresses skills.unnecessary for an extra install. It does not relax a profile-required skill (use `off` for that), and it is not version-checked. Document `pnpm xy skills pick --skill <name> [--skill <name>]` from the repo root. Note that it accepts only the 10 catalog names, validates all of them before installing, records every pick as `required`, needs --skill without a TTY, and that `--help` does not print help. Until the toolchain fix lands, warn that pick rewrites xy.config.ts: with no `skills:` key it replaces the whole file, and an existing block is replaced by only this run's picks. Commit first, or edit `commands.skillsLint.skills` by hand, which is the only way to record allowed or off. State that `xy-agent` in `skills`, `additionalSkills` or `pick` is a config error that makes `xy skills lint` and `xy check` exit 1. Install it with `pnpm xy skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --skill xy-agent -y` instead. Reword :171 to name the XY subcommands (defaults, lint, pick), with everything else forwarded to Skills.sh. Extend the :163 row and the SKILL.md:34 router to cover `skills pick` and per-skill presence.

findings.title: `xy skills pick` overwrites an existing xy.config.ts that has no `skills:` block and drops earlier presence entries
findings.current: pick.ts:76-87: if xy.config.ts exists, it calls `spliceObject(current, 'skills:', skillsBlock)` and then `fs.writeFileSync(filePath, replaced ?? body)`, where `body` is a fresh file holding only `commands.skillsLint.skills`. spliceObject (:90-102) returns undefined when the text 'skills:' is absent.
findings.truth: In any repo whose xy.config.ts lacks a `skills:` key, which today is every ariestools repo, running the stable `xy skills pick --skill <name>` replaces the whole config (compile mode, monolith and deplint settings, and so on) with a skills-only config. When a `skills:` block does exist, it is replaced by only the skills picked in this run, all set to `required`, so earlier `allowed`/`off` entries are silently lost. The splice also targets the first 'skills:' substring anywhere in the file. The spec covers only a missing file (skillsPick.spec.ts creates a temp dir with no config).
findings.evidence: pick.ts:58-102. I copied writeSkillPresence and spliceObject verbatim into the scratchpad and ran them on (A) a config with compile.mode 'monolith' plus commands.deplint: the output was only the skillsLint block, with compile and deplint gone; and on (B) a config with 'xl1-scaffold': allowed and 'ariestools-sdk': off: the output held only 'xy-toolchain': required. `grep -c 'skills:'` returns 0 for xy.config.ts in toolchain (30 lines), sdk-js (22), sdk-react (21), actor-kit (8), browser-kit (17) and cli-kit (8). stability.ts:184 rubric: 'No known data-loss --fix'. spec/skills/skillsPick.spec.ts (b8653a52d) tests only a fresh dir.
findings.recommendation: Never fall back to `body` when a file exists. Insert or merge `commands.skillsLint.skills` structurally (AST or a magicast-style edit), or refuse and print the snippet for the user to paste. Merge the new picks into existing presence entries instead of replacing them. Allow `--presence allowed|off` per pick. Match the key under `skillsLint` rather than the first 'skills:' substring. Add specs for an existing config without a skills block and one with prior allowed/off entries. Until this is fixed, the xy-toolchain skill must carry the warning above.

findings.title: xy-agent is still outside the catalog in 10.1.1, now behind a stable `xy check` gate it documents. The new pick/presence knobs reject it, and `skills defaults` installs it but lint never sees it
findings.current: defaults.ts:13-17 ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain']; skillRules.ts:65 XY_SKILLS = ['xy-development','xy-toolchain']; repo-init/skillsInstall.ts:34 has a second hardcoded ariestools set without xy-agent; the defaults help (xy/common/skills/index.ts:17) and docs/STABILITY.md:72 list only three ariestools skills.
findings.truth: This differs from the known findings, which said xy-agent cannot be required and that no install path puts it beside xy-development. (1) `xy skills defaults` does install it. It runs `skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --all` (or `--skill '*'`), and origin/main has skills/xy-agent (v0.1.5). Afterwards lint ignores it: it is never version-checked and never flagged unnecessary, because both filter on isXyoSkillName. That is why none of the 52 workspace skills-lock.json files lists it. (2) 10.1.1 shipped `xy agent` as a stable command that implements 'the repository documentation convention described by the xy-agent skill'. `xy check` now runs it in every repo, and `agents.file-present` is error-level. So xy-agent is now the guidance for a gate every toolchain consumer must pass. It should be tier-required at the xy tier, not merely requirable. (3) Both new 10.1.1 mechanisms reject it with a hard failure. A presence entry makes `xy skills lint` exit 1 ('Unknown skill in commands.skillsLint.skills: xy-agent'), which also fails `xy check`. `xy skills pick --skill xy-agent` exits 1 ('only manages the Aries Tools and XYO/XL1 catalog'). Today the only lint-enforced route is a package.json `xy.skills` entry with an explicit `source` (packageSkills.ts:134-150), and no package uses it.
findings.evidence: toolchain defaults.ts:13-17,67-74 (--all / --skill '*'); skillRules.ts:65,73-77,113-131,175-177; lint.ts:217-226 (version fetch only for catalog names); repo-init/skillsInstall.ts:34; xy/common/skills/index.ts:17,61-63; docs/STABILITY.md:72-78; xy/common/checkCommand.ts:14,49-50 (agent lint in check); actions/agent/rules.ts:87-91 (agents.file-present, error); stability.ts:47 ('agent': 'stable'); .xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json description (convention 'described by the xy-agent skill'); `git ls-tree origin/main skills/` in ariestools-skills -> includes skills/xy-agent; scratch probes: `xy skills lint --offline` with skills:{'xy-agent':{presence:'required'}} -> 'Unknown skill ... xy-agent. Known skills: ariestools-sdk, xy-development, ...' exit=1; `xy skills pick --skill xy-agent` -> exit=1.
findings.recommendation: Register xy-agent in the managed catalog. Add it to ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS (defaults.ts:13-17) and SKILL_ORDER (skillRules.ts:36-47). Replace the hardcoded set in repo-init/skillsInstall.ts:34 with ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS so it installs from ariestools/ariestools-skills (skillSourceForName follows ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS). In the same change, give it a requirement level, because catalog membership alone makes existing `skills defaults` installs warn skills.unnecessary. Either (a) make it optional at every tier (extend optionalSkillsForTier, currently xl1-only), as the toolchain's work item XYW-20260901-263436 specifies, or (b) add it to XY_SKILLS so xy, xyo and xl1 repos require it, matching the `xy check` agent gate. Update the defaults help (xy/common/skills/index.ts:17), the lint help source list (:61-63) and docs/STABILITY.md:72 to name four skills. findings.title: The global-flag table does not list the new `--defer` flag. Since 10.1.1, `publish` and `deploy` no longer hand off to a same-named root script by default
findings.current: skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md:26: "| `--no-defer` | Bypass a same-named local package script |". This is the only text in the pack about deferral, and it implies every command hands off to a matching root script by default. `--defer` appears nowhere in skills/.
findings.truth: Since 10.1.1 (commit b75077b16), `deploy` and `publish` are 'sensitive lifecycle commands' and never hand off to a matching root package.json script unless `--defer` is passed. Without the flag the CLI prints 'Not delegating "<cmd>" to the local script. Pass --defer to run it.' and runs the toolchain command with its preflight (e.g. the publish whoami check). `--no-defer` or XY_NO_DEFER=1 still wins if both flags are given. `--defer`/`--no-defer` are stripped from the arguments passed to the script. Every other command still defers by default.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/lib/tryRunLocalScript.ts:13 `const SENSITIVE_LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS = new Set(['deploy', 'publish'])`, :19-21 isDeferralExplicitlyRequested, :45-50 refusal branch, :53-56 strips --defer/--no-defer from forwarded args. packages/toolchain/src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:126-130 new global option `defer` ('Allow publish and deploy to run a matching root package.json script'). spec/lib/tryRunLocalScript.spec.ts (b75077b16) covers 'does not defer publish or deploy unless --defer is present' and '--defer --no-defer → no defer'. `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs deploy --help` (10.1.1 dist) lists `--defer  Allow publish and deploy to run a matching root package.json script [default: false]` next to `--no-defer`. docs/code-review-2026-10-06.md:186-193 (finding #20) is the motivation. `npm view @ariestools/toolchain dist-tags` → latest 10.1.1. Once it upgrades, `pnpm xy deploy` runs the toolchain's version-bump/build/publish flow instead of the Vercel script unless `--defer` is given.
findings.recommendation: In commands.md Global behavior, add a row `| --defer | Let publish and deploy run a same-named root package.json script (off by default since 10.1.1) |`. Add one sentence: 'xy publish and xy deploy always run the toolchain implementation, including its preflight checks. To run a repo's own deploy/publish script through xy, pass --defer, or call the script directly with pnpm run <name>.' When the known release-commands gap (deploy/publish) and the toolchain.md root-scripts deferral gap are fixed, carry this exception into both places.

findings.title: New stable `commands.updo.ignoreDeps` setting (10.1.1) is not documented. It is how a repo stops `xy updo` from updating chosen dependencies
findings.current: absent. commands.md has no `xy updo` entry and no `commands.updo` key: the Configuration section at skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md:293-327 shows only `dead` and `deplint`. grep for 'updo' or 'ignoreDeps' across skills/ returns nothing. This extends two known findings: the missing `up`/`updo` command docs and the missing stable command configs (publint, apiExposure, license, packman). Neither covers this new field.
findings.truth: 10.1.1 (commit 8688075c9) adds `CommandsConfig.updo?: UpdoConfig { ignoreDeps?: string[] }`, marked stable. Each entry is an exact dependency key or a positive glob such as '@vendor/*'. Matching uses the package.json declaration key, so an `npm:` alias is matched by its alias name (e.g. `typescript-native`). Root entries apply to every workspace, and a package xy.config.ts adds to the root list instead of replacing it. Matching declarations are left out of the chooser and are never rewritten, even when another workspace updates the same name. Negations, empty strings, or a non-array throw before any manifest is written. The setting only stops updates; it does not pin the installed tree, and it is separate from pnpm's `update.ignoreDeps`, which xy updo does not read. updo still filters candidate versions by pnpm `minimumReleaseAge`. The setting is already being adopted: dapp-kit (toolchain ~10.1.1) has uncommitted work that sets it in a package config to keep one package on Vitest 4.1 while the root moves to Vitest 5.

findings.title: Native AGENTS.md reading exists, but any CLAUDE.md in the working directory or above turns it off. Keep the @AGENTS.md import; this reverses the fix the 'reads natively' finding implies
findings.current: agents-md.md:100 "Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`, and supports `@path` imports expanded into context at launch"; agents-md.md:122-124 says to verify only with `/context` under Memory files; auditing.md:32 accepts CLAUDE.md that is "an `@AGENTS.md` import, a symlink, or absent".
findings.truth: Both claims behind the apparent contradiction are true. Claude Code v2.1.277+ reads AGENTS.md natively in its default `claude-md-or-agents-md` mode, but only when no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or any directory above it. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the managed CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules do not count. If a CLAUDE.md is found, Claude reads the CLAUDE.md files only. A CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md never causes a double read. CLAUDE.md sits above every repository here, so native reading never happens for a session started inside a repo, and an absent repo CLAUDE.md hides that repo's AGENTS.md. The `claude` on PATH is 2.1.187, older than the 2.1.277 floor. The `@AGENTS.md` import therefore stays necessary, which matches the toolchain's scaffolds.
findings.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, section 'AGENTS.md' and 'When Claude Code reads AGENTS.md': by default Claude reads AGENTS.md "only when you have no `CLAUDE.md` in your working directory or above it". The same page says reading AGENTS.md directly needs v2.1.277 or later and lists the four 'Project instructions' values. Its 'Remove an earlier AGENTS.md workaround' section says keeping an `@AGENTS.md` import never loads AGENTS.md twice. Its 'My AGENTS.md isn't loading' section says /memory lists a natively read AGENTS.md from v2.1.280. findings.title: `agents.adapter-thin` rejects Claude's documented adapter shape, rejects the output of `xyex plan lint --fix`, and requires a Copilot `@AGENTS.md` form that most Copilot surfaces do not expand
findings.current: document.ts:46-50 `isThinAgentsImport` strips comments and requires exactly one remaining line matching `^@(\.\/)?AGENTS\.md$`. rules.ts:70-84 errors on anything else that is not a symlink to AGENTS.md.
findings.truth: (1) Claude Code documents `@AGENTS.md` followed by Claude-specific sections as the standard adapter, and this rule errors on it. (2) The experimental plan-lint fixer, in actions/plan/rootDocs.ts:53-56, prepends the template from plan/templates.ts:30-32 to existing CLAUDE.md content. The result, `@AGENTS.md` plus the old text, then fails `agents.adapter-thin` with pointer-not-import, so `xyex plan lint --fix` followed by `xy check` fails. (3) For .github/copilot-instructions.md, only Copilot CLI documents expanding `@` file references; github.com Chat and the IDE chats do not, so they see the literal line. The Copilot CLI page does not say which directory relative `@` paths resolve from. Claude, Gemini CLI and VS Code all resolve relative paths from the importing file, so `@AGENTS.md` inside .github/ plausibly targets .github/AGENTS.md (unverified for Copilot). The regex also rejects `@../AGENTS.md`. (4) The rule accepts a symlinked copilot-instructions.md, but the Copilot cloud agent already reads AGENTS.md and combines every instruction set, so the content plausibly loads twice. No deduplication is documented.
findings.evidence: Toolchain paths and lines as above, at 812b27a91 (v10.1.1). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, sections 'Share one file with other coding tools' and 'Import additional files' (relative paths resolve from the importing file). https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-custom-instructions: @-references are supported in copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, not in GEMINI.md or *.instructions.md, and no base directory is stated. https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-instructions-support: the support matrix per surface. https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-instructions: references use Markdown links, resolved from the instructions file.
findings.recommendation: Accept `@AGENTS.md` (or `@./AGENTS.md`) as the first non-comment line followed by tool-specific content. Keep erroring on full copies and divergent adapters that never import AGENTS.md. Use one shared predicate for agent lint (document.ts isThinAgentsImport) and the plan-lint fixer (plan/markdown.ts hasClaudeAgentsImport, rootDocs.ts) so that `xyex plan lint --fix` output passes `xy check`. For .github/copilot-instructions.md, accept a Markdown link to ../AGENTS.md or `@../AGENTS.md`, or recommend leaving the file absent. VS Code resolves links from the instructions file, and the Copilot CLI does not document a base directory for @ paths. Do not claim that symlinked Copilot instructions double-load in the CLI, which documents deduplicating identical instructions. Flag it only as undocumented for the cloud agent.

According to Claude's docs, a CLAUDE.md that only tells Claude in words to read AGENTS.md means Claude sees it only if it chooses to open it. findings.title: The adapter check passes an absent GEMINI.md, but by default Gemini CLI loads only GEMINI.md, never AGENTS.md
findings.current: auditing.md:32 "`CLAUDE.md` is an `@AGENTS.md` import, a symlink, or absent — never a copy, never a divergent file. Same for `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `GEMINI.md`"; the hand-run script at auditing.md:65-67 checks only CLAUDE.md.
findings.truth: Gemini CLI's default context file is GEMINI.md. It reads AGENTS.md only if `context.fileName`, a string or list, names it, for example in a committed project `.gemini/settings.json`. It expands `@file` imports recursively, with a default maximum depth of 5, so a GEMINI.md of `@AGENTS.md` works. An absent GEMINI.md with no such setting leaves Gemini without the repository guidance. For Copilot, an absent copilot-instructions.md is fine for the cloud agent, CLI and VS Code chat, which read AGENTS.md natively. github.com Chat and the Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode and Eclipse chats read only copilot-instructions.md. No repository in the workspace has a GEMINI.md or .gemini/, which is why this is low.

findings.title: Refines the known high finding. It holds, but the cause is that Skills.sh installs by name and the last install wins. --all is not the cause. -g and --copy behave the same.
findings.current: xyo-skills/README.md:145 `npx skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --all`, then :147 `npx skills add XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills --all`; :157-158 the same pair with `-g`; :166 `npx skills add XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills --all --copy`; :174 `npx skills update`. Known finding wording: 'xyo-skills install docs use `--all`, which overwrites canonical xy-development/xy-toolchain with redirect stubs'.
findings.truth:
Checked in skills 1.7.1 (current npx latest, and the CLI that toolchain 10.1.1 bundles) and in 1.5.12. The overwrite claim holds.

- Install target and lock entry are both keyed by the frontmatter `name`. The second install of the same name overwrites the first. It never skips and never merges.
- `installSkillForAgent` runs `rm -rf` on the canonical `.agents/skills/<name>` (or on each agent dir in `--copy` mode), then copies the new source in. This deletes the canonical-only files: typescript.md and git.md from xy-development; commands.md, eslint.md and the rest from xy-toolchain.
- `--all` expands to `--skill '*' --agent '*' -y`, so there is no prompt. The only sign is a yellow 'overwrites:' line in the summary.
- Without -y, the user sees that line and one 'Proceed with installation?' prompt for the whole batch. There is no per-skill skip.
- `-g` behaves the same: the canonical dir under ~/.agents/skills is replaced, and the ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json entry is replaced (installedAt is kept).
- `--copy` behaves the same.
- `--all` is not the trigger. Any whole-pack selection installs the stubs: `-y` with no `--skill` selects every skill, and running inside Claude Code, Codex or Cursor forces -y.
- Order decides the result: running xyo-skills first leaves the canonical copies in place.
- The project skills-lock.json entry is rewritten to `XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills`, so `npx skills update` (README:174) keeps reinstalling the stub.
- Detection exists only for project installs in toolchain repos. There, `xy skills lint` (run by `xy check`) reports error `skills.migrated-source`, and `--fix` reinstalls from ariestools. Global installs are never seen, because the toolchain reads only ./skills-lock.json, ./.claude/skills and ./.agents/skills.
- Downstream xyo links still resolve, to stub shims: the 24 links all target SKILL.md, workflow.md(#anchors) or testing.md, which the stubs keep.
- `xy skills defaults` avoids the collision because it names the 7 XYO skills explicitly.
- The stubs are not marked `metadata.internal: true`.
- No local repo currently holds a stub: 0 of 53 skills-lock.json files, and no installed SKILL.md has `status: redirect`.

Severity stays high. The documented commands reliably replace the Layer 1/2 skills, the replacement survives `skills update`, `-g` installs are undetected, and the result fails an error-level enforced rule.

findings.title: Corrects known findings: the 'xy-agent resolves to xyo-skills' misroute cannot happen today; xy-agent can only be installed by declaring it in a package.json xy.skills entry with a source
findings.current: Known architecture findings say the toolchain catalog 'misroutes'/'mis-sources' xy-agent to XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills and that lint 'never installs' it. defaults.ts:84-86 `skillSourceForName` returns XYO_SKILLS_SOURCE for any name not in ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS.
findings.truth:
In 10.1.1 no call to skillSourceForName can receive a name outside the catalog, so the misroute is dormant:
- lint.ts:95 passes required, outdated and unmigrated names, all from the catalog, or uses an explicit source for package-declared skills.
- versions.ts:9 is typed XyoSkillName and fed through an isXyoSkillName filter (lint.ts:217-226).
- pick.ts:113-116 throws before routing.
- packageSkills.ts:115-116 routes only catalog names.

The real gate is catalog validation:
- `additionalSkills` throws TypeError for xy-agent (skillRules.ts:98-102).
- `commands.skillsLint.skills` throws for xy-agent (skillRules.ts:120-121).
- `xy skills pick` throws.

The one route by which lint --fix can install xy-agent is a workspace package or direct dependency declaring `"xy": {"skills": [{"name": "xy-agent", "source": "ariestools/ariestools-skills"}]}`. Without `source` it is a `skills.package-recommended` error.
- With a source, `--fix` runs `skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --skill xy-agent -y`.
- This route is documented in toolchain/docs/xy-config.md:101-106.
- No package declares it today.

The misroute becomes live only if xy-agent is later added to XYO_DEFAULT_SKILLS without also being added to ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS. Skills.sh would then fail with 'No matching skills found for: xy-agent' (cli.mjs:5283-5290).

findings.title: `--all` in `xy skills defaults` and both READMEs also means every agent: stale Eve copies land in agent/skills/, and the help text understates what is installed
findings.current: defaults.ts:68 `const installSelector = hasSkillsAgentFlag(args) ? ['--skill', '*'] : ['--all']`; xy/common/skills/index.ts:16-18 help: 'ariestools/ariestools-skills  (xy-development, xy-toolchain, ariestools-sdk)'; ariestools-skills README.md:37/40 and xyo-skills README:145/147/157/158 use `--all`.
findings.truth:
In skills 1.7.1 `--all` also sets `--agent '*'`, which covers all 79 agents.

In a project install:
- The Eve leg always writes real copies with rewritten frontmatter to `<repo>/agent/skills/<name>`, because Eve's canonical dir is agent/skills.
- Other agents get symlinks wherever their root dir already exists. OpenClaw's root is `skills/`, so in a repo with a top-level skills/ dir (both skill packs), createSymlink runs `rm -r` on `skills/<name>` and replaces it with a symlink.

In a global install, it creates ~/.<agent>/skills symlink dirs for every agent with a global dir, installed or not.

`xy skills lint` scans only .claude/skills and .agents/skills, so the agent/skills copies are never checked or refreshed. The workspace root shows exactly this:
- agent/skills (2026-08-13) holds 8 copies with rewritten frontmatter, including xy-development 1.1.29 (the old xyo full copy).
- .agents/skills holds the current 0.1.5.
- skills-lock.json does not list the agent/skills copies.

`--all` installs every ariestools skill, including xy-agent, so the help text that lists three skills is wrong.

- List xy-agent in the defaults help, or exclude it deliberately.
- In both READMEs, prefer `--skill '*' -y` (or explicit names) over `--all`.

findings.title: `xy skills pick` (new in 10.1.1, under the stable `xy skills`) overwrites the whole xy.config.ts when the file has no `skills:` key
findings.current: pick.ts:80-87: `const replaced = spliceObject(current, 'skills:', skillsBlock); fs.writeFileSync(filePath, replaced ?? body)`; docs/xy-config.md:98-99 '`xy skills pick` installs from the catalog and writes that intent.'
findings.truth:
The function finds the first `skills:` text in the file and replaces that block.

When the file has no `skills:` key:
- spliceObject returns undefined;
- pick writes the 13-line default body over the whole file;
- all compile, deplint and other config is lost.

This applies to sdk-js, toolchain and sdk-react today: their xy.config.ts files are 22, 30 and 21 lines, and none contains `skills:`. Note that `skillsLint:` does not match `skills:`.

When the key exists, the block is replaced with only the skills just picked. Earlier `off` and `allowed` entries are dropped.

The only spec covers an empty temp dir (spec/skills/skillsPick.spec.ts:30-48). `skills` is listed as stable in `xy --stability`, and the promotion rules there say 'No known data-loss --fix'.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/pick.ts:58-102,110-131; commit b8653a52d (2026-10-08) feat(skills): add xy skills pick; `grep -c 'skills:'` gives 0 for ariestools/{sdk-js,toolchain,sdk-react}/xy.config.ts; `grep -c 'needs a TTY. Pass --skill' packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs` gives 1; `xy.mjs --stability --json` shows {"name":"skills","stability":"stable"}; toolchain/docs/xy-config.md:97-99.
findings.recommendation:
Fix in the toolchain before the xy-toolchain skill documents `xy skills pick`:
- Never write `body` over an existing file. Fail with a message, or insert a `skillsLint.skills` key using an AST edit.
- Merge new presence entries into existing ones instead of replacing the block.
- Add specs for a populated xy.config.ts.

Until then, tell agents in xy-toolchain to edit `commands.skillsLint.skills` by hand.

findings.title: No 9.x-to-10.x upgrade note: 10.0.0 removed four aliases that now pass silently, and 9.2.0 removed `xy skills updo`
findings.current: toolchain.md:126-132 ("Migration and troubleshooting") covers only renaming @xylabs/* packages to @ariestools/*. No skill file mentions `gitlint`, `lintlint`, `node-lint`, `republint` or `skills updo`.
findings.truth:
10.0.0 (13350616a and 78f3807d6, 2026-09-03) removed the deprecated top-level aliases `xy gitlint`, `xy lintlint`, `xy node-lint` and `xy republint`. They were also dropped from RULE_COMMANDS aliases and stability.ts. Replacements: `xy git lint`, `xy lint lint`, `xy node lint`, `xy publint --fresh`. In 9.x they still ran, with a deprecation warning (v9.0.4 gitlintCommand.ts:42-45).

On 10.1.1 each removed name prints `Command not found [gitlint]` and exits 0, because the '*' fallback in xy.ts:121-129 sets no exit code. A CI step or agent check that used an alias now silently passes without linting anything.

9.2.0 (d37b662eb) removed `xy skills updo`: the custom skills subcommands went from {defaults, lint, updo} at v9.1.1 to {defaults, lint} at v9.2.0. It is replaced by `xy skills lint --fix`, which updates outdated skills only from 9.2.0. On 9.0.x/9.1.x, `--fix` only installs missing skills.

Neither removal is in toolchain CHANGELOG.md.

Real exposure: six XYO repos on 10.0.7-10.1.1 track `.claude/commands/xy-gitlint.md`, which runs `xy gitlint`: plugins, sdk-os-js, sdk-protocol-js, sdk-xyo-client-js, wallet-xl1-chrome, xl1-protocol. So does sdk-xyoworld-js (9.0.4), which will break when it upgrades. Several repos also track legacy xylabs-xy-cli skills listing `xy lintlint`/`xy gitlint`: plugins, sdk-protocol-js, sdk-xyo-react-js, sdk-react.

10.0.x patch releases also add error-level gates (not-public 10.0.3, package READMEs 10.0.5, importsMatchExports 10.0.9), and 10.1.1 adds agent lint to `xy check`. A version bump within 10.x can therefore turn a green `xy check`/`xy build` red.
