findings.title: Skill freshness ignores the repo's toolchain version: `xy check` requires the newest skill from main whatever toolchain is installed
findings.current:
- versions.ts:8-10 fetches `raw.githubusercontent.com/<source>/main/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- versions.ts:59-69 compares only the installed and latest `metadata.version`.
- lint.ts:93-96 installs with `skills add <source> --skill <name> -y`, with no ref.
- lint.ts:343-364: `skills.required-current` is error-level and fixable.
- skills-lock.json entries record only source, skillPath and computedHash.
- STABILITY.md:72: "Skill content is versioned on that repo's cadence, not npm lockstep."
findings.truth:
No part of `xy skills lint` (run by `xy check` since ≤v8.7.29) knows which toolchain version a skill describes, or which one the repo has installed.

Once xy-toolchain documents 10.1.x surfaces, every 9.x/10.0.x repo gets an error until it installs that skill. On ≥9.2.0, `--fix` installs it from main. There is no way to pin a skill compatible with the installed toolchain, and no warning that the skill is ahead of it.

On 9.0.x/9.1.x (16 consumers), `--fix` cannot update outdated skills (the fix arrived in d37b662eb, v9.2.0). The path there was `xy skills updo`, which 9.2.0 removed.

This is separate from the known findings about the backward comparison for xyo-skills 1.1.x copies and the version reset.
findings.evidence:
- packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/versions.ts:8-10 and 59-69.
- packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/lint.ts:93-96, 147-177 and 343-364.
- The same main-branch URL is used at v9.0.4 (`git show v9.0.4:…/versions.ts`). At v9.0.4 `skills.required-current` has defaultLevel 'error' and no fix branch (`git show v9.0.4:…/lint.ts` lines 235-244).
- v9.0.4 checkCommand.ts:69-70 runs skillsLint.
- XYOracleNetwork/xyo-cash/skills-lock.json has no version or ref field.
- Installed xy-toolchain skill survey: 0.1.5 present in repos on 9.2.0 and 10.0.5-10.1.1; 0.1.3 in six 9.0.x repos.
findings.recommendation:
Define a compatibility field in skill frontmatter, e.g. `metadata.toolchain: ">=9.0.1"` plus `metadata.verified-toolchain`.

Have versions.ts parse it from the upstream SKILL.md. When the repo's installed @ariestools/toolchain is below the minimum, emit an info or warn diagnostic ("latest xy-toolchain skill documents toolchain ≥X; upgrade the toolchain or rely on its since-notes") instead of only demanding the update.

Print the installed toolchain version in `xy skills lint` output.

Until then, the skill itself must carry the since-notes (see the SKILL.md finding).

findings.title: The browser-realm setup never says to download Chromium, so `xy test` fails on fresh machines and on every CI runner
findings.current: testing.md:27-33 says "Add `@vitest/browser-playwright` and `playwright` only when browser projects are enabled" and shows only `pnpm add -D @vitest/browser-playwright playwright`. testing.md:43-49 enables `browser: { provider: playwright() }`. testing.md:219 says "If the shared preset skips browser tests, verify `browser.provider` is set and Playwright is installed." Nothing covers browser binaries or CI.
findings.truth: Installing the npm packages does not download a browser. playwright@1.63.0, the version pinned in the repos, has no lifecycle scripts. pnpm also runs build scripts only for packages listed in allowBuilds. The Chromium binary has to be installed separately with `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`. Every repo whose vitest.config.ts enables the Playwright provider has that step between build and test. Repos without a browser realm do not.
findings.evidence: `jq '{version,scripts}' sdk-js/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.63.0/node_modules/playwright/package.json` returns `{"version":"1.63.0","scripts":null}`. sdk-js/pnpm-workspace.yaml:3-5 has `allowBuilds: esbuild, unrs-resolver`. Browser realm plus install step: sdk-js/vitest.config.ts:2,9 with sdk-js/.github/workflows/verify.yml:48-49 (`pnpm exec playwright install chromium`); actor-kit/vitest.config.ts:2,8 with actor-kit/.github/workflows/verify.yml:41-42; browser-kit/vitest.config.ts:2,8 with browser-kit/.github/workflows/verify.yml:41-42. No browser realm and no step: sdk-react/vitest.config.ts:3-4 ('Node project only') with sdk-react verify.yml:37-47; cli-kit (no playwright devDependency). sdk-js commit 3c03e7856 (2026-09-07) added the Chromium step when tests moved into CI. The previous build.yml said tests stayed local-only because 'browser tests are too expensive for hosted runners'.
findings.recommendation: After the install block at testing.md:29-33, add: "The npm packages do not download browsers. Run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` once on each machine, and in CI after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and before `pnpm xy test`. Add `--with-deps` on runners that lack Chromium's system libraries. Rerun it after bumping `playwright`, because browser binaries are matched to the Playwright version." Split testing.md:219 into two cases. (1) No browser tests run: the `browser` option was omitted or set to `false` in `defineXyVitestConfig`, because the preset creates the browser project only when `browser: { provider: playwright() }` is passed. (2) The browser project fails to launch: the Chromium binary is missing, so run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`. Link the proposed CI gates subsection in commands.md.

findings.title: Following 'use `--strict` when warnings must block CI' fails every fresh CI checkout, yet still lets agent-lint and skills-lint warnings through
findings.current: commands.md:165: "`xy check --fix` runs the fixable forms of the policy families included by `xy check`. Rerun without `--fix`, and use `--strict` when warnings must block CI."
findings.truth: (1) `xy check` runs git lint. git.autocrlf and git.eol warn unless core.autocrlf=false and core.eol=lf are set in git config. An unset key reads as undefined and produces a finding. A CI clone does not carry the repo-local .git/config, so unless the runner's global git config sets both keys, `xy check --strict` exits non-zero on every fresh checkout. (2) Inside `xy check`, agent lint and skills lint are called without a strict flag, and both force `strict: false`. Their warnings therefore never fail `xy check --strict` or `XY_STRICT=1 xy check`. Publint, packman lint, lint lint, git lint and repo lint do honor strict mode. The skills-lint half of the gap already existed in 10.1.0. The agent-lint half is new in 10.1.1.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/gitlint.ts:31-56 (`getGitConfigBool('core.autocrlf') === false`, `getGitConfig('core.eol') === 'lf'`); toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/gitConfig.ts:12-44 (returns undefined when unset); `xy.mjs git lint --rules` lists git.autocrlf, git.eol, git.ignorecase and git.ignore-toolchain-cache, all at warn. checkCommand.ts:50 `agentLint({ cwd, fix })` and :74 `skillsLint({ fix })`; actions/agent/lint.ts:24 `strict: options.strict === true`; actions/skills/lint.ts:472 `isStrict = options.isStrict === true || options.strict === true` and :521 `strict: isStrict`; ruleRunner.ts:183 and :253 (default `strict = isStrictMode()`); publint.ts:79, packman/lint.ts:394 and lintlint.ts:440 pass `isStrictMode()`. Baseline: `git show 7eb43c3c2:packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/lint.ts` line 470 has the same isStrict expression.
findings.recommendation: Replace commands.md:165 with text along these lines: "`xy check --fix` applies the fixable forms of the families `xy check` runs; use it locally only, never in CI. In CI, set the clone's git config with plain git before the gate (`git config core.autocrlf false && git config core.eol lf`, plus `git config core.ignorecase false` on case-insensitive filesystems), because git lint warns on unset values and a fresh clone carries none. Do not use `xy git lint --fix` for this, because it also rewrites .gitignore. Then run `pnpm xy check --strict`. In 10.1.1, `--strict` and `XY_STRICT=1` do not escalate agent-lint or skills-lint warnings inside `xy check`. When those must block, also run `pnpm xy agent lint --strict` and `pnpm xy skills lint --strict`." Revisit the last sentence once the toolchain bug in finding 5 is fixed.

(1) gitlint.ts:33 requires `getGitConfigBool('core.autocrlf') === false` and :48 requires `getGitConfig('core.eol') === 'lf'`. lib/gitConfig.ts returns undefined for unset keys, so a clone without those keys produces two warn diagnostics. runGitlint passes no `strict`, so ruleRunner.ts:253 defaults to isStrictMode(), and :183 then exits 1 on warnings under --strict or XY_STRICT=1. findings.title: No recommended CI gate set; line 42 only says 'run the gates required by the target repository or CI'
findings.current: commands.md:42: "Run the gates required by the target repository or CI rather than treating one aggregate command as universal." commands.md:21 documents `--jobs` with 'default is 16' and gives no CI advice. No skill file describes a workflow. toolchain.md:111-122 ('New project baseline') has no CI step.
findings.truth: Every ariestools repo's CI runs the same recipe: pnpm/action-setup@v6.1.0, then actions/setup-node with `cache: pnpm`, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm xy build --jobs 1`, then (browser realm only) `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`, then `pnpm xy test`. Jobs set `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, `permissions: contents: read`, a concurrency group and a 120-minute timeout. They run on a self-hosted trusted runner and trigger only on push to main and workflow_dispatch, never pull_request. No repo runs `xy check` or `--strict` in CI. The toolchain ROADMAP still expects `xy check` to pass on a fresh scaffold, and its 'north star' is 'Run only xy in CI'. Facts a CI author needs, none of them in the skills: (a) `xy build` is incremental by default, but a fresh checkout has no `.xy/cache/incremental` snapshot, so it does a full build. Do not cache `.xy/cache`, or pass `--no-incremental`. (b) `xy check` has to run after build, because publint's pub.platform and pub.publint rules (error level) compare export maps with compiled output. (c) `xy check` is not hermetic. skills.required-current (error) fetches each skill's SKILL.md from raw.githubusercontent.com on main, and `xy check` has no `--offline`. docs.stale depends on today's date. docs.evidence-immutable counts commits with `git rev-list`, so it needs `fetch-depth: 0` (on a shallow clone it passes trivially). repo.dependabot-enabled shells out to `gh api`. (d) On `--jobs`: the default is `os.availableParallelism()`, so it scales with the runner's core count. The lint pool runs that many child processes, and each inherits NODE_OPTIONS, so an 8 GiB heap per process oversubscribes memory on many-core runners. That is why every repo passes `--jobs 1`. `xy test` ignores `--jobs` (Vitest sizes its own pool), and no environment variable sets the job count. (e) pnpm/action-setup@v4 cannot bootstrap pnpm 12 on a runner without Node on PATH. v6.1.0 is the first release that can.

findings.title: `xy check --strict` and `XY_STRICT=1` do not apply to the agent-lint and skills-lint families
findings.current: checkCommand.ts:50 calls `agentLint({ cwd: process.cwd(), fix: isFix })` and :74 calls `skillsLint({ fix: isFix })`. agent/lint.ts:24 passes `strict: options.strict === true`. skills/lint.ts:472 sets `isStrict = options.isStrict === true || options.strict === true`.
findings.truth: runRuleChecks defaults to `strict = isStrictMode()` (ruleRunner.ts:253), but both wrappers pass an explicit false. Their warnings, such as agents.h1-not-filename, agents.size-budget, docs.stale, skills.duplicate-install and skills.unnecessary, never set a non-zero exit even though `--help` describes `--strict` as 'exit code = errorCount + warningCount'. Standalone `xy agent lint` also ignores `XY_STRICT=1`, because it reads only `argv.strict` (common/agent/index.ts:31-35). The skills half dates from before 10.1.0. The agent half is new in 10.1.1.
findings.evidence: ruleRunner.ts:180-183 and :253; publint.ts:79, packman/lint.ts:394 and lintlint.ts:440 use `isStrictMode()`; `xy.mjs check --help` (--strict 'Treat warnings as errors (exit code = errorCount + warningCount)'); xyParseOptions.ts:58 sets strict mode from --strict or XY_STRICT=1; `git show 7eb43c3c2:packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/lint.ts | grep 'isStrict ='` gives line 470.

That makes `xy check --strict`, `XY_STRICT=1 xy check`, `XY_STRICT=1 xy agent lint` and `XY_STRICT=1 xy skills lint` all escalate warnings, as `--help` promises. Add specs asserting that an agent-lint warning and a skills-lint warning fail `xy check` under --strict and under XY_STRICT=1.

findings.title: Scaffold Node 22: the hard-coded volta pin 22.14.0 is the bug. It warns in `xy check`, fails only under `--strict`, and the CI Node never follows it
findings.current: Root package.json.tmpl:53-56 has `"engineStrict": true, "volta": { "node": "22.14.0" }` and :40 has `"@types/node": "~26.1.2"`. The package template has `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }` (package/package.json.tmpl:55-57). The workflows hard-code `node-version: "22"` (build-pnpm.yml.tmpl:17-20, build-npm and build-yarn :15-18). The skill's toolchain.md:115 says 'Require Node.js 22 or newer'.
findings.truth: Static result for a monorepo scaffold. engines `>=22` contains latest Current 26.8.2 (and LTS 24.21.0), so repo.engines-lts reports no error. volta 22.14.0 is older than both, so repo.engines-lts reports it as a warning: volta lag goes to result.warnings, which map to level warn even though the rule is error-level. `xy check` therefore exits 0 and `xy check --strict` exits 1. That holds under `nodeTrack: 'lts'` too, because 22.14.0 < 24.21.0. node.volta-node-latest (warn) also fires but is not part of `xy check`. Its `--fix` rewrites volta to 26.8.2 while CI stays on 22, so CI never runs the pinned development runtime. @types/node 26 lets Node-26-only APIs type-check against a Node 22 floor. Testing on 22 is defensible as the engines floor: it matches the toolchain's REQUIRED_NODE_RANGE '>=22' and the toolchain's own CI. But as the only, hard-coded job it drifts. This sharpens the known nodeTrack finding: an LTS-or-older volta pin only warns, and `xy check` fails only when an engines range excludes the latest version.

findings.title: Single-package (`--no-monorepo`) scaffold drops `packageManager` and `volta`, but its workflow relies on `packageManager` for pnpm/action-setup
findings.current: mergePackageJsonRecords (scaffold.ts:127-150) returns `{ ...packagePkg, dependencies, devDependencies, private: false, scripts }`. Only devDependencies and scripts are taken from the root template.
findings.truth: The package template has no packageManager or volta (package/package.json.tmpl:1-62). The merged single-package package.json therefore loses the root template's `packageManager` (`{{packageManager}}`, root :52) and `volta` (:54-56). The generated build.yml is deliberately version-less: it uses `pnpm/action-setup@v4` with no `version:`, and the spec asserts `not.toContain('version: 11')`, relying on packageManager (toolchain commit 576b8592a 'ci: use packageManager for pnpm/action-setup'). Unless something such as Corepack auto-pin adds the field during install, the single-package workflow has no pnpm version source, and the repo has no Node pin at all. ROADMAP names exactly this `--no-monorepo` path in the Phase 2 exit criterion. The spec for this path checks the workflow text but not `packageManager`.
findings.evidence: scaffold.ts:127-150, :160-164 and :210-229; templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:52-56; templates/repo/cli/package/package.json.tmpl:1-62; templateVars.ts:7-11 and :117; build-pnpm.yml.tmpl:15; spec/actions/repoInit.spec.ts:224-240; docs/ROADMAP.md:132. findings.recommendation: Carry `packageManager`, `volta` and `engineStrict` over from the root template in mergePackageJsonRecords. Assert `pkg.packageManager` and `pkg.volta` in the single-package repoInit spec.

findings.title: Scaffold workflow lags the toolchain's own CI bar (action pins, permissions, pnpm 11, no check step)
findings.current: build-pnpm.yml.tmpl:1-29 uses `actions/checkout@v4`, `pnpm/action-setup@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: "22"`, and runs `pnpm xy build` and `pnpm xy test`. It has no `permissions`, `concurrency` or `timeout-minutes`. templateVars.ts:10 writes `packageManager: pnpm@11.13.1`.
findings.truth: ROADMAP 2.1 says the 'Scaffold CI matches this repo's public bar: … pinned action versions'. The toolchain and its sibling repos now pin pnpm/action-setup@v6.1.0, because v4 cannot bootstrap pnpm 12 without Node on PATH, which applies to their self-hosted runners. They also declare `permissions: contents: read`, a concurrency group and a timeout, and all of them use pnpm 12. The scaffold's pnpm 11 pin keeps v4 working on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest today. A scaffolded repo that moves to pnpm 12, as every ariestools repo has, then hits the sdk-js failure on any runner without Node on PATH. The toolchain's own GitHub-hosted build.yml still uses v4 with pnpm 12.10.1, so the failure is runner-specific.
findings.evidence: docs/ROADMAP.md:136; toolchain/.github/workflows/verify.yml:9-14,22,30-32; sdk-js commit cb8e3150d message; toolchain/.github/workflows/build.yml:16 (v4 on windows-latest and macos-latest); `jq .packageManager` shows pnpm@12.4.2 to 12.10.1 across the toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit.
findings.recommendation: Move packageManagerField('pnpm') (templateVars.ts:10) to the current pnpm 12 line. When it moves, use pnpm/action-setup at 6.1.0 or later in build-pnpm.yml.tmpl so the workflow also works on runners without Node on PATH, and update the repoInit spec's `pnpm/action-setup@v4` assertion to match. Optionally add `permissions: contents: read` and `node-version-file: package.json`; the latter needs finding 7 fixed so single-package scaffolds keep volta. Add `xy check` (after build, with the plain `git config` step) once the AGENTS.md template passes agent lint (finding 4). Do not describe the current template as violating ROADMAP 2.1.

findings.title: Toolchain rule gap: neither `xy skills lint` nor `xy check` detects or removes retired toolchain-generated agent files
findings.current: `xy skills lint --rules` lists only duplicate-install, migrated-source, package-recommended, required-current, required-installed and unnecessary. skills.unnecessary is 'Installed skills are required or optional for the detected repo profile' and is not fixable.
findings.truth: installed.ts:6 and :59-74 scan .claude/skills and .agents/skills, so xylabs-* directories are read into `installed`. They are then dropped: unnecessarySkillsForProfile filters `installed.filter(isXyoSkillName)` (skillRules.ts:202-205), and collectSkillNamesToCheck does the same (lint.ts:221-224). Skills outside the 10-name catalog (defaults.ts:13-27, 47-50) are therefore invisible by design. The rule exists so repo-local skills such as xyo-sdk-architecture and xl1-protocol-guide are not flagged, but it means the toolchain's own retired output is never reported. Every fixable rule only installs or reinstalls (lint.ts:296-390); skills.unnecessary has no fix (lint.ts:391-401). Nothing in the toolchain reads .claude/rules or .claude/commands: `git grep` for 'claude/rules|xylabs-' in toolchain src/docs returns no hits. The 10.1.1 additions do not cover it either: `xy agent lint` rules (actions/agent/rules.ts ids agents.*, docs.*, decisions.*, papers.*) and `xy skills pick` (pick.ts:34, 114-116) are catalog- or docs-only. findings.title: Merge known findings (a) and (b): default to the root barrel. Mixed or class-bearing subpath imports split runtime classes and static state; the type split is only a 9.0.1 artifact
findings.current: conventions.md:5 "Prefer named exports from `@ariestools/sdk/<module>` or the root barrel."; :6 "Prefer **subpath imports** for clarity and smaller mental graphs ... when only a few symbols are needed."; :17 "Prefer subpaths in libraries that care about minimal dependency graphs."; :56 "Prefer `@ariestools/sdk` + subpath for neutral helpers."; :58 "Install optional peers (`zod`, OTel) only when used."
findings.truth:
This answers questions (1) to (4). It is a different conclusion from the known findings (a), (b) and the 'subpaths keep peers optional' low item.

(1) Runtime. sdk-js builds @ariestools/sdk with the default `moduleLinkage: 'bundle'`, so every entry is a self-contained copy. In Node, root resolves to dist/node/index.mjs; bundlers with the browser condition get dist/browser/index.mjs. Each subpath resolves to its own dist/neutral/<m>.mjs. instanceof fails between root and any subpath. It also fails between two subpaths: the Base behind /creatable, the Base behind /events and /base.Base are three different classes.

Static state splits the same way. `initDefaultLogger` called from /base does not reach root classes or /creatable classes, and calling it from root does not reach /creatable classes. actor-kit Actors read root's `Base.defaultLogger`, so an app that follows the skill and calls `initDefaultLogger` from `@ariestools/sdk/base` leaves every Actor without the default logger.

(2) TypeScript, 9.0.1. Each platform has a full 256-file `modules/**` declaration tree. Under the house NodeNext resolution, root types come from dist/node, while subpath types come from dist/neutral. Twelve declaration files carry private/protected members (no `#` members), for example AbstractCreatable, PromiseEx, Base, BaseEmitter, Events, IdLogger and ApiClient. For these classes root and subpath types are not assignable (TS2322). Classes without such members, such as FetchClientError, stay structurally compatible. Subpaths share the one neutral declaration tree, so subpath-to-subpath types are assignable even though the runtime classes differ. Bundler resolution without customConditions picks `types` (the neutral tree), so it reports no type error.

(3) The published 9.0.1 has the same split. Toolchain 10.0.9 or later shares declarations on the next sdk-js build, which removes the type errors but not the runtime copies. Once the types are shared, tsc no longer reports the mismatch.

(4) Consumers import from the root barrel almost exclusively. sdk-js's own specialist packages use subpaths, but only for `import type` and stateless functions.

Peers: the root barrel loads zod (hex, object and zod modules) and @opentelemetry/api (through @ariestools/telemetry). Because actor-kit, sdk-react and the XYO libraries all import root, any app using them needs zod and OTel installed anyway. Subpath imports in the app's own code therefore save no peers and only add copies. Size: 11 common subpaths (assert, creatable, events, base, promise, delay, timer, forget, retry, fetch, logger) total 131,660 B, more than the 124,675 B root bundle.

Replace conventions.md:5-6 and :56 with:

"Import from the root `@ariestools/sdk` by default. Libraries that depend on it (actor-kit, sdk-react, XYO/XL1) import the root. In 9.x every entry is a separate bundle, so a class or module state reached through a subpath is a different object from the root's. Use subpaths only for `import type` and stateless functions (assertEx, exists, delay, typeof guards, toSafeJsonObject, fetchJson*). Never import classes or stateful setup through a subpath: creatable/AbstractCreatable, Base/initDefaultLogger, BaseEmitter/Events, PromiseEx, TimerScheduler, ApiClient, logger classes. Never combine two class-bearing subpaths. Across packages, use the `is*` brand guards (isFetchError), not instanceof. Use one import style per package across the whole dependency graph."

Rewrite Tree-shaking (:15-17): the root is `sideEffects: false` and tree-shakes in bundlers, and subpath bundles duplicate shared code.

Change checklist item 3 (:58) to "Root import requires zod ^4.6 and @opentelemetry/api ^1.9 (installed by the app). Subpaths keep them optional only if nothing in the graph imports the root."

findings.title: storage-adapters: the root barrel and /mongo carry separate MongoClientWrapper pool caches; every consumer uses /mongo
findings.current: packages.md:36-41 table lists `@ariestools/storage-adapters` ("Root barrel"), `/indexed-db` and `/mongo` as interchangeable, with no import-style rule.
findings.truth: storage-adapters is also a bundle-linkage monolith. MongoClientWrapper is defined in 4 entries: browser/index, neutral/index, neutral/mongo and node/index. Its `static readonly clients` Map, documented as a "Global cache" of pooled MongoClients, therefore exists once per entry. An app that imports MongoClientWrapper from the root while a library uses /mongo gets two wrappers, and so two connection pools, for the same URI, with separate reference counts. All 50 consumer imports in the workspace use `@ariestools/storage-adapters/mongo`. The root barrel also requires both the idb and mongodb peers (known finding). For this package the consistent style is therefore the backend subpath, the opposite of @ariestools/sdk.

findings.title: Known finding (c) is overstated: correct its severity from medium to low and narrow it to two sentences
findings.current: compilation.md:99 already says "Use `moduleLinkage: 'external'` when subpaths must preserve shared runtime identity across `instanceof`, contexts, registries, or singletons; the default bundled linkage duplicates shared code across entries." There is no mention of 10.0.9 declaration sharing or of external-linkage requirements.
findings.truth:
The only decision that matters, choosing a linkage, is already documented and accurate. The 10.0.9 declaration sharing runs automatically for both linkages and needs no configuration. The identity invariant applies only to external linkage. It is enforced by the error-level `pub.importsMatchExports` rule and by layout-sync warnings, and a missing `conditionalImports.<m>.distImports` is a thrown error. An agent following the current text does not get a wrong result.

Two useful additions remain:
(i) From 10.0.9 on, tsc no longer flags root-vs-subpath class mismatches in bundle-linkage packages, while the runtime copies remain. Rebuilding sdk-js with 10.0.9 or later therefore hides the problem from type checking.
(ii) External linkage requires `distImports` for every conditional import. A real platform variant must be declared on both sides, `conditionalImports` and `platformEntries`.

The rest belongs to the known 'Monolith section omits MonolithConfig surface' and 'Troubleshooting omits publint rules' findings.
findings.evidence:
Toolchain packageCompileMonolith.ts:119-123: dedupe runs without a linkage check. monolithDedupeDeclarations.ts:7-28. monolithLayoutLint.ts:91: lint is external-only. monolithCompileLayout.ts:131: throws without distImports. papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md:284-288; CHANGELOG.md:20-21,27.

Version history: 6e056462a first ships in v10.0.9 (published 2026-10-05). moduleLinkage has existed since 78175963c (2026-07-06, first tag v8.6.7).

Simulation: running dedupeMonolithDeclarations from the toolchain source on a scratchpad copy of the sdk 9.0.1 dist removed 482 platform copies, and dist/node/index.d.ts then re-exports '../neutral/modules/...'. The same tsc test then reports no errors under NodeNext or Bundler+browser, while runtime `root.PromiseEx === /promise.PromiseEx` stays false.
findings.recommendation: Lower (c) to low. In the Monolith section add: "Since 10.0.9, platform declaration trees reuse the modules-platform declarations, so each class has one declaration. Under bundle linkage this hides the runtime duplication from tsc: choose `external` for any package that exports classes, contexts or module state across subpaths. External linkage requires `conditionalImports.<m>.distImports`, and a real platform variant must be declared in both `conditionalImports` and `platformEntries`; `pub.importsMatchExports` fails a mismatch." Merge the remaining surface into the existing MonolithConfig and publint findings.

findings.title: Resolve the known Layer 1 vs ariestools-sdk import contradiction in Layer 1's favor: keep the root-barrel rule and add 'do not mix styles'
findings.current: typescript.md:64-78 "Import from the root barrel package of each monorepo ... Tree shaking eliminates what you don't use", with an XYO example and a pointer to XYO skills.
findings.truth: Two known findings say this section contradicts ariestools-sdk's subpath guidance, which implies Layer 1 should yield. The evidence points the other way. For @ariestools/sdk 9.x the root barrel is the import that keeps one class copy per platform. Every downstream library uses it (actor-kit 18/0, sdk-react 115/0, xl1-protocol 2083/0, xyo-chain 3529/0). The toolchain's own `xy lint init` also steers toward umbrella barrels (lint-init.ts:56-67). What Layer 1 lacks is the generic reason: monolith packages ship each subpath as a separate bundle, so mixing a package's root and subpath imports duplicates classes and module state. The right form of the rule is 'one style per package across the graph', which for storage-adapters means its /mongo subpath.
findings.evidence: skills/xy-development/typescript.md:64-78. Toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:56-67 ("SDK barrels whose individual sub-package imports we steer toward the barrel"). Consumer counts and runtime evidence are in the conventions.md and packages.md findings.
findings.recommendation: Keep the root-barrel rule and the existing sub-package example. Add one generic sentence: 'Some packages publish subpaths as separate bundles. Do not mix a package's root and subpath imports in one dependency graph. Follow the style the package's other consumers use, and check that package's skill for exceptions (for example, ariestools-sdk conventions).' If an @ariestools example is wanted, add it as a second root-vs-subpath example rather than replacing the XYO sub-package one.

findings.title: sdk-js publishes about 50 subpaths under bundle linkage and its README advertises them, though 'external' linkage has existed since toolchain 8.6.7
findings.current: packages/sdk/xy.config.ts:8-153 has no `moduleLinkage`, so the default 'bundle' applies. packages/sdk/README.md:11-18 says to import "a single slice via a subpath export (tree-shaking-friendly — you only pay for what you import)". Base.ts:109-110 documents `Base.defaultLogger` as the "process-wide default logger".
findings.truth:
The skill's subpath advice was copied from upstream, and upstream ships a layout in which that advice splits identity and module state. The toolchain fix, `moduleLinkage: 'external'`, has been available since July (78175963c, first tag v8.6.7): each module gets one canonical bundle per platform, so root and subpaths share classes and subpaths keep peers optional. 10.0.9 adds its safety net: pub.importsMatchExports and layout-sync warnings for the platform/url `platformEntries` that sdk-js uses.

sdk-js is pinned at toolchain ~10.0.7 (lock 10.0.7). The next update within that range, to 10.0.9 or later, fixes only the declaration side. storage-adapters is in the same situation.

The SDK already hardens two classes against copies: isFetchError's brand and AbstractCreatable's `Symbol.for` construction key. Other state is not hardened: Base statics and MongoClientWrapper.clients.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/xy.config.ts:8-153; sdk-js/package.json:42 "@ariestools/toolchain": "~10.0.7"; pnpm-lock.yaml:724. Toolchain MonolithConfig.ts:153-166; `git log -S moduleLinkage` gives 78175963c 2026-07-06; `git tag --contains` gives v8.6.7 first. FetchError.ts:196-203; AbstractCreatable.ts:25. Runtime results are in the conventions.md finding.
findings.recommendation: In sdk-js, either set `moduleLinkage: 'external'` with `distImports` for the platform/url conditional imports, then verify with `xy publint` and layout sync on toolchain 10.0.9 or later, or stop advertising subpaths for class- and state-bearing modules in README.md:11-18. Make the same decision for storage-adapters. Once sdk-js ships external linkage, the ariestools-sdk skill can relax the root-only guidance and recommend subpaths again for peer-light consumers, with a version gate.

findings.title: sdk-react-foundation's root barrel has its own UserEventsContext, separate from /user-events, which every sdk-react package and app uses. The planned sdk-react skill must not copy the sdk 'use root' rule
findings.current: No skill covers sdk-react. The known finding proposes a new ariestools-sdk-react skill, and its import guidance is unspecified.
findings.truth:
sdk-react-foundation is a bundle-linkage monolith (no moduleLinkage). `UserEventsContext`, `DebugUserEventsContext`, `UserEventsProvider` and `useUserEvents` are exported from the root bundle (dist/browser/index.mjs:991-1040) and again from user-events.mjs:3-4, as two distinct React contexts. sdk-react-app, analytics and ui consume `@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation/user-events`, and the umbrella @ariestools/sdk-react re-exports the sub-package subpaths. A provider imported from the foundation root therefore never reaches their `useUserEvents`, and events are silently dropped.

Current consumers avoid this: 10 imports use '/user-events' and 5 use '@ariestools/sdk-react/pixel'. It is still a latent trap. For sdk-react the consistent style is the umbrella or the sub-package subpaths, the reverse of @ariestools/sdk. A blanket 'use the root barrel' rule would be wrong here.
findings.evidence:
sdk-react/packages/sdk-react-foundation/xy.config.ts (mode monolith, modulesPlatform browser, no moduleLinkage). src/modules/user-events/Context.ts:77,88. `grep -n createContext( dist/browser/*.mjs` shows index.mjs and user-events.mjs. sdk-react/packages/sdk/dist/browser/*.mjs: `export * from '@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation/<subpath>'`.

Runtime check: `node --conditions=browser` in sdk-react-foundation printed "root.UserEventsContext === /user-events.UserEventsContext: false".

Workspace grep: 10 imports from '@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation/user-events' and 5 from '@ariestools/sdk-react/pixel'; none use the foundation root.
findings.recommendation: In the planned ariestools-sdk-react skill, say: 'Import from @ariestools/sdk-react (root or its subpaths; both forward to the same sub-package subpath bundles). Never import from a sub-package root barrel such as @ariestools/sdk-react-foundation, whose root bundle carries its own UserEventsContext, separate from /user-events.' In sdk-react, set moduleLinkage: 'external' for sdk-react-foundation or drop context-bearing modules (user-events) from its root barrel. Write the general rule as 'one style per package, matching the package's other consumers', and keep Layer 1's umbrella-root rule, which already holds for @ariestools/sdk-react.

verify.code: confirmed: sdk-react-foundation/xy.config.ts is a monolith with modulesPlatform 'browser' and no moduleLinkage. dist/browser/index.mjs:991-992 defines its own UserEventsContext/DebugUserEventsContext, and user-events.mjs:3-4 defines separate ones. With `node --conditions=browser`, root.UserEventsContext === /user-events.UserEventsContext gives false. sdk-react-analytics/dist/browser/pixel.mjs:1362 imports from '@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation/user-events'. The umbrella sdk-react pixel.mjs re-exports '@ariestools/sdk-react-analytics/pixel', and its other modules re-export foundation subpaths. Workspace imports use '/user-events' or '@ariestools/sdk-react/pixel', never the foundation root, so the trap is latent. Side note: PromiseSettingsContext is also duplicated across 4 foundation entries. That copy is not observable today, because PromiseSettingsProvider is not exported.
verify.skill: adjusted: The duplication is real. sdk-react-foundation/xy.config.ts is monolith with modulesPlatform browser and no moduleLinkage. dist/browser/index.mjs:990-1004 creates its own UserEventsContext and DebugUserEventsContext, separate from user-events.mjs:3-4. The finding overstates the scope, though. The umbrella @ariestools/sdk-react is safe: its root re-exports sub-package subpaths (sdk/dist/browser/index.mjs: `export * from '@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation/flexbox'` and others), and its own subpaths are pure forwarders (sdk/dist/browser/flexbox.mjs:1), so umbrella root and umbrella subpaths share identity. UserEventsProvider and useUserEvents reach the umbrella through '@ariestools/sdk-react-analytics/pixel', which imports '@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation/user-events' (pixel.mjs:1356-1362,1395-1410). So Layer 1's 'root barrel of the monorepo' rule is correct for sdk-react, and 'the reverse of @ariestools/sdk' is wrong. Only a sub-package root barrel (@ariestools/sdk-react-foundation) is the trap. Nothing imports the foundation root: the sdk-react src imports of foundation all use subpaths, with 9 from /user-events, and no skill points agents at it. That makes this a latent issue, which is low rather than medium.

findings.title: sdk-react has not declared @ariestools/sdk since 11.1.6 but imports its root barrel at runtime, so apps silently need @ariestools/sdk, zod and OTel
findings.current: sdk-react/xy.config.ts:14 `'@ariestools/sdk': { placement: 'dev', presence: 'allowed' }`. Every sdk-react package lists @ariestools/sdk only in devDependencies.
findings.truth:
The published sdk-react-foundation 12.0.1 dist contains runtime `import ... from "@ariestools/sdk"` (for example `delay`, `Enum`, `getApiStage`), but its dependencies are only async-mutex and its peers only react, react-dom and @mui/material. The peer `@ariestools/sdk: ^8.1` existed in 11.1.5 and was dropped in 11.1.6, when the 2026-07-24 'deplint' commit replaced `refType: 'peer'` with `placement: 'dev'`.

Because the root barrel loads zod and @opentelemetry/api, a sdk-react app has to install @ariestools/sdk ~9, zod and @opentelemetry/api itself. Nothing in the dependency chain tells it to. The import only resolves through hoisting, and without a peer no package manager enforces a single @ariestools/sdk version shared with the app. That single shared copy is exactly what the root-import identity rule relies on.
findings.evidence: `npm view @ariestools/sdk-react-foundation@<v> peerDependencies dependencies`: 11.1.5 includes "@ariestools/sdk":"^8.1"; 11.1.6, 12.0.0 and 12.0.1 omit it. `git log -L` on sdk-react/xy.config.ts shows b753abb17 (2026-07-24, 'deplint') replacing `'@ariestools/sdk': { refType: 'peer' }`. sdk-react-foundation/dist/browser/index.mjs, flexbox.mjs, rich-result.mjs and shared.mjs contain `from "@ariestools/sdk"` (dist built 2026-10-05 16:45; 12.0.1 published 2026-10-05T23:53Z). sdk-react/xy.config.ts:5-8 apiExposure `peerForwarding: 'when-used'` notes that zod and OTel are left to the upstream declarer, which nothing declares.
findings.recommendation: In sdk-react, restore `@ariestools/sdk` as a peer (~9.0) of every package that imports it, and let deplint enforce it. In the planned sdk-react skill and in the ariestools-sdk install guidance, say until then: "Apps using @ariestools/sdk-react 12.x must add @ariestools/sdk ~9, zod ^4.6 and @opentelemetry/api ^1.9 themselves."

verify.code: confirmed: sdk-react/xy.config.ts:14 sets `'@ariestools/sdk': { placement: 'dev', presence: 'allowed' }`, and :5-9 sets apiExposure peerForwarding 'when-used'. Every sdk-react package that lists @ariestools/sdk has it only in devDependencies (~9.0.1). npm view of @ariestools/sdk-react-foundation: 11.1.5 has peer "@ariestools/sdk": "^8.1"; 11.1.6, 12.0.0 and 12.0.1 drop it, with dependencies only async-mutex. `git log -L14,14:xy.config.ts` shows b753abb17 (2026-07-24, 'deplint') as the change. The installed published 12.0.1 tarball (crypto-cards node_modules) has runtime `import { getApiStage | delay | Enum } from "@ariestools/sdk"` in index, flexbox, rich-result and shared.mjs. Locally, sdk-react-app (7 files) and sdk-react-ui (8) also import the sdk root at runtime, and analytics (3) does too. The sdk root bundle statically loads zod and @ariestools/telemetry, which loads @opentelemetry/api, so apps must supply all three without being told.
verify.skill: confirmed: sdk-react/xy.config.ts:14 has `'@ariestools/sdk': { placement: 'dev', presence: 'allowed' }`. All 9 sdk-react packages list @ariestools/sdk only in devDependencies. `npm view` shows sdk-react-foundation 11.1.5 with peer '@ariestools/sdk': '^8.1', while 11.1.6 and 12.0.1 have peers react, react-dom and @mui/material only, and dependencies async-mutex only. `git show b753abb17` (2026-07-24, 'deplint') replaces `refType: 'peer'` with placement 'dev'. Published runtime imports exist: dist/browser/index.mjs:336, 615 and 934 import getApiStage, delay and Enum from '@ariestools/sdk', and the same happens in flexbox.mjs, shared.mjs and rich-result.mjs. The root sdk import loads zod/mini and telemetry (see [0]), and xy.config.ts:5-9 leaves those to an upstream declarer that does not exist. None of the 10.1.1 toolchain commits change deplint placement semantics. Medium fits: this is a packaging defect outside the skills, and it currently only works through hoisting.

findings.title: compile.mode 'tsc' now fails the compile; say so instead of 'not wired'
findings.current: "`mode: 'tsc'` is reserved in the public type but is not wired into `packageCompile`. Do not recommend it as an operational mode." (compilation.md:78)
findings.truth: Since 9.2.0, `compile.mode: 'tsc'` makes package-compile print an error and return exit code 1. It no longer falls back to esbuild. It is listed as experimental config surface `compile.mode.tsc` in `xy --stability`.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/compile.ts:21-27; CHANGELOG.md:60 ('compile.mode: 'tsc' now errors instead of silently using the esbuild path'); src/xy/stability.ts:142-146; architecture.md:40.
findings.recommendation: Reword: "`mode: 'tsc'` is reserved (experimental surface `compile.mode.tsc`); `xy compile` rejects it with exit code 1. Use library/bundle/transpile/monolith/vendor." Optionally tell readers to run `pnpm xy --stability` for the current experimental compile surfaces.

verify.code: confirmed: package/compile/compile.ts:21-27 prints an error ('compile.mode "tsc" is experimental and not wired into xy compile...') and returns 1. CHANGELOG.md:60, under [9.2.0] (published 2026-09-01 per npm view), says it 'now errors instead of silently using the esbuild path'. architecture.md says it is 'rejected (not silently esbuild)'. stability.ts lists the surface compile.mode.tsc. The skill's 'not wired' is not false, but it omits that the compile hard-fails with exit code 1. Low severity is appropriate. 10.1.1 does not change this.
verify.skill: refuted: The skill's statement is still correct and its guidance does not change. compilation.md:78 says mode 'tsc' 'is not wired into packageCompile. Do not recommend it as an operational mode.' The toolchain describes it the same way. packageCompile's own error text is 'compile.mode "tsc" is experimental and not wired into xy compile' (actions/package/compile/compile.ts:21-27), and the stability catalog says 'Reserved `compile.mode: 'tsc'`. Not wired into packageCompile.' (stability.ts, compile.mode.tsc, unchanged at 10.1.1). Since 59e39e529 (2026-09-01) it fails loudly with exit 1 instead of silently falling back, but that only enforces the advice the skill already gives. An agent following the skill never uses it, so the proposed rewording is optional polish, not a correction.

findings.title: 'Typically compiled to dist/neutral/' understates the umbrella's per-platform builds
findings.current: overview.md:12 "All packages are **ESM only** (`.mjs` + `.d.ts`), typically compiled to `dist/neutral/`."
findings.truth: ESM-only is correct. However, the umbrella's root `.`, `./platform` and `./url` exports have separate `node`, `browser` and neutral builds (`dist/node`, `dist/browser`, `dist/neutral`), and the root `default` condition resolves to the browser build. The other subpaths are neutral-only.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json:128-142 (root: node → dist/node/index.mjs, browser → dist/browser/index.mjs, default → dist/browser/index.mjs), :271-284 (./platform), :349-362 (./url).
findings.recommendation: Reword to: "ESM only (`.mjs` + `.d.ts`). Most entry points are neutral (`dist/neutral/`); the umbrella root, `/platform` and `/url` resolve per-platform builds through `node`/`browser` export conditions. Do not deep-import `dist/*`."

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim is correct. In sdk/package.json:128-142 the root export has node → dist/node, browser → dist/browser, and a bare default → dist/browser/index.mjs; ./platform (:271-284) and ./url (:349-362) carry node/browser/default(neutral) conditions. Those are the only sdk exports with platform conditions. The recommended rewording ('Most entry points are neutral; the umbrella root, /platform and /url resolve per-platform builds') is incomplete for the specialist packages, which line 12 also covers ('All packages'). @ariestools/express exports only a `node` condition, so it does not resolve under browser or neutral conditions. @ariestools/pixel ships only dist/browser. @ariestools/threads uses node/browser conditions with no neutral fallback on ., /implementation, /master, /pool and /worker, and /register is node-only. @ariestools/crypto has node/browser builds. A grep of each package.json for dist/ targets confirms this.
verify.skill: refuted: overview.md:12 says 'typically compiled to `dist/neutral/`'. That is a hedged, still-correct simplification: every subpath except root, /platform and /url is neutral-only. The platform-conditional nuance is already documented at modules.md:98-100: 'platform and url use conditional package exports (node / browser / default neutral)… Do not import deep dist/node/... paths by hand'. conventions.md:8 already forbids `@ariestools/sdk/dist/...` imports. The root barrel's separate builds also make no practical difference. `cmp` shows dist/node/index.mjs, dist/browser/index.mjs and dist/neutral/index.mjs are byte-identical (124675 bytes each, built 2026-09-24). Telling agents the root 'resolves per-platform builds' would add a nuance with no behavioral effect. No change is needed.

findings.title: Nested packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md is recommended, but the toolchain's documented repo contract forbids it
findings.current: structure.md:24 "packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md   delta only, where a package genuinely differs"
findings.truth: The toolchain repo-docs contract says: "Keep agent instructions at the repository root. Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages." No lint rule enforces this. Some repos still have nested files: xl1-protocol/packages/{protocol,sdk}/AGENTS.md and ariestools/ariestools/packages/{dashboard,datalake-saas}/AGENTS.md.
findings.evidence: toolchain docs/repo-docs.md:16 (added in eb11282ab, 2026-09-08, "feat: lint monorepo markdown contract for agents and packages"; included in v10.1.0); `find` across the workspace for packages/*/AGENTS.md returned the four files listed above.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two conventions. findings.title: Rule that every document carries front matter, and its state vocabulary, conflict with the toolchain's single-owner metadata model
findings.current: lifecycle.md:3 "Every document under docs/, papers/, and specs/ carries YAML front matter." lifecycle.md:7-35 lists `state: draft|active|normative|superseded|retired`.
findings.truth: The plan manifest requires exactly one owner for lifecycle metadata: `metadata.source: manifest` (the documented norm for existing repos, "Use inline manifest metadata until front matter is adopted; never maintain both") or `front-matter`. The manifest separates `lifecycle` (accepted|active|archived|deprecated|draft|proposed|superseded) from `authorityLevel` (descriptive|evidentiary|informative|normative). xy-agent's `state` mixes the two by treating `normative` as a state. No toolchain doc or paper carries YAML front matter. The papers use a visible header, and plan-lint paper templates use a `## Status` section.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34. plan-manifest.v1.schema.json $defs.documentMetadata (oneOf manifest | front-matter; lifecycle and authorityLevel enums; description "never maintain both"). `head -1` of toolchain/docs/*.md and papers/*.md shows a Markdown H1 with no `---`. toolchain/papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md:3-5 header block. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/templates.ts:100-147.
findings.recommendation: Make front matter conditional: use it only where the repository has chosen front matter as the metadata owner (manifest `metadata.source: front-matter`), and never duplicate lifecycle, review date or supersession in both places. Align the vocabulary with the shipped schema. Either rename `state` to `lifecycle` with the schema's values and add `authorityLevel` (normative/informative/descriptive/evidentiary), or document an explicit mapping (normative → lifecycle accepted + authorityLevel normative; retired → archived/deprecated).
